prisma-calibration/technical-reference/e.filePath: Prisma Calibration/Technical Reference/Extraction artifact sinks and blank registration.md
prisma-calibration/technical-reference/e.title: Extraction artifact sinks and blank registration
prisma-calibration/technical-reference/e.content:
Extraction produces derived JPEGs through a small sink protocol, while blank registration establishes the flatfield evidence used by extraction. These are related filesystem concerns but different ownership layers: live thumbnails are replaceable derived output; a registered blank is durable metadata that points at an onboarded image asset.
Related: The extraction pipeline · Processing and extraction · Assigning images · Data access and persistence · calibration.processing.artifact_sinks · calibration.processing.blank_registry
Artifact sink contract
ExtractionArtifactSink in processing/artifact_sinks.py exposes two operations:

wants_image(kind) -> bool lets a destination decline artifacts it does not own.
write_image(sample_id, kind, image_bgr, max_dim=800) -> Path writes one requested image.

The allowed kinds are source, blank, strip, appearance, and transmission_roi. Sample IDs are restricted to alphanumeric characters plus _, ., and -, and kinds come from an allow-list, so neither value can inject arbitrary path components. sink_wants_image preserves compatibility with older test or extension sinks that implement only write_image, treating them as interested in every kind.
stage_jpeg_image rejects empty arrays, optionally downsizes the longest dimension with OpenCV INTER_AREA, and encodes a quality-80 JPEG to a unique same-directory temporary file. It verifies that cv2.imwrite returned success and that the staged file exists and is non-empty. write_thumbnail_image then promotes that checked file with publish_staged_files; it does not write directly over a live target.
publish_staged_files requires every staged file to be a non-empty sibling of a distinct target. It copies any existing target to a rollback sibling, replaces the targets with os.replace, and restores already-replaced targets if a later replacement fails. A rollback copy is deliberately preserved if restoring it also fails. This makes an ordinary multi-file publication rollback-capable, but it is not by itself a database transaction or a process-kill journal.
The three built-in destinations
Live accepted-sample thumbnails
LiveThumbnailSink owns only source and strip. It writes:
{data_root}/thumbnails/{sample_id}/source.jpg
{data_root}/thumbnails/{sample_id}/strip.jpg
It rejects blank, appearance, and transmission_roi as review-only artifacts. Those three images are useful while judging an extraction candidate, but they are not part of the durable accepted-sample thumbnail contract.
Hidden live-publication staging
StagedLiveThumbnailSink also accepts only source and strip, but writes them into a hidden per-operation directory under:
{data_root}/_system/extraction_visual_stages/stage_<uuid>/
Normal committed automatic and manual extraction on the SQLite backend create this sink internally. A caller cannot substitute a custom sink for a committed SQLite extraction. The staged pair is validated before it participates in the extraction-publication transaction described below.
Candidate and review directories
SampleArtifactDirectorySink writes all five artifact kinds into a caller-owned fixed directory. The filenames are:





























KindFilenamesourcesource.jpgstripstrip.jpgblankblank_review.jpgappearanceappearance_review.jpgtransmission_roitransmission_review.jpg
Maintenance re-extraction uses it for a candidate directory. Ordinary manual preview uses it under maintenance/manual_extraction_reviews/{sample_id}. Manual review directories are transient: closing the ordinary manual workflow requests their deletion, a committed or failed manual attempt removes them, and startup removes abandoned manual-review directories.
Committing SQLite semantics and live visuals together
The SQLite production path coordinates the extraction result, sample workflow state, and the two live JPEGs through processing/extraction_publication.py rather than asking a sink to approximate a database transaction.

create_visual_stage gives the processor a hidden StagedLiveThumbnailSink.
The processor writes and verifies source.jpg and strip.jpg there.
prepare_publication creates a durable pub_<uuid> directory under {data_root}/_system/extraction_publications/, copies and fsyncs both visual payloads, and atomically writes journal.json before the semantic commit.
The semantic callback atomically saves the replacement extraction result and sample state in SQLite.
Only if the replacement extraction-result ID is current does the coordinator publish both live visuals. Existing live files are backed up and restored on an ordinary replacement failure.
Completed automatic/manual records are marked complete and removed. Re-extraction records may require separate candidate finalization before their journal is removed.

This is recover-forward publication, not a claim that SQLite and the filesystem share one atomic primitive. If the process stops before the SQLite replacement is current, startup discards the uncommitted/superseded publication. If SQLite committed but visual promotion did not finish, startup republishes the journaled pair. Ambiguous or invalid journals are preserved and reported rather than guessed through. Thumbnail resolution can serve the current committed journal payload while recovery is pending, preventing a stale live path from being treated as authoritative.
Startup also deletes rigorously named abandoned visual-stage directories and interrupted live .publication/.rollback siblings when it can identify them safely. Unknown, unsafe, invalid, or ambiguous paths are preserved for diagnosis.
Invalidation and cleanup
source.jpg and strip.jpg are derived views of the current extraction result. Sample invalidation deletes the durable extraction result transactionally, then the surrounding workflow requests best-effort live-visual cleanup; a filesystem cleanup error does not roll the database invalidation back. Rejecting a pending-review result uses that invalidation path. Review-only images belong to their candidate/review workspace and are discarded rather than promoted into the live thumbnail tree.
The artifact sink itself never creates, accepts, rejects, or deletes an extraction result. Its responsibility ends at validated image output. SQLite transactions, publication journals, invalidation helpers, and the caller’s review lifecycle own the durable state changes.
Blank registration: SQLite production path
POST /api/blanks/register dispatches to SQLiteDataStore.register_blank_from_image on the production SQLite backend. The method resolves an onboarded image_assets row, rejects an already registered asset, allocates the next blank ID, and inserts a registered_blanks row in a write transaction. The returned Blank.storage_path is the image asset’s managed relative path. Registration does not copy a second file into blanks/.
list_blank_assets exposes the joined blank/image information current consumers need, and get_blank_storage_path resolves a blank ID back to the managed image. A blank cannot be unregistered while a sample assignment references it.
Image rotation is less comprehensive than blank registration. set_image_rotation blocks and invalidates sample assignments only where the rotated asset is the sample’s strip image. It does not currently inspect samples that use the same asset through blank_id. Rotating a registered blank after extraction can therefore leave those samples’ existing results bound to the earlier blank orientation. Until that runtime gap is fixed, set blank rotation before processing and explicitly reprocess every affected sample after a change.
CSV pending-blank registration
The CSV assignment importer can register an unregistered blank as part of an explicitly confirmed commit. For that path, save_samples_with_blank_registrations clones the proposed samples, registers every needed managed image as a blank, substitutes the allocated blank IDs, and saves all sample assignments inside one SQLite write transaction. If any sample save fails, both the new blank registration and all assignments roll back. Existing registered-blank CSV commits likewise save their sample set in one transaction. See CSV assignment import and commit lifecycle for preview custody and stale-state validation.
JSON compatibility path
The JSON DataStore route calls processing.blank_registry.register_blank_image. It resolves the source through get_image_path, rejects duplicate original filenames, best-effort reads EXIF DateTimeOriginal, copies the source into root/blanks/{blank_id}{suffix}, and registers a legacy Blank pointing at that copy. If registration fails, it deletes the copied file. This remains a compatibility and migration path, not the distributable SQLite custody model.
Anchors

prisma-calibration/technical-reference/f.title: Frontend architecture
prisma-calibration/technical-reference/f.content:
Calibration’s browser UI is a zero-build, native-ES-module application under Prisma/calibration/app/. It remains a light-only interface; the Generator theme preference and dark-mode tokens are not shared with Calibration.
index.html is the declarative shell and loads a single module entrypoint, bootstrap.js. Bootstrap creates an injectable API client, creates the application context, installs core services and feature commands, initializes owned state, and starts the app. It does not publish application state or compatibility functions on window.
Module boundaries

api/ owns the fetch client and endpoint groups for records, profiles, images, backup/restore, maintenance, geometries, modeling, and initial loading. api/index.js composes them through createCalibrationApi.
core/ owns shared state, DOM lookup, dialogs, rendering helpers, polling, formatting, UI primitives, and lifecycle disposal. core/application-context.js defines the state slices and command registry shared by installed features.
features/ owns UI behavior by workflow: shell/navigation, logbook, images, processing, filaments, geometries, modeling, and operations. Each installer adds its commands to the application context; event handlers and asynchronous work stay with the feature that owns them.
styles/ contains ordered component and feature styles. style.css is an import-only manifest whose order preserves the established cascade. styles/tokens.css defines the current light UI palette.

Backend calls should go through the relevant api/ module rather than calling fetch from a feature. Cross-feature interaction goes through explicit app.commands and state slices rather than globals. Pollers and listeners that need teardown use app.lifecycle.
For the operational server and job model, see Driving the calibration app and Web API and job orchestration. The Python Architecture/ pages describe backend modules only; this page is the maintained map for the browser code.

prisma-calibration/technical-reference/g.filePath: Prisma Calibration/Technical Reference/Geometry and strip definition.md
prisma-calibration/technical-reference/g.title: Geometry and strip definition
prisma-calibration/technical-reference/g.content:
In one sentence: a calibration strip’s shape is a frozen GeometryDefinition (calibration.geometry_builder), validated to a strict canonical form, hashed into a structural_fingerprint, and turned into a build-independent body plan that the STEP/STL exporters render — the notebook-era strips/generator.py is off the production SQLite path.

This page is the code-level map of how a strip geometry is represented and exported. For the concept — what a swatch, a role, and the spine are, and why the strip is shaped the way it is — see Sample Geometry. How a sample points at its geometry, and where geometries are persisted, is in Data access and persistence.
Related: calibration.geometry_builder · calibration.lightweight_step · calibration.strips.generator · calibration.strips.step_parser · Sample Geometry
The source-of-truth definition
Everything hangs off three frozen dataclasses in geometry_builder.py, deliberately independent of a CAD kernel:

GeometryDefinition — the whole strip: layout_rows × layout_columns, per-swatch and spine dimensions in millimeters, a tuple of roles, and a tuple of swatch_slots. swatch_count is just rows * columns.
GeometryRoleDefinition — one bottom-to-top material slot, tagged role_kind "fixed" or "variable", with a role_index and (for fixed roles) a fixed_thickness_mm.
GeometrySwatchSlotDefinition — one swatch cell’s position (row_index, column_index) and its variable_thickness_mm (the thickness the single variable role takes at that swatch).

Note what is absent: there is no layer height and no layer count. Thicknesses are absolute millimeters; the definition never knows about a slicer’s layer grid. (The legacy generator below does snap to a layer height — a key difference.)
The canonical invariants
validate_geometry_definition is the gatekeeper; it accumulates every violation and raises one ValueError. The invariants worth knowing, because they are what “a valid geometry” means everywhere downstream:

Roles are contiguous from 1. role_index values must be exactly 1..len(roles).
Exactly one variable role. Not zero, not two — one. This is the layer whose thickness varies swatch to swatch; every other role is fixed.
Role labels are unique and, if set, must equal LR_%02d of the index.
Fixed roles carry a positive thickness; variable roles carry none.
Slots tile the layout exactly. len(swatch_slots) must equal rows * columns, swatch_index must be contiguous from 0, and no two slots may share a (row, column).
The spine is tall enough. spine_total_thickness_mm must be at least the tallest swatch stack, as summed by _slot_stack_height.

Structural fingerprint — the identity
compute_structural_fingerprint is how the system decides whether two geometries are “the same shape.” It builds a canonical_geometry_payload — layout, roles (variable roles force fixed_thickness_mm to null), and slots, every float rounded to 6 places by _canonical_float — serializes it with sorted keys and no whitespace, and SHA-256s it. Because the payload is canonicalized (roles and slots sorted, floats rounded), two definitions that differ only in field order or sub-micro precision noise fingerprint identically; any structural change that survives six-decimal canonicalization produces a new hash.
build_geometry_body_plan re-derives the fingerprint and refuses to build if a definition arrived carrying a structural_fingerprint that no longer matches its content — a cheap guard against a stored geometry being edited out from under its hash.
The live API and persistence path
The production web path is the structured-geometry API, not the older STEP-record generator. The server exposes GET /api/geometries, GET /api/geometries/{geometry_id}, POST /api/geometries, PATCH /api/geometries/{geometry_id}, and DELETE /api/geometries/{geometry_id}. These routes call the corresponding SQLiteDataStore methods — list_geometry_definitions, get_geometry_definition, create_geometry_definition, update_geometry_metadata, and delete_geometry_definition — and serialize the dataclass through _geometry_payload.
SQLiteDataStore.create_geometry_definition accepts the structured roles and swatch slots, computes the fingerprint through _definition_from_create_command, and inserts one geometry row plus its geometry_roles and geometry_swatch_slots rows in one write transaction. Both alias and structural_fingerprint are unique in the database. Updating metadata changes only alias and notes; changing dimensions, roles, or slots means creating a different definition. Deletion is rejected when the geometry is referenced by a sample or bundle.
The server still exposes GET /api/steps and returns StepRecord objects. In SQLite, that is a compatibility projection reconstructed by _step_records_by_id / _step_record_from_geometry, not a second geometry store. The projection supplies compatibility values such as file_name = {geometry_id}.step and _COMPAT_LAYER_HEIGHT_MM; layer height is not part of the source-truth GeometryDefinition.
The old POST /api/steps/generate route is not the SQLite production creation path. _guard_sqlite_unimplemented_write rejects it with HTTP 501 for the SQLite backend because the route still targets the legacy DataStore/STEP-record workflow. The structured replacement is POST /api/geometries, followed by the structured artifact endpoint described below. This is a current compatibility boundary, not evidence that SQLite geometry artifact generation is absent.
The body plan
build_geometry_body_plan turns a definition into a GeometryBodyPlan of GeometryBodyPlanItems — axis-aligned RectPrisms grouped by role, in canonical builder coordinates. It has no CAD dependency; it is pure geometry the exporters consume. Two body families:

Swatch bodies (_swatch_bodies). Each role is laid down as a z-interval stacked from 0 upward in role order by _role_intervals_for_slot. A fixed role that spans every swatch at the same z-interval collapses to one swatch_area prism over the whole grid; otherwise the role emits one swatch prism per nonzero slot. This keeps the common fixed-backing case a single solid instead of N identical boxes.
Spine bodies (_spine_bodies). The surrounding frame (left, right, and top borders from _spine_interval_bodies) is split into z-intervals, each owned by the highest-index role present in any swatch at that height (_spine_owner_for_interval), with adjacent same-owner intervals merged. If no swatch role is present above the tallest stack, the top role owns the remaining spine height.

Footprint is columns * swatch_width + 2 * spine_width wide and rows * swatch_height + spine_width tall (_footprint_width, _footprint_height).
Export — lightweight STEP and per-role STL
geometry_builder.py delegates production serialization to lightweight_step.py; neither path imports a CAD kernel:

export_geometry_step calls export_geometry_step_lightweight and writes one role-grouped STEP.
export_geometry_stls calls export_geometry_stls_lightweight and writes one binary STL per geometry role, named {prefix}_{role}.stl. A geometry role is still an unfilled material slot at this point; the filament is assigned only when a sample is created.
export_geometry_artifacts is the convenience wrapper that emits a STEP plus a stl/ subdirectory in one call and returns a GeometryExportResult.

build_lightweight_geometry groups the body plan’s axis-aligned prisms by role and computes exact boundary components for each union. Every component is validated as a closed, positively oriented rectilinear solid with the expected volume before serialization by _validate_component. write_lightweight_step emits millimeter, planar AP214-style BREP records and labels each role’s product and solid. write_lightweight_stl triangulates those same validated quad boundaries into atomic binary STL files. STEP and STL therefore share one geometry model instead of asking two independent exporters to reinterpret the strip.
The packaged Calibration runtime excludes build123d, OCP, and VTK. Build123d remains a development/test dependency only for independent parity comparisons; it is not on the production structured-geometry path.
SQLite artifact lifecycle
POST /api/geometries/{geometry_id}/artifacts calls SQLiteDataStore.generate_geometry_artifacts. The store rebuilds the definition with an empty stored fingerprint, recomputes the builder fingerprint, and stages managed artifacts beside their final _system/geometry_artifacts/{geometry_id}/{fingerprint} directory. The managed STEP also has a staged compatibility copy destined for _system/step_artifacts/{geometry_id}.step.
Each generation writes manifest.json into the staged fingerprint directory. The manifest records the database and builder fingerprints, builder_version, the complete managed STEP/STL inventory, the subset requested by the current API call, body names, and remembered public export paths. get_geometry_artifact_summary resolves the manifest-owned filenames back inside the current fingerprint root rather than trusting historical absolute roots; it reports a missing/unreadable manifest, missing STEP, absent or incomplete STL set, and absent or incomplete body labels separately. The Maintenance missing-artifact audit and regeneration preflight consume that same health classification.
When export_to_output is true, the public destinations are under store.step_export_dir (Calibration/Output/Steps in the packaged Suite): {export_name}.step and an {export_name}/ directory containing the per-role STL files. A request without overwrite=true returns HTTP 409 when those destinations conflict. With overwrite enabled, Prisma stages every requested public file before publication and removes only obsolete STL paths recorded as owned by the previous manifest; unrelated files in an existing export directory are preserved.
Publication is one rollback-capable filesystem transaction across the staged fingerprint directory, compatibility STEP, requested public STEP/STLs, and manifest-owned stale removals. Existing targets are displaced to short sibling rollback paths, staged targets are promoted with os.replace, and any later failure removes promoted replacements and restores every displaced path. Generation or manifest-staging failure occurs before this boundary and cannot alter live files. The transaction rejects filesystem links and hardlinked mutable file targets; managed trees are inspected for nested links before replacement. A rollback failure preserves and reports its recovery path instead of deleting it. POST /api/steps/{step_id}/ensure-artifact remains the compatibility repair endpoint and calls this same structured generator.
The public endpoint can generate STEP, STL, or both, but it rejects a request that selects neither. Unrequested managed file types already present in the current fingerprint directory are retained and inventoried, while the response’s legacy step_path/stl_paths fields continue to describe the types requested by that call. The lightweight serializer collects every disconnected component of one role into the same role product/file, so STL export still produces one file per role.
Geometry bundles and sample creation
Bundles are SQLite records that group geometry definitions and map each geometry role to a shared material slot. They are not CAD artifacts. geometry_bundles and geometry_bundle_members store the bundle and ordered geometry membership; geometry_bundle_material_slots and geometry_bundle_role_slot_mappings store the material-slot vocabulary and role assignments.
_bundle_detail_in_tx derives mapping_status as unmapped, incomplete, invalid, or mapped and exposes creation_eligible only for the fully mapped state. save_bundle_mapping validates the draft against the member roles and rewrites the slot and mapping rows transactionally. create_samples_from_bundle_slots refuses any bundle that is not mapped, then creates samples for every bundle member, with optional multiple filament values for one batch material slot. The bundle API is therefore a role-assignment and sample-generation layer above geometry definitions; it does not alter the geometry fingerprint.
Role labels in STEP
Role labeling is now part of serialization rather than post-export string surgery. write_lightweight_step creates one named PRODUCT and ADVANCED_BREP_SHAPE_REPRESENTATION per role, while _add_component_geometry gives every component’s MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP the same role-derived name. Fusion and OrcaSlicer therefore receive role identity directly from the generated STEP entities.
The legacy strip generator (off the production path)
strips/generator.py (calibration.strips.generator) is the older geometry code, self-described as “Used by experiment_builder.ipynb.” It hardcodes a fixed 8-swatch strip with baked physical constants (SWATCH_W = 12.0, N_SWATCHES = 8) and snaps thicknesses to a layer height through snap_offset — the opposite of the flexible, layer-height-free GeometryDefinition. It has its own generate_step / generate_stls, and is imported only by the JSON DataStore (data_access.py), not by the production SQLite path — so it is dormant in the packaged app. The live geometry consumers are sqlite_data_access.py and maintenance.py, both of which use geometry_builder.py.
strips/step_parser.py (calibration.strips.step_parser) is a small compatibility helper that parses metadata (variable_thicknesses_mm, fixed_layers, layer_height_mm, layer_count) back out of legacy STEP filenames, tolerating both the double-underscore and older single-underscore naming. It is a filename reader, not part of structured geometry construction. The SQLite projection does not need it to reconstruct a geometry; it reads the normalized role and slot tables instead.

prisma-calibration/technical-reference/g.filePath: Prisma Calibration/Technical Reference/Geometry-bundle role mapping and sample creation.md
prisma-calibration/technical-reference/g.title: Geometry-bundle role mapping and sample creation
prisma-calibration/technical-reference/g.content:
Geometry bundles group normalized geometry definitions and add a mapping layer from each member’s canonical geometry roles to shared material slots. They do not change a geometry’s structural fingerprint. The live mapping and sample-creation path is SQLite-only and is implemented in SQLiteDataStore.
Bundle detail and mapping state
GET /api/geometry-bundles/{bundle_id} returns _bundle_detail_in_tx output. Each member has a stable geometry_bundle_member_id, an ordered geometry_id, and the roles loaded from geometry_roles. Each role carries geometry_role_id, contiguous role_index, role_label (normally LR_%02d), role_kind, fixed thickness when applicable, and its mapped material_slot_id.
Material slots are bundle-local rows with persisted IDs, positions, keys, and labels such as Shared Filament A. A mapping save deletes and rebuilds these rows, assigning canonical slot IDs/keys/labels by saved position; draft slot IDs are editor-local references, not identities that survive the rewrite. Role mappings are bundle-member-specific: each submitted geometry_role_id is checked against the member’s geometry, and a mapping row is invalid if its member, role, or slot foreign reference is missing or inconsistent.
The derived mapping_status is:

unmapped when there are no material slots or mappings;
invalid when a member, geometry role, or material-slot reference is inconsistent;
mapped when every role across the members has a valid slot; or
incomplete for a remaining partial state.

creation_eligible is true only for mapped. This state is computed from current database rows; it is not a manually editable flag.
Saving a mapping
PUT /api/geometry-bundles/{bundle_id}/mapping accepts draft slot IDs and a role map for every current bundle member. save_bundle_mapping optionally checks expected_updated_at for an optimistic-concurrency conflict, requires the submitted member set to match the current members, rejects duplicate or foreign role IDs, and rejects unknown draft slots. Unless allow_incomplete is true, every role must be assigned.
The save deletes and rebuilds the bundle’s material-slot and role-mapping rows in one write transaction. Only draft slots used by an assignment are retained. They are normalized to persisted slot IDs based on position, with canonical keys and labels. The bundle updated_at changes after the rewrite. An incomplete mapping can therefore be saved for editing, but it cannot be used for sample creation.
Creating samples from slots
POST /api/samples/from-geometry-bundle requires the SQLite store’s create_samples_from_bundle_slots. It refuses a missing bundle, a non-mapped bundle, unknown/duplicate/missing slot assignments, and unknown filament IDs. Every persisted material slot must receive a filament unless it is the selected batch_material_slot_id; batch mode requires at least two batch_filament_ids and substitutes each batch filament into that slot.
For each batch value—or once when not batching—the store walks every bundle member. For each role it looks up the mapped material slot, creates an explicit {role_index, filament_id} assignment, identifies the single variable role, and collects fixed-role thicknesses. It then builds and inserts one sample per member. With batching, the result is one sample per member per batch filament. Allocation and inserts occur in one SQLite write transaction, and the created samples are reloaded from the database before returning.
The route returns only sample summaries (sample_id, name, step_id, and step_file) and an empty errors list on success. The ordinary POST /api/samples/from-bundle route is a separate compatibility/list-based bundle workflow; it can accept per-step role assignments, but it does not consume the persisted material-slot mapping described here.
Boundary with geometry source truth
GeometryDefinition owns the physical roles and swatch slots; the bundle mapping assigns filaments to those roles for a group of geometries. A bundle’s material_slot_id is not a filament ID and is not a role index. The resulting sample stores canonical role assignments and legacy-shaped variable/fixed fields derived from them. Changing a geometry definition is a different operation and is guarded by geometry persistence rules; mapping a bundle does not rebuild geometry artifacts.

prisma-calibration/technical-reference/m.filePath: Prisma Calibration/Technical Reference/Model workflow, publication, and review.md
prisma-calibration/technical-reference/m.title: Model workflow, publication, and review
prisma-calibration/technical-reference/m.content:
In one sentence: the Fit Models maintenance operation drives execute_model_fit_workflow (calibration.fitting.model_fit_workflow), which runs Color Model v1 and v2 and conditionally runs the Camera Transform in a fixed order, replaces each successfully fitted family’s current Calibration fit through calibration.fitting.model_publication, and leaves one registered artifact set per family for modeling_review.py (calibration.modeling_review) — while the separate Publish Models workflow copies an exact, validated snapshot into an immutable Generator model library.

This page is the hub that ties the three model fitters together. It maps the unified fan-out and preflight, Calibration’s replaceable one-current-fit-per-kind contract, the separate immutable-library publication boundary, the read side that powers the operator’s modeling surface, and the three shared modules every fit calls before it touches color data. In older implementation names, publish_model_fit means “make this Calibration fit current”; it does not mean “publish a library to Generator.” It does not re-derive any model’s math — the physics of each fit lives in its own page and in How It Works. For the three fitters themselves see Spline model fitting (v1), Photo-stack model fitting (v2), and The camera transform fitter; for the model forms, Color Model v1 / Color Model v2 / The Camera Transform.
Related: calibration.fitting.model_fit_workflow · calibration.fitting.model_publication · calibration.model_library_publication · lib.standard_model_library · lib.model_library_store · calibration.modeling_review · calibration.fitting.physical_stack · calibration.fitting.filament_roles · calibration.fitting.filament_exclusions
The unified fan-out — one button, three fitters
“Fit Models” is the operator label for the maintenance operation refit_calibration_models. It is registered as a maintenance operation, so it runs through the same preflight/execute boundary as every other operation: _preflight_refit_calibration_models and _execute_refit_calibration_models, both of which delegate to model_fit_workflow.py through options_from_scope, build_model_fit_preflight, and execute_model_fit_workflow. The workflow preflight is SQLite-only; non-SQLite stores are returned as blocked rather than being sent through the fitters.
The workflow recognizes three model kinds, named by module constants: MODEL_LEGACY_SPLINE = "legacy_spline", MODEL_PHOTO_STACK = "photo_stack_v2", MODEL_CAMERA_TRANSFORM = "camera_transform". execute_model_fit_workflow runs them in a fixed sequence and short-circuits on the first failure:

Legacy spline (v1) — run_legacy_spline_fit_all(..., publish=True), from calibration.fitting.legacy_spline_fit_job. Detail: Spline model fitting (v1).
Photo Stack (v2) — run_photo_stack_fit_job(..., publish=False), then the exception-compensated publish_photo_stack_fit. Detail: Photo-stack model fitting (v2).
Camera Transform — run_camera_transform_build_job(..., publish=False), then the exception-compensated publish_camera_transform_fit. Detail: The camera transform fitter.

The three fitters are parallel siblings on a shared spine, not layered: each loads its own evidence, fits, and independently replaces its current Calibration fit; the workflow just orders them and aggregates status. The legacy-spline and photo-stack stages always run; the Camera Transform runs only when its plan says so (below). _stage_progress rescales each fitter’s inner progress into an overall bar sized by total_stages. The workflow contains cooperative cancellation checks before and between stages, and the legacy-spline fitter also accepts the callback while it runs. However, the registered Fit Models maintenance operation uses the default not_supported cancellation policy, so the application does not offer a user cancel action. Photo Stack and Camera Transform also have no intra-stage cancellation callback.
Workflow options and the preflight
ModelFitWorkflowOptions is a frozen two-field dataclass: force_camera_transform and use_fit_exclusions (the latter pinned to True). options_from_scope builds it from the request scope, reading only force_camera_transform — the per-run fit-state exclusions are always on for this workflow.
build_model_fit_preflight is the gate. It first refuses any non-SQLite backend outright (“Fit Models requires the SQLite backend”), then builds a model_plan for the three kinds. Legacy and Photo Stack are hardwired to action: "run" with reason always_refit_color_models — the two color models are always refit. The Camera Transform is the only conditional stage: _build_camera_transform_plan compares the live fit-input fingerprint against both the stored artifact manifest and the current model-fit record. It returns run for a forced, missing, invalid, unregistered, fingerprint-mismatched, old-fingerprint, or input-changed transform; skip/up_to_date for an unchanged transform; and skip/insufficient_evidence when fewer than five eligible samples exist. An insufficient-evidence skip does not manufacture a current Camera Transform, so immutable-library publication remains blocked if one is missing or stale.
The preflight also computes a plan_digest through _build_plan_digest — a SHA-256 over the scope, per-kind action/reason, the Camera Transform input hash, legacy target filaments, and Photo Stack evidence hash. execute_model_fit_workflow recomputes the preflight and refuses to run if the stored plan_digest no longer matches (“Model fitting plan changed. Run preflight again”), so a reviewed plan cannot silently change before execution.
The result envelope carries status, per-kind model_results, a historically named partial_publication map recording which kinds actually got a new current model_fit_id, and a ui_refresh directive that invalidates the model-artifact caches for all three kinds. Current-fit replacement is not a transaction spanning all three fitters: the spline stage can complete before Photo Stack or Camera Transform fails, and the internal cancellation paths after a completed stage return the earlier replacement with a targeted refresh. No immutable Generator library is created by Fit Models.
V1 has an additional partial-success boundary inside its own stage. If at least one profile fits and pair-correction generation succeeds, its successful subset can be published even when another filament failed. The unified workflow then sees the nonzero v1 failed count, returns an overall failure with partial_publication.legacy_spline = true, and does not start v2. “Rollback-capable publication” therefore describes recovery from ordinary publication exceptions; it does not mean every target filament must fit before any v1 replacement can occur.
Direct fitter entry points
The unified operation is the main fan-out, but the server also exposes separate asynchronous Photo Stack and Camera Transform jobs and synchronous/asynchronous spline /api/profiles/fit-all routes. These paths run one fitter and replace its current result through the same coordinated publication boundary; they are not alternate model kinds and do not publish a Generator library. The server uses _try_begin_model_fit_run / _end_model_fit_run around these jobs and the direct spline routes, so overlapping model-fit jobs are rejected with a conflict rather than allowed to replace the same working state concurrently. The unified maintenance job also claims the maintenance_model_fit owner and is checked by the same blocker logic. The current Modeling UI calls the unified workflow; the old direct-profile frontend renderer remains dormant.
The direct asynchronous v1 worker has a status-reporting defect: after _run_profile_fit_all returns it records the job as completed even when the result contains per-filament failures or a failed status. The unified workflow does not share this defect because it explicitly checks those fields and stops. Treat the direct async route as a compatibility/developer surface, not the user-facing success authority.
Internal current-fit replacement — one fit per kind, staleness aware
calibration.fitting.model_publication holds the shared publish helpers that every fitter routes through. It keeps common path/artifact registration logic at the store boundary and imports each model family’s pointer-management helpers inside the coordinated publisher that needs them. The entry shapes are:

Directory publish primitive — publish_artifact_directory_model_fit walks an artifact directory through model_artifacts_from_directory, converts every file to a store-relative POSIX path through store_relative_posix_path (which raises if a path escapes the data root), and calls the store’s publish_model_fit.
Coordinated directory-model publishers — publish_photo_stack_fit and publish_camera_transform_fit activate the staged filesystem pointer, invoke the directory primitive with an explicit artifact set, roll the pointer and staged directory back if ordinary SQLite publication raises, and garbage-collect the prior run/generation only after both layers succeed. Camera Transform uses the family directory as its registered root and registers the active CURRENT pointer alongside the three generation files; Photo Stack registers the selected run directory.
Legacy-spline publish — production fitting uses publish_staged_legacy_spline_fit, which swaps the staged successful-profile subset and pair_corrections.json into place, calls publish_legacy_spline_fit, and restores the old files if ordinary database publication raises. The lower-level publisher records one spline_profile:{fid} artifact per fitted filament plus the shared pair-correction file. publish_legacy_spline_artifact_set is the sibling that republishes current files outside the staged fit path, guarded by profile_file_is_publishable: excluded filaments and profile JSON carrying stale / stale_reason / stale_at are omitted.

All of them converge on the store’s historically named publish_model_fit, which treats a model family as one replaceable current Calibration fit, not a fit-history archive. Before writing, it collects every existing row for the same model_kind. In one SQLite write transaction it inserts the replacement fit, contributors, and artifacts as current, then deletes all prior parent rows; foreign-key cascades remove their contributor and artifact rows. The return payload reports those deleted ids as superseded_model_fit_ids, but there is no durable superseded activation state. model_kind is validated against _MODEL_KINDS = {"camera_transform", "legacy_spline", "photo_stack_v2"}, and current-fit replacement requires at least one contributor.
The SQLite transaction does not include the preceding filesystem or pointer changes. All three publishers compensate for ordinary exceptions, but none has a process-kill journal. A hard stop inside v1’s directory/pair swaps can leave missing or mixed artifacts; a hard stop after v2 latest.json or Camera Transform CURRENT advances can leave pointer-reading consumers on the new files while SQLite still names the old fit. Startup does not complete or reverse these model-publication transitions. Publication readiness detects resulting hash/pointer mismatches; it does not repair them.
stale means something different from superseded. A currently retained fit is marked stale when tracked evidence or fit controls that contributed to it are changed, so its artifacts no longer describe the corpus state from which it was fitted. Adding newly accepted evidence does not retroactively stale an existing fit merely because that sample was not among its recorded contributors. One current exception is review revocation: changing a contributor’s accepted result back to pending removes it from future-fit eligibility but does not stale the existing fit. The ordinary UI has no standalone unaccept action; Reject uses full extraction invalidation. A stale row remains available to status/review code until a successful current-fit replacement deletes it. Startup also calls prune_superseded_model_fits to collapse databases created under the older history-retaining lifecycle to one row per family.
User publication — one-way immutable copy to Generator
The topbar Publish Models workflow is a separate ownership boundary implemented by calibration.model_library_publication, lib.standard_model_library, and lib.model_library_store. It never changes Calibration’s current-fit lifecycle. GET /api/models/publication/readiness verifies that all three required fits are current, their registered artifacts still match their hashes and schemas, the combined contract is consistent, and the public filament catalog is available. A missing, stale, changed, or incomplete component blocks both publication actions. Camera Transform readiness specifically requires the registered and hash-matching camera_transform/CURRENT pointer plus the three registered files in the generation it names.
After the operator supplies the library name, version, and publisher (plus optional description and release notes), the dialog offers two copies of that exact current generation:

Export Library Package calls POST /api/models/publication/export and writes a validated ZIP under Calibration/Output/Published Models.
Publish to Generator calls POST /api/models/publication/install and installs a new immutable library under Generator’s Model Libraries folder. It is deliberately inactive; the operator uses Model Library → Manage in Generator’s configuration rail and chooses Activate and Restart Prisma.
Open Published Models Folder calls the local-only POST /api/models/publication/open-folder.

The allowlisted payload contains the public filament manifest/catalog plus the runtime artifacts for legacy spline v1, Photo Stack v2, and Camera Transform. It does not contain Calibration’s SQLite database, source or extracted images, samples, raw evidence, per-sample calibration predictions, or private notes. Publication stages and validates a copy, then either packages it or lets the Generator library store install it; Calibration does not retain a mutable published-model tree and cannot later modify or activate the installed copy. Generator likewise cannot see or alter Calibration’s working artifacts.
The read side — what the Modeling page renders
calibration.modeling_review is the read half: it never fits anything, it loads Calibration’s current working artifacts and compares them against observed color. It is imported only by calibration.server, which exposes it at /api/models/status and /api/models/review/.... Its six public builders back The Modeling page:

build_model_status_payload — per-kind currentness (state, generated_at, stale_reason) via _model_currentness_payload, labeled by MODEL_LABELS: legacy_spline → "Color Model v1", photo_stack_v2 → "Color Model v2", camera_transform → "Camera Transform".
build_modeling_overview — inclusion counts (samples/swatches included vs excluded) plus an attention block.
list_modeling_samples / get_modeling_sample — the per-sample review, whose _sample_model_detail is the heart of the comparison.
list_modeling_filaments / get_modeling_filament — the per-filament view.

_sample_model_detail is where observed and predicted meet. It loads the current Camera Transform as the display transform, then builds two predictions: _photo_stack_model_domains (reads the v2 sample_predictions.json selected by latest.json) and _legacy_spline_model_domains (recomposes v1 on the fly through composition.compose using the sample’s canonical geometry). Both, plus the measured values, are emitted in two domains — transmission (raw linear-to-hex) and appearance (the Camera Transform applied to model predictions) — each with corrected and uncorrected prediction variants. The Camera Transform is not a fourth per-swatch prediction: measured appearance comes directly from the accepted extraction sidecar, while v1 and v2 transmission predictions are transformed for display. If the Camera Transform is missing, predicted appearance is returned unavailable while measured embedded-JPEG appearance can still be present. Because v2 review reads latest.json directly, an interrupted publication can temporarily disagree with SQLite currentness until the working set is repaired. The transform math is The Camera Transform; the modeling surface is The Modeling page.
The sample and filament evidence tables are accepted-only because modeling_review._model_eligible_sample_rows filters rows by has_accepted_extraction. This is explicit on the read side, in addition to the SQLite measurement projection that protects all three production fit adapters.
Shared foundation 1 — the sample→stack bridge
calibration.fitting.physical_stack is the single bridge from a sample record to a canonical bottom-to-top layer stack; its module docstring is explicit that callers “must not reconstruct stack order from legacy fixed/variable convenience fields.” Both v1 and v2 go through it (its Imported by list is fitting and the v2 evidence module).
physical_stack_for_swatch reads sample.roles in canonical role_index order, pulls the one variable role’s thickness from the swatch’s variable series, validates exactly one variable role, and returns a frozen PhysicalStack of RoleLayers. Along the way _model_role_hints assigns each layer a semantic role from physical position: a white below all color is base_white, white above is cap_white, color is color, and a white sandwiched between non-white layers is rejected as ambiguous. physical_stacks_for_sample maps it over every swatch. Two predicates round it out: has_fixed_above_variable and is_legacy_spline_supported_stack (true only when the variable role is physically topmost) — the latter is how v1 decides whether it can interpret a geometry at all. Failures raise PhysicalStackError rather than guessing. The optics of stacking these layers is Color Model v1 / Color Model v2.
Shared foundation 2 — filament role and white classifiers
calibration.fitting.filament_roles supplies the explicit model-white classification used by the color-model fitters:

White — model_white_filament_ids returns the set of filaments flagged white_cap_eligible; is_model_white tests membership. This is the set physical_stack’s role-hint logic uses to tell base white from cap white.
Crucially, the module also bakes classifier provenance into a color-model fit. filament_role_snapshot captures each filament’s white_cap_eligible and exclude_from_model flags; filament_role_snapshot_hash hashes that snapshot; photo_stack_bundle_classifier_metadata packages the white-classifier schema, version, id list, and snapshot hash into the v2 runtime bundle. require_known_filaments fails loudly if evidence references a filament absent from the library. Camera Transform validation instead groups only by sample and measured transmission.

Shared foundation 3 — per-filament model exclusion
calibration.fitting.filament_exclusions is a small, always-on, stateless dropper: a filament flagged exclude_from_model in the registry is removed from every production fit. It is imported by all three fit paths (v1 fitting, v2 evidence, CT corpus).
The precise semantic is the load-bearing part. excluded_filament_ids reads the flagged ids from the registry. sample_references_excluded_filament drops a sample if the excluded filament appears in ANY role — variable or fixed backing — via _sample_filament_ids, which walks the canonical sample.roles table and returns every referenced filament id, not just the characterized (variable) one. So excluding a white backing filament removes not only its own solo strips but every overlay sample that stacks on top of it. samples_excluded_by_filament precomputes that whole-corpus set of dropped samples; only the v1 spline fit unions it in directly. The v2 Photo Stack evidence builder and live Camera Transform corpus instead read excluded_filament_ids and apply the same rule per sample — row by row rather than from the precomputed set.
This is distinct from the per-run fit_exclude / fit_state toggles (which are UI-gated on use_fit_exclusions): exclude_from_model is a permanent property of the filament, ungated, replacing the old hardwired SKIP constant. Where the flag is set and what it means operationally is Managing filaments.

prisma-calibration/technical-reference/p.title: Photo-stack model fitting (v2)
prisma-calibration/technical-reference/p.content:
In one sentence: the calibration side of Color Model v2 is a thin driver — live datastore samples become canonical fit evidence (calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.evidence), that evidence is bridged into the vendored research numerical fitter and renamed into the public contract (calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.live_fit), a fit-job boundary writes a staged candidate (calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.fit_job), and the shared publication boundary coordinates its latest.json activation with SQLite replacement before deleting the old run — while the heavy model math lives entirely in lib.photo_stack_model.*.

This page is the code-level map of the v2 (photo-stack) fit driver. It maps the modules, the data flow, and what is live versus vestigial. It does not re-derive the model itself — for what an optical-density curve, a white-context term, or a pair correction is, and why the model is shaped the way it is, read the How It Works page Color Model v2 — model and correction layer both — (and, for the earlier spline model, Color Model v1). The shared numerical model — fitting, prediction, and artifact I/O — lives in lib.photo_stack_model.model, lib.photo_stack_model.predict, and lib.photo_stack_model.artifacts; calibration only feeds it and files its output. How this fit is triggered, published, and reviewed within the unified model-fit workflow is Model workflow, publication, and review; the operator’s-eye view is The Modeling page.
On this page, publish_photo_stack_fit and similar code names mean “make this Calibration fit current.” They replace Calibration’s working generation and do not create, activate, or mutate an immutable Generator model library; user-facing publication is the separate Publish Models boundary.
Related: calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.evidence · calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.live_fit · calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.fit_job · calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.write_artifact · calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.photo_stack_engine · calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.metrics · calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.smoke_fit_job
The driver pipeline at a glance
One public entry point strings the stages together. run_photo_stack_fit_job in calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.fit_job reports six progress phases:

Build evidence — build_photo_stack_evidence(store, …).
Fit — fit_live_photo_stack_bundle(evidence), run under a heartbeat so a long fit still emits progress.
Fit the correction layer — apply_or_build_photo_stack_correction(…), which lives in the shared lib.photo_stack_model.correction_layer.
Write the candidate — write_photo_stack_candidate(…, update_latest=publish). Both production webapp callers pass publish=False, leaving activation to publish_photo_stack_fit after the fit returns.

Steps in between assemble a measured-vs-predicted review payload through _build_sample_predictions and a review summary through _review_summary. The reached-from edges are on the fit-job node’s Imported by list: calibration.fitting.model_fit_workflow (the unified workflow that calls it live), calibration.server, and the dev harness smoke_fit_job — see the Model workflow, publication, and review page for the workflow wiring.
Stage 1 — evidence: live samples → canonical fit rows
build_photo_stack_evidence walks store.list_samples() and emits one canonical evidence document: a summary, an input_fingerprint, per-sample records, and per-swatch records. It is strict by design — the docstring notes geometry must be annotated, with no swatch-index fallback. Failures raise EvidenceBuildError.
What the adapter does, and does not, decide:

It filters, it does not fit. Samples are skipped (recorded in skipped_samples, not silently dropped) for referencing an exclude_from_model filament, not being processed, or missing measurements / strip definition.
Accepted review is enforced by the SQLite sample projection. The adapter tests processed plus Sample.measurements; it does not repeat a review_accepted condition. In production SQLite, measurements are hydrated only from an accepted extraction, so a pending-review result never reaches the evidence rows. The focused pending-review payload test covers this boundary.
Measured color comes from the sidecar, not the sample. _MEASURED_SOURCE = "sidecar" makes the per-swatch linear RGB read from the extraction-result sidecar via _sidecar_swatch_map, which fails loud if the sidecar is absent or malformed. Fit-control state (fit_state, exclusion_reason) stays a live read off the sample. use_measured_source("legacy") can temporarily flip back to the Sample.measurements color path. For what the sidecar is, see Extraction and Data access and persistence.
It classifies the physical stack. Each swatch’s realized bottom-to-top layer stack (from physical_stack_for_swatch) is tagged by _classify_realized_stack into evidence classes (white_only, naked_single_filament, color_over_white, single_color_sandwich, cross_color_multilayer_sandwich, …) that the fitter later uses to pick a role family.
It fingerprints its inputs. input_fingerprint hashes the samples directory, the filament registry, the filament-role snapshot, the source-sample projection, and the evidence itself. It also records the resolved data-root path, so it is a same-workspace fit identity rather than a location-independent content identifier.

use_fit_exclusions (default False) controls whether excluded samples/swatches are marked included=False; the live workflow passes True (see Stage 3). The color math here (linear-to-OKLab, optical density) is inlined deliberately without importing the spline runtime through _linear_to_oklab — it is bookkeeping, not the model.
Stage 2 — live_fit: the bridge to the vendored fitter
live_fit.py (calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.live_fit) describes itself as the Prisma-owned bridge from calibration datastore evidence to the accepted research numerical fitter: the research math is vendored unchanged, while the wrapper handles live evidence adaptation, candidate metadata, runtime-bundle export, and public naming. The model math is not here — the fitter is imported from the vendored research engine package, and the public model/predict/artifact surface is lib.photo_stack_model.model / lib.photo_stack_model.predict / lib.photo_stack_model.artifacts.
fit_live_photo_stack_bundle does three things:

Reshape. evidence_payload_to_photo_stack_rows flattens the canonical evidence into the wide pandas row schema the research fitter expects, reading each swatch’s explicit bottom-to-top model_layer_triples through _model_layers_from_swatch rather than inferring stack order from legacy fixed/variable columns. It raises if there is not at least one included swatch.
Fit on the full corpus — no holdout. The rows are passed straight to research_fit.full_fit_predictions(rows, …); the model is fit and predicted on the same included rows. There is a fold = sample_num % 5 column, but the live fit does not split on it — predictions are in-sample. Excluded swatches are dropped upstream (Stage 1) via the included flag, not held out for validation here.
Rename into the public contract. Because the vendored engine stamps its own codenames, _sanitize_public_payload and _rename_research_prediction_columns rewrite research identity tokens to the public photo_stack / v2 names. Only strings change; numbers are untouched. The assembled _build_bundle validates against the shared lib.photo_stack_model.bundle schema and stamps a reproducible fingerprint that deliberately excludes wall-clock timing fields through _fingerprint_payload. The return value is a frozen LiveFitResult.

Stage 3 — fit_job: orchestration, correction layer, review payload
Back in fit_job.py, after the live fit the job:

Validates the bundle is a live source-of-truth artifact through _validate_live_fit_bundle.
Builds/refits the correction layer by handing the live predictions to the shared apply_or_build_photo_stack_correction, producing the photo_stack_v2_corrected model named by CORRECTED_MODEL_NAME. What the correction layer does is covered by Color Model v2’s correction-layer section; the code lives in lib.photo_stack_model.correction_layer.
Assembles the review payload — _build_sample_predictions turns the corrected full-fit rows into per-sample, per-swatch measured-vs-predicted chips (with stack diagrams and OKLab deltas), and _review_summary rolls up mean / p90 / max ΔE. This is the JSON the review UI renders; see The Modeling page.
Emits progress through _emit / _run_with_heartbeat so the six phases surface in the webapp job stream.

When the unified workflow drives this job it passes use_fit_exclusions=True, so operator sample/swatch exclusions are honored; the standalone default is False.
Stage 4 — staged write and coordinated publication
write_photo_stack_candidate is a thin pass-through to the shared writer write_candidate_artifact in lib.photo_stack_model.artifacts — its only job is to write a candidate without touching legacy spline profile outputs. Everything structural happens in the shared writer:

Candidates land under data_root/filaments/photo_stack_models/<run_id>/ through candidate_root, written atomically: files go to .tmp-<run_id>, required files and the runtime bundle are validated, then os.replace publishes the complete directory.
write_candidate_artifact still supports update_latest=True for direct/compatibility callers, but that is not the production webapp publication path. The workflow and standalone server job deliberately write with publish=False.
publish_photo_stack_fit validates the staged directory, atomically advances latest.json with activate_candidate_artifact, and then calls SQLite publish_model_fit. If ordinary SQLite publication raises, it restores the prior pointer and deletes the staged run. Only after both pointer and database replacement succeed does it attempt to garbage-collect superseded run directories, keeping one.

There is no operator-facing commit step, but there is an internal publication sequence with compensating filesystem rollback for ordinary exceptions. A successful fit becomes the sole retained photo_stack_v2 database fit. The superseded run-directory cleanup is deliberately best-effort, so a Windows lock can leave an old, unregistered directory behind without making it current or selectable.
The pointer and SQLite update are not process-kill atomic. A hard stop after latest.json advances but before publish_model_fit commits can leave the new run selected by pointer-reading review code while SQLite still reports the old fit. There is no startup journal that reconciles this split. SQLite-aware runtime bundle lookup prefers the registered fit, but the Modeling sample-prediction reader uses latest.json directly; publication readiness detects the artifact mismatch rather than repairing it. Do not kill Calibration while Fit Models is publishing, and verify model status/readiness after an abnormal stop.
Vestigial and support modules
Three modules in this package are not on the live fit path:

photo_stack_engine.py (calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.photo_stack_engine) is largely vestigial. Its docstring states outright that live fitting now happens in fitting.photo_stack_model.live_fit. What fit_job still imports from it is only ENGINE_STATUS_READY. The pending-payload machinery — build_pending_photo_stack_candidate_payload, build_context_index, require_photo_stack_runtime_ready — describes an “engine not yet wired” era and is diagnostic-only; its Imported by list is just the fit job.
metrics.py (calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.metrics) is a near-stub. Its single function summarize_metric_rows returns {"row_count": …} and nothing more; the module’s docstring calls it a helper “for future photo stack fitting jobs.” Its Architecture node shows it is not imported by any other calibration module.
smoke_fit_job.py (calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.smoke_fit_job) is a developer CLI. Its docstring calls it a developer smoke harness, not a user-facing webapp command. It constructs a raw DataStore and runs the fit job from a --data-root argument; it is not imported by anything.

(For contrast, the sibling legacy_spline_fit_job.py — the v1 driver — is live despite its name, reached through the same unified model-fit workflow; that is documented on the Color Model v1 fitting page, not here.)

prisma-calibration/technical-reference/s.title: Sample mutations, invalidation, and profile staleness
prisma-calibration/technical-reference/s.content:
Sample evidence and provenance changes are handled by sample_mutations.py (calibration.sample_mutations) and by the SQLite-aware routes in server.py. Those mutation paths keep measurements, extraction artifacts, review state, and contributor-backed fitted models aligned when geometry, role, image, blank, orientation, or processed evidence changes. Review acceptance is a narrower state transition with an important current limitation described below.
Status is derived only for unprocessed samples
recompute_sample_status(sample) leaves processing_status unchanged when sample.measurements is present. Otherwise it assigns assigned only when assigned_image, assigned_blank_id, and orientation_rots are all set; any incomplete evidence assignment becomes unassigned. This helper does not inspect the database extraction-result table.
The server’s _maybe_mark_assigned is an older local helper and is not the main mutation seam for the current assignment routes. assign-image, assign-blank, image swapping, rejection, and provenance updates call invalidate_sample_processing when their meaning changes, then save through the selected store.
What counts as processing output
_has_processing_outputs treats any of the following as output: in-memory measurements; status processed, failed, or flagged; a SQLite extraction result; a legacy JSON thumbnail directory; or a JSON extraction-result sidecar. A pending SQLite extraction result therefore counts even if the model object has no measurements yet.
When invalidation finds no output, it only recomputes assignment status. When output exists, it clears measurements, flag_reason, review_accepted, excluded_swatches, and, by default, fit_exclude. It then recomputes assigned/unassigned from the evidence fields.
For the JSON backend, invalidation also removes thumbnails/{sample_id} and the extraction-result sidecar. If the previous sample could have contributed to a fit—its measurements existed or its status was processed—the previous sample’s variable and fixed filament IDs are passed to flag_profile_stale.
For SQLite, invalidate_sample_processing itself does not call mark_profiles_stale_for_sample and does not delete the extraction row. SQLite performs those durable operations inside SQLiteDataStore._save_sample_in_tx when the changed sample signature is saved: geometry, role assignments, evidence, and a transition away from a processed state can trigger contributor-based model-fit staleness and extraction-result deletion. This split is intentional in the current code path: callers must save the mutated sample for the SQLite invalidation to become durable. The post-commit cleanup then removes derived sample visuals.
Evidence routes
POST /api/samples/{sample_id}/assign-image verifies the managed image, clears orientation when the image changes unless the request explicitly supplies one, and invalidates on image or orientation changes. POST /api/samples/{sample_id}/assign-blank verifies the blank and, for SQLite, rejects a missing non-active blank source. It invalidates when the blank changes.
POST /api/samples/swap-images swaps the two image fields, clears both orientations because orientation is source-photo-specific, invalidates both samples, and uses SQLite save_samples when available. POST /api/samples/{sample_id}/reject invalidates the sample and saves it for reprocessing.
Deletion differs by backend. The JSON route conservatively calls the per-filament stale helper before deletion when the sample has measurements or processed status. On SQLite that helper is deliberately a no-op; SQLiteDataStore.delete_sample marks every model fit that actually names the sample as a contributor stale and deletes the sample in the same database transaction, then removes derived visuals after commit.
Provenance mutation
PUT /api/samples/{sample_id} resolves a StepRecord, validates explicit role assignments, and can update the geometry reference, variable/fixed filament fields, notes, and review acceptance. In SQLite, canonical role_assignments are required for writes that change sample geometry or roles; the legacy variable/fixed fields are compatibility payloads and cannot remap a SQLite sample by themselves. A role assignment must cover exactly the selected geometry’s role indices, resolve every filament, contain exactly one variable role, and preserve the role’s role_kind.
When geometry or role provenance changes, the route compares the old and new role/geometry signatures, calls invalidation with a reason naming the changed fields, and saves with the explicit role payload. SQLite’s save transaction compares the current database signature with the new signature, deletes the extraction result when the signature meaningfully changes, marks affected model fits stale, rewrites role rows, updates the evidence relation, and writes fit controls as needed.
Review acceptance and current model fits
Changing review_accepted through the live sample-update route keeps the projected sample flag and SQLite extraction row in lockstep within the sample-save transaction. An accepted result becomes eligible for a future fit; a pending result is omitted from accepted_model_contributors.
The current implementation does not mark an already published model fit stale merely because an extraction result changes between accepted and pending_review. Accepting a new result therefore expands the evidence available to the next fit without invalidating the existing fit. More importantly, directly revoking acceptance from a result that was recorded as a contributor removes it from future-fit eligibility but leaves that existing fit’s currentness_state unchanged. The ordinary review UI has no standalone unaccept action: Reject follows the full invalidation path instead. This gap matters to direct API or data-store callers and should not be mistaken for a stronger currentness guarantee.
The lower-level apply_sample_update function is retained as domain logic for older callers. It has a compatibility-era geometry rebuild that supplies fallback strip dimensions rather than the canonical StepRecord.strip_geometry; the live SQLite route contains the authoritative explicit-role path. Its comment claiming that notes is absent from Sample is obsolete: Sample.notes now exists, but this compatibility helper still does not assign the requested note. The live PUT /api/samples/{sample_id} route does assign and persist notes, so callers should not treat apply_sample_update as the current SQLite write seam.
Profile ownership
sample_profile_filament_ids returns the sample’s variable filament and all nonempty fixed filament IDs. That conservative dependency set is used by JSON invalidation and the JSON-side pre-delete stale call. SQLite instead uses recorded model_fit_contributors, so it stales the fits that actually named the sample. Neither mechanism claims that every per-filament profile necessarily consumed every layer.
Anchors
