prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: Preprocessing operators
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: Generator ships five self-registering, default-off preprocessing operators—A1, B1, B3, C1, and C2—plus shared nozzle-scale and circular-hue helpers.

Operator modules are discovered lexically from preprocessing/operators/ and register with @register_preprocessing. Runtime execution is independently sorted by (order, fully-qualified class name). All five accept and emit srgb_f32; C1 and C2 internally visit OKLab and request F2 palette metadata.
Defaults and persisted state









































OperatorModule IDOrderPalette metadataA1 bilateral denoisea1_bilateral_denoise120noB1 print-scale bilateralb1_printscale_bilateral210noB3 TV flattenb3_tv_flatten220noC1 achievable tonemapc1_achievable_tonemap310yesC2 soft gamut compressc2_soft_gamut_compress330yes
Every class declares default_enabled=False. The current app persists choices in the Generator Workspace’s config/modules.json; a new workspace with no file falls back to those class defaults. The repository’s generator/app/modules.json is still consumed by evaluation scripts but is not the server’s live product-state path.
Parameters are persisted separately under preprocessing_params. A parameter record does not enable its operator.
A1—bilateral denoise
A1 applies one OpenCV bilateral filter globally to the solve-grid sRGB raster. Its flat-region mask is diagnostic only; it affects reported variance metrics, not where the filter runs.

























ParameterDefaultRangeradius_px31–8sigma_range0.040.005–0.25sigma_spatial2.0 px0.5–10.0 px
The kernel diameter is 2 × radius_px + 1. Its debug map is absolute luma change.
B1—print-scale bilateral
B1 anchors the spatial sigma to physical print scale:
feature_scale_mm = 2 × nozzle_diameter
sigma_spatial_mm = feature_scale_multiplier × feature_scale_mm
sigma_spatial_px = sigma_spatial_mm / solver_fine_pitch_mm
The pixel sigma is clamped to [0.5, 15], the odd kernel diameter is derived from its rounded value, and one to three bilateral passes run before a final [0,1] clip.

























ParameterDefaultRangefeature_scale_multiplier1.00.5–2.0sigma_range0.050.005–0.25passes11–3
If the fine pitch is unavailable, B1 uses 0.20 mm for this conversion.
B3—TV flatten
B3 calls scikit-image’s Chambolle total-variation denoiser. A compatibility wrapper adapts to the installed max_num_iter/n_iter_max and channel_axis/multichannel signatures.
With autoscaling enabled:
effective_weight = tv_weight × feature_scale_mm / 0.40
The effective weight is clamped to [0.005, 0.30]; the operator writes a log warning when clamping occurs and reports the final effective weight in its metrics.






























ParameterDefaultRange/choicestv_weight0.040.005–0.40weight_autoscaletruebooleanchannel_axisoklab_L_absrgb_rgb, oklab_L_ab, oklab_L_onlyn_iter_max1002–500
oklab_L_only denoises L and reattaches the original a/b channels; oklab_L_ab denoises all three OKLab channels.
n_iter_max is an iteration cap, not a requested iteration count. A low cap
can stop the Chambolle solver well before convergence; 100 remains the
recommended default. The minimum is 2 because the installed implementation
returns its input unchanged when capped at one iteration. Generator validates
known preprocessing parameters against these descriptor bounds before a solve
starts while retaining unknown module and parameter blocks for forward
compatibility.
C1—achievable tonemap
C1 maps source OKLab lightness into F2’s sampled achievable black/white interval while preserving a/b. Source shadow and highlight percentiles become the outer PCHIP anchors; the midpoint target is controlled by 0.5 ** midtone_contrast. Linear tails extend beyond the source anchors, the result is clamped to the achievable interval, and strength blends the remap with original L.






























ParameterDefaultRangestrength1.00–1shadow_percentile0.50–10highlight_percentile99.590–100midtone_contrast1.00.5–2.0
The constructor also requires shadow percentile below highlight percentile. A collapsed F2 lightness range or coincident source anchors produces an identity result; the former is marked as a degenerate palette. Debug maps include delta_L and clamp masks.
C2—soft gamut compress
C2 converts the source to OKLab, interpolates F2’s chroma ceiling around the hue circle and along lightness, and compresses chroma above knee_start_ratio × bound with the pinned tanh soft knee. It scales a and b together, so hue is preserved and L is unchanged.




















ParameterDefaultRangeknee_start_ratio0.850.50–1.00knee_softness0.500.05–1.50
Missing metadata raises ValueError. Empty, malformed, or effectively zero ceilings produce identity with a degenerate metric. Debug maps include chroma_scale and over_bound_mask.
Shared feature scale
resolve_feature_scale_mm returns a positive explicit override when supplied; otherwise it returns twice the active nozzle diameter. Missing, non-numeric, or non-positive nozzle data falls back to 0.40 mm. This is a reproducible-feature heuristic, not the printer’s minimum line width. B1 and B3 are its live operator callers.
Circular hue interpolation
interpolate_circular_degrees sorts normalized sample hues, extends the final sample by −360° and the first by +360°, then uses linear interpolation across the seam. A single sample returns a constant; empty or misaligned sample arrays raise. C2 is its live production caller.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: Preprocessing, detail cap, and luminance runtime
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
Generator has three separate boundaries that are easy to conflate:

F1 preprocessing changes the source raster before target construction;
the optional luminance handler derives source-driven boundary/detail cap guidance;
Stage 4 detail-cap smoothing cleans only the luminance detail-cap map.

They share configuration plumbing but not one enable switch.
F1 module state
Preprocessing operators are discovered from preprocessing/operators/, registered, and executed by run_preprocessing_pipeline. The live solve runs F1 after profile loading and before compute_solve_target_cloud.
All current operator class defaults are off. The server’s live toggle file is <Generator Workspace>/config/modules.json, resolved as data_paths.CONFIG_DIR / "modules.json". If it is absent, load_module_state fills every discovered module from its class default. It also drops retired keys. GET /api/modules, POST /api/modules/toggle, and PUT /api/modules/state expose and persist this state.
preprocessing_params is a separate settings dictionary keyed by module ID. It configures an enabled operator but does not enable one.
Mandatory product normalization
server._force_mandatory_product_settings is used at configuration, profile, solve, and archive boundaries. It:

removes retired quiet-drop extras;
rounds the minimum cap upward to an integral layer count;
forces model-domain ingress;
forces printability enforcement and cap-continuity cleanup;
forces printable color-region targeting and detail-cap construction;
forces the Stage 2 and Stage 4 printability override/gate flags.

detail_cap_enabled is therefore not a current product switch. API/profile/archive validation rejects a persisted false value, and normalization restores true. detail_cap_smoothing_enabled remains separately configurable, but it has an effect only when luminance handling is active.
luminance_mode normalizes to standard or luminance_detail. Applying the luminance-detail preset selects smooth_variable cap mode, enables the handler and detail residual, establishes its conservative defaults, and keeps detail-cap/printability behavior mandatory. Applying the standard preset with reset_standard=True turns the handler off. Retired cap_mode="fixed" is rejected.
Luminance-handler lifecycle
The handler defaults off in both PipelineConfig and SolveConfig. When enabled, run_pipeline configures it twice:

a provisional pre-LUT pass after target construction and white rescaling;
a final pass after target gamut mapping.

That runtime state can constrain effective_boundary_d_wc_max, giving Stage 2 and Stage 4 the same bounded boundary-cap authority.
LuminanceHandler.build_reference samples the configured appearance provider’s white-base/white-cap response, maps target lightness into layer-quantized reference caps, and may include swap-band white fill. build combines that reference with raw solver-implied cap information and returns boundary_cap_request_mm plus detail_cap_reference_mm. Detail guidance is clipped by total-height headroom and the full cap ceiling; it is guidance, not a second color-stack solve.
Provider identity is enforced. If the configuration requests photo_stack_bundle, the handler does not silently substitute the historical spline provider.
Stage 4 detail-cap smoothing
staged.stage4.build_cap_plan computes remaining cap budget from
t_max - color_ceiling, resolves boundary and detail requests, and applies cap
floors and printability gates.
_apply_stage4_detail_cap_smoothing runs only when all three are true:

luminance handling is enabled;
detail_cap_enabled is true;
detail_cap_smoothing_enabled is true.

Thus standard mode normally bypasses it even though the smoothing setting defaults true. When active, the helper converts detail height to integer layer counts, calls smooth_detail_cap_layers, converts back to millimeters, and clamps to remaining budget and any desired final-cap target.
The smoother removes exact-height speckles and cleans small components/holes in cumulative detail masks. It does not edit color maps, boundary cap, or recipe topology. Its result still passes the Stage 4 printability gates.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: Frontend architecture
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
Generator’s browser UI is a zero-build, native-ES-module application under Prisma/generator/app/. index.html remains the declarative shell and loads the import-only stylesheet manifest style.css plus one module entrypoint, bootstrap.js.
Bootstrap creates the application context, initializes the session, image, palette, settings, solve, export, and ui state slices, installs feature commands, and starts the application. It does not expose application state or compatibility functions through window.
Module boundaries

api/ owns the injectable fetch client and endpoint groups for images, palettes, settings, runs, exports, printers, and model libraries.
core/ owns the application context, state store, DOM registry, lifecycle and polling utilities, persistence wrappers, formatting, dialogs, progress, and pure theme helpers.
features/ owns behavior by workflow: shell, image, palette, settings, solve, printers, and model libraries. Event listeners, timers, abortable work, and state writes stay with the feature that owns them.
styles/ contains tokens, base/layout rules, shared components, and feature styles. style.css imports them in the established cascade order.

Cross-feature interaction goes through explicit app.commands, app.api, and named state slices rather than peer-feature imports or globals. Pollers, listeners, and lightboxes receive lifecycle owners so stale work can be disposed.
Theme and first paint
Generator supports browser-local System, Light, and Dark preferences. features/shell/theme.js owns the menu, persistence, cross-tab synchronization, and system color-scheme listener; core/theme.js contains validation and resolution logic.
A deliberately small synchronous script in the document head applies the validated preference before CSS loads. This is the sole exception to module-owned startup and prevents a light-theme flash. Theme state is UI-only and is never written into settings profiles, runs, exports, or backend configuration.
Static result lightboxes are owned by features/solve/lightbox.js. Their toolbar occupies a fixed viewer row while the image scales in the remaining stage. Highpass, Explorer, and Recipe Viewer keep their specialized controls.
For the server, jobs, and browser-to-API contract, see Driving the Generator. The Python Architecture/ pages describe backend modules only; this page is the maintained map for browser code.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: Pipeline Map
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: one webapp solve runs a fixed five-step spine (run_pipeline) with one pluggable slot (preprocessing, inside Load) plus an optional two-pass swap-banding path that fires before LUT build when the palette overflows the AMS color slots — and the heavy lifting in the Solve step is the staged Stage 0–5 backend (run_staged_backend_path).

This is the wiring diagram for one full solve. For the narrative walk-through read How a Solve Works; for the optics read The Transmission Model and The Joint LUT and Staged Solve; for the overflow two-pass read AMS grouping and swap planning. The Mermaid below renders natively in Obsidian and in a Quartz-published site, so it travels with the docs.
Page boundary: this page owns the one-run wiring diagram and nested stage order. What Actually Runs owns liveness classifications; The Solve Facade owns entry-point/config translation; The Joint LUT building and querying owns LUT construction/query implementation. Details below are included only where they explain a connection in this graph.
Two layers: the spine, and the staged backend inside the Solve step
There are two nested orchestrators, and it matters which one you are looking at:

The spine — pipeline.runner.run_pipeline. Five fixed steps: load → build LUTs → gamut → solve → stats, always in this order. When a full solve’s palette has more colors than PipelineConfig.color_slots(), _swap_banding_requested inserts a scout → band-plan → prepare expansion between Load and Build LUTs; the full story is in AMS grouping and swap planning.
The staged backend —
pipeline.staged_runner.run_staged_backend_path. This stable import is a
compatibility facade over pipeline.staged.orchestration; it is the
spine’s Solve step. Internally it runs its own Stage 0–5 sequence. Every
facade preset takes this path; solve.py supplies only focused gamut and
prediction helpers, not a competing solve engine.

    FAC --> RUN["pipeline.runner.run_pipeline<br/>FULL_PRESET"]

Fixed spine vs. the two optional expansions
The orange nodes are the only parts of the spine that vary per run: the preprocessing slot (module-toggled) and the swap-banding two-pass (fires by palette size, no toggle). Everything else is hard-wired.

Preprocessing resolution happens once, in the facade: _resolve_pipeline_slots reads saved module state and returns the preprocessing chain. There is no pluggable grouping module and no grouping_enabled preset flag anymore; swap grouping is the built-in banded two-pass, engaged by AMS overflow. See AMS grouping and swap planning.

Disambiguation (do not confuse these): the swap-banding two-pass in grouping.band_plan chooses AMS swap groups before the solve. The optional Stage 2 _seed_zone_recipe_labels_with_beam search instead seeds regional recipe labels; it is unrelated to swap banding.

The five spine steps, with their code

Inside the Solve step — the staged Stage 0–5 backend

The stage titles below are short paraphrases; the literal progress labels are “Planning solve directives…”, “Planning color regions…”, “Solving visible color stacks…”, “Planning filler support…”, “Solving white cap structure…”, and “Building solved material maps…”.

Two read-only diagnostic passes can run between Stage 4 and Stage 5 — they emit reports/counters, not geometry. Geometry attribution remains config-gated by emit_geometry_attribution. The blueprint printability diagnostic still has an emit_blueprint_printability field, but the normal web-server solve posture forces it on; it is not a user-facing optional switch. Neither report changes the already-built plan, and the old blueprint debug maps are not exposed as normal browser views.
What lands on PipelineState
After the staged result returns, _finalize_staged_backend_state copies one bundle onto the legacy-facing state exactly once:

state.staged_result = the full StagedBackendResult
state.solved_plan ← build_solved_material_plan_for_export(...) (historical function name; the resulting plan currently drives Explorer/recipe artifacts, not mesh construction)
state.thickness_maps ← float32 copies of the bundle thickness maps
state.export_maps / state.export_metadata ← the Stage 5 canonical mesh-export contract
state.diagnostics[...] ← bundle diagnostics; __de__ is recomputed here by _recompute_de_diagnostics, never read from thickness_maps

The later STL/3MF request consumes the cached thickness maps plus export_maps/export_metadata. It does not derive its geometry from state.solved_plan.
Appearance provider — the color oracle on the side
The Appearance provider is not a stage; it is built once in spine step 1 and queried by spine step 2 (LUT build) and prediction paths inside the staged solve. model_kind == "historical_spline" is Color Model v1; the live SolveConfig default is "photo_stack_bundle", which triggers the provider-LUT path and the cap range resolved by _provider_lut_d_wc_max. prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: The Joint LUT and Staged Solve
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: the transmission model only runs forward (recipe → color), so the generator inverts it by precomputing a table of achievable recipes and, for each target pixel, picking the recipe whose color is the nearest neighbor in OKLab.

This page is the conceptual bridge between the color you want and the print recipe that makes it. It deliberately stays at that altitude — how the table is built and queried lives in The Joint LUT building and querying, and how the per-pixel ideal recipes become a printable plan lives in The staged backend (Stage 0-5).
Page boundary: this page explains why the inversion is joint and how it connects to the staged solve. It is not the liveness authority or a second LUT implementation reference; use What Actually Runs for caller status and The Joint LUT building and querying for builder/query mechanics.
The inversion problem
The forward model is easy: give it a stack of filament thicknesses and it returns a color (model.compose_stack). Solving needs the reverse — given a color, find a stack — and there is no clean closed-form inverse. Too many filament/thickness combinations can land near the same color, and the achievable set is a discrete, budget-constrained lattice, not a smooth function you can analytically invert.
The generator sidesteps this entirely. It enumerates the achievable recipes once, records the color each produces, and at solve time treats inversion as a nearest-neighbor lookup: the target color goes in, the closest precomputed entry’s recipe comes out. That table is the The Joint LUT and Staged Solve.
”Joint” — cap and color together
Each entry fixes both a white-cap thickness and a color-layer recipe at once, and stores the OKLab of the full stack:
oklab( T_wb × T_wc(d_wc) × ∏ T_ci(d_ci) )

Cap and color are represented in one lookup entry rather than in two independent tables — that is what “joint” means. Two consequences follow directly from lut.LUTEntry and the LUT builders:

The white base T_wb is baked into every entry. The solve target is therefore the full-stack color, and T_wb is never divided back out at query time (model.image_to_target states this explicitly). The module-level prose near the top of lut.py still contains the contradictory historical target = T_source / T_wb description; the live builders and model-domain ingress use full-stack color.
An entry carries its color filament subset, the per-filament color thicknesses, the cap thickness, and the unscaled OKLab color — so the batch nearest-neighbor query returns complete recipes, with the cap surfaced under __white_cap__ by query_luts_batch.

Nearest neighbor in OKLab
The match runs in OKLab, a perceptually-uniform space, so “closest color” means “closest to how the eye sees it.” Each LUT subset holds a SciPy KDTree over its OKLab points; query_luts_batch queries every tree for k=1 and keeps the global best across subsets. The returned ΔE is plain Euclidean OKLab distance.
One twist worth knowing as a user: chroma weight. When chroma_weight != 1.0, the L* (lightness) axis is divided by the weight before the tree is built and before each query, so the nearest-neighbor search prioritizes the chromatic axes over exact lightness. The reported ΔE is always recomputed unweighted so quality numbers stay comparable.
The live product’s SolveConfig.de_threshold defaults to 0.01 (the lower-level PipelineConfig retains a 0.05 direct-construction default). Before Stage 2, pipeline.runner._apply_target_gamut_mapping uses the unweighted distance to the nearest raw LUT sample to identify unreachable targets and optionally remap them. Stage 2 then queries the mapped targets and records its own post-mapping __gamut_mask__; that later mask is a result diagnostic, not the input that drove gamut mapping.
From “ideal per-pixel recipe” to a printable plan
The nearest-neighbor lookup gives the ideal recipe for each pixel in isolation. A lithophane printed that literally would be unmanufacturable — single-pixel color islands, sub-nozzle features. So the webapp solve does not stop at the lookup. pipeline.staged.orchestration.run_staged_backend_path coordinates the stage-owned implementation: Stage 1 forms color regions, Stage 2 uses the per-pixel Joint-LUT results to construct and score regional candidates and apply visible-material gates, and Stage 4 plans the white cap under the active printer’s limits. pipeline.staged_runner is only the stable compatibility import through which the outer runner reaches that orchestrator.
That is the division of labour this page bridges:

























LayerJobWhere it’s documentedTransmission modelrecipe → color (forward)The Transmission ModelJoint LUTenumerate recipes + colors; nearest-neighbor invertThe Joint LUT building and queryingStaged backendper-pixel ideal → printable region/cap planThe staged backend (Stage 0-5)

Liveness note for developers. query_luts_batch is the sole LUT
recipe-query surface and is called by
staged.stage2.candidates._query_stage2_pixel_stacks plus live diagnostics.
The obsolete scalar, fixed-cap, and cap-curve query variants have been
removed. build_hull_from_luts remains live through
pipeline.runner._apply_target_gamut_mapping when hull mapping is selected.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: The Solve Facade
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: generator/facade.py is the typed handoff between server/evaluation callers and the staged pipeline: it resolves enabled preprocessing operators, translates SolveConfig into PipelineConfig, invokes run_pipeline, and converts PipelineState into the richer SolveResult returned to callers.

This page owns the facade API and translation boundary. What Actually Runs owns production liveness, Pipeline Map owns stage ordering, and The Joint LUT and Staged Solve owns numerical behavior.
Entry points























Entry pointPresetRoleCurrent statussolve_previewPREVIEW_PRESETone-palette preview/evaluation workrepository tooling and testssolve_fullFULL_PRESETproduction solvelive server and evaluation callers
Both entry points share the same translation and runner. Their presets select the candidate-height ceiling and full-only behavior.
Quality presets
QualityPreset contains only name and max_layers:




















PresetNamemax_layerspreviewpreview15fullfullautomatic (None)
The preview ceiling limits the candidate height search. The preset name also controls downstream behavior: automatic swap banding is considered only for a full solve whose palette exceeds the available color slots, and full-only palette-fit/solver-loss diagnostics are omitted from preview results.
Resolving preprocessing
_resolve_pipeline_slots returns loaded module state plus an ordered list of enabled preprocessing operator instances. It prefers explicitly supplied in-memory state, otherwise loads the configured modules.json; legacy callers with neither receive an empty list.
For every registered preprocessor it:

reads the enable flag, falling back to the class default only if the flag is absent;
constructs the operator with its named preprocessing_params block; and
sorts by numeric operator order and then fully-qualified class name for deterministic ties.

The live web app passes server._MODULES_PATH, which is <Generator Workspace>/config/modules.json. When that file is absent, pipeline.modules.load_module_state normalizes the registered class defaults; all five current preprocessors default off. Persisted user or Settings Profile choices can replace those defaults. The checked-in generator/app/modules.json is not the production state file.
Swap grouping is not a facade slot. For an overflowing full solve, pipeline.runner runs a bounded scout, chooses a consecutive band plan, attaches white-fill maps, and reruns the real solve with that plan. Preview does not initiate that two-pass banded workflow. See AMS grouping and swap planning.
SolveConfig to PipelineConfig
The 81 shared settings are declared once by config.solve_settings.SolveSettings. SolveConfig adds declarative preprocessing parameters; PipelineConfig adds the resolved operator instances, quality preset, and declared runtime carrier.
Before compilation the facade copies and normalizes the request, forcing detail_cap_enabled=True as part of the mandatory product posture without mutating the caller. PipelineConfig.from_solve_settings then copies the authoritative shared-field inventory automatically, including max_layers, and attaches the resolved preprocessing chain and preset. _to_pipeline_config remains the compatibility helper around those operations.
Two boundaries are easy to miss:

A preset is an execution ceiling. Full uses the configured or physical layer budget; preview uses the smaller of that budget and 15.
Source resampling occurs at server image ingress. The live source_resample_kernel session/profile setting is consumed by image_ingress.load_image; it is not carried through SolveConfig or PipelineConfig after the raster has been prepared.

Preprocessing parameter dictionaries likewise stop at their consumer: the facade reads SolveConfig.preprocessing_params while constructing enabled operators, and PipelineConfig receives the ordered instantiated chain rather than a second parameter copy.
SolveResult
run_pipeline returns a mutable PipelineState; _state_to_solve_result creates the facade result but does not deep-copy every payload. The current SolveResult carries:

normalized thickness maps, profiles, statistics, and the effective copied SolveConfig;
resolved_max_layers, the actual preset-aware execution budget used by default reconstruction;
the appearance-provider object and a copy of the runner’s reference image;
palette-fit and solver-loss images, maps, and RMS diagnostics for full solves;
physical image-domain dimensions;
the canonical solved material plan and staged result;
diagnostics and debug maps;
copied export maps and deep-copied export metadata;
preprocessing metrics and cap-quality data;
a deep-copied swap-grouping plan when banding was used.

The exact ThicknessMaps, solved_plan, and staged_result objects are retained. The outer diagnostics, debug-map, preprocessing-metrics, and cap-quality dictionaries are shallow-copied, so their contained arrays or nested objects remain shared. Export-map arrays and the reference image are copied; export metadata and swap grouping are deep-copied.
The live staged blueprint-printability diagnostic lives on staged_result.cap_plan.blueprint_printability_diagnostic and is summarized into staged performance/diagnostic data. Export owns a separate mesh-side quality/report contract.
Predicted views
SolveResult.predict_image() reconstructs the full backlit image from base, colors, final white cap, and — for a banded solve — the per-band white-fill maps. It uses the selected appearance provider for v2 and the fast spline composition path for v1. Its default layer count is the resolved execution budget; directly constructed compatibility results fall back to their request config.
predict_image_color_only() removes the final variable white cap before reconstruction so its luminance shaping does not obscure the color recipe view. It does not erase fixed swap-band white fill: that fill is part of the physical banded color-stack plan and remains in both provider paths.
Progress and cancellation boundary
The facade accepts a progress callback and passes it to run_pipeline. The runner emits structured stage progress.
The facade itself does not own HTTP job state. Server-side ProgressReporter cancellation checks raise at cooperative checkpoints before or during facade work.
What this layer does not own

All live entry points call pipeline.runner; its Solve step reaches the stage-owned backend through the thin pipeline.staged_runner compatibility facade. There is no alternate batch-solver entry point.
It does not persist runs, caches, exports, or profiles.
It does not choose the active published model library.
It does not decide frontend settings state; it receives a typed snapshot.
It does not resolve swap grouping as a pluggable module.

See also

How a Solve Works
Pipeline Map
The Joint LUT and Staged Solve
Settings, resolution, and the config contract

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: The pipeline orchestrator and shared state
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: pipeline/ is the small framework layer — a single orchestration function (run_pipeline) that loads profiles, runs an optional preprocessing chain, optionally scouts a swap-banding plan when the palette overflows the AMS color slots, builds LUTs, hands the heavy solve to the staged backend, and finalises one shared PipelineState carrier, with one pluggable slot (preprocessing operators) that self-registers from disk and persists its on/off state to JSON.

This is the developer companion to the generator.pipeline.runner package. It covers the data carriers, the fixed-spine design, the preprocessing plugin base class, parameter self-description, registry auto-discovery, and module on/off persistence. It also flags the revalidate() compatibility seam, which is wired but dormant in production.

What changed: the old pluggable grouping slot (GreedyGrouping / GroupBudgetGrouping, a grouping_enabled preset flag, a grouping registry) was deleted. Swap grouping is now the built-in two-pass swap-banding path in the runner, engaged purely on AMS overflow — no module, no toggle. The full story lives in AMS grouping and swap planning; this page describes only where it plugs into the spine.

Related: generation_pipeline (narrative walkthrough) · generator.facade (the entry layer above this) · generator.pipeline.staged_runner (the compatibility entry below it) · generator.pipeline.staged.orchestration (the Stage 0–5 implementation orchestrator) · The staged backend (Stage 0-5) · AMS grouping and swap planning · Module management and settings.

How to drive it (users)
You never call this package directly — you change its behavior through the Generator’s Settings drawer. The launcher prefers port 8010 but may choose another free local port. Two settings families land here:

Preprocessing operators — a chain of optional image-cleanup / gamut steps that run on the source raster before color solving. Several can be on at once. This is the only module-toggled slot.
Quality preset — preview vs full vs compare; controls how many layers. (Swap banding is not a knob — it fires automatically on FULL_PRESET when the palette overflows the AMS color slots.)

Toggling a preprocessing module in the UI writes to a JSON file (modules.json) so the choice survives a restart. The contract is enforced server-side: see Module on/off persistence below.

The shared carriers (pipeline/state.py)
Everything the pipeline produces is accumulated on one mutable object that is threaded through every stage. There are four dataclasses, all defined in pipeline/state.py.
PipelineState — the bag of solve state
pipeline.state.PipelineState is the object passed through all stages. run_pipeline constructs it once and mutates it in place. Fields, grouped by who fills them:

See AMS grouping and swap planninglutsLUT spinebanded or plain, spline or provider LUTsobserved_target_oklab, solve_target_oklabrunnertwo grids; see Observation vs solve gridthickness_maps (ThicknessMaps)staged finalisecopied from the staged compatibility bundlesolved_plan (SolvedMaterialPlan)staged finalisecanonical recipe/stack artifact used by Explorer and recipe-breakdown output; current mesh export does not consume itstaged_resultstaged finaliseraw staged-backend resultdiagnosticsrunnerthe sole canonical home for __de__ / __gamut_mask__ on this pathexport_maps, export_metadatastaged finalisecanonical white-cap field target plus physical/policy metadata required by post-solve mesh exportstats (SolveStats)_compute_statsfinal solve statisticscap_qualitystaged finalisesummary of the staged cap plansource_image, preprocessing_tracepreprocessing slotpopulated only when the chain is non-emptypreprocessing_metricsluminance runtime / compatibility callerscurrently receives luminance-handler metrics when that runtime is enabled; the preprocessing runner itself writes the trace and debug maps, not this dict
The diagnostics dict is load-bearing: on the staged/webapp path __de__ and __gamut_mask__ live in state.diagnostics, never mirrored into thickness_maps. _compute_stats reads diagnostics first and only falls back to thickness_maps for legacy/CLI-style states.
PipelineConfig — the mutable per-run carrier
The numerical and physical settings are declared once by config.solve_settings.SolveSettings. PipelineConfig inherits them as the pipeline execution wrapper; the production path builds it through facade compilation, while tests and evaluation code can still construct it directly. Its bare de_threshold=0.05 is the one intentional shared-default override for lower-level compatibility; facade compilation copies the request value instead.
Beyond the shared fields it carries:

preprocessors: List[Any] — the ordered list of enabled operator instances. Sorting happens in the facade resolver, not here.
preset: QualityPreset — defaults to FULL_PRESET.
runtime: PipelineRuntime — non-constructor luminance authority, swap-band cap, and scout flag.

Parameter dictionaries live on SolveConfig and in session/profile state. The facade consumes them while constructing the ordered operator instances; the pipeline receives those instantiated operators and does not carry a duplicate parameter dictionary.
PipelineRuntime replaces hidden attributes formerly stamped onto the config. dataclasses.replace(config) initializes a fresh runtime carrier, which keeps the bounded swap scout isolated from its parent run.
(There is no grouping field anymore — the pluggable grouping slot was removed. When swap banding fires, its plan lives on PipelineState.swap_grouping, not on the config.)
The shared effective_* methods compute the context-free arithmetic. PipelineConfig extends effective_max_layers() so the preset is a ceiling on the physical/configured budget, and extends effective_boundary_d_wc_max() with runtime luminance and swap-band limits. Palette canonicalization and the resolution backstop also live on the shared base.
ProfileSet and QualityPreset
ProfileSet is a three-field bundle of loaded filament profiles: color_profiles, wb_profile, wc_profile. QualityPreset now carries just name and max_layers — the old grouping_enabled flag was removed. Two named instances exist:

















Presetmax_layersPREVIEW_PRESET15FULL_PRESETNone (no preset-imposed ceiling; the physical/configured budget still applies)
The record itself carries only a name and layer ceiling. Downstream code also branches on the preset name: _swap_banding_requested requires name == "full" and an overflowing palette, and full-only palette-fit diagnostics use the same name. There is no separate grouping flag on the preset.

The orchestrator: fixed spine plus two slots (pipeline/runner.py)
pipeline.runner.run_pipeline is the whole orchestration. The structure is a fixed spine of always-run stages, with the preprocessing slot woven into Load and an optional swap-banding two-pass inserted before LUT build on AMS overflow. Reading the function top to bottom:



























































#StageKindStable source anchor1Load — validate palette, load profiles, create appearance provider, run the optional swap scout/band plan and preprocessing chain, then compute target cloudsspine + optional expansionsrun_pipeline; _run_swap_banding_scout; compute_solve_target_cloud—Swap-banding two-pass — scout solve → choose_band_plan → write state.swap_groupingAMS overflow only_swap_banding_requested; _swap_grouping_metadata—F1 Preprocessing — run the enabled operator chain, overwrite state.imageslotpreprocessing.runner.run_preprocessing_pipeline—Target clouds + white-point/luminance setupspine detailcompute_solve_target_cloud; _apply_target_white_rescale; configure_luminance_handler_runtime2Build LUTs — spline or provider path, plain or bandedspinelut builder functions selected by run_pipeline3Gamut — _apply_target_gamut_mapping + final luminance-authority passspine_apply_target_gamut_mapping; configure_luminance_handler_runtime4Solve — run_staged_backend_path then _finalize_staged_backend_statespinethose two named functions5Stats — _compute_statsspine_compute_stats
Two facts that the stale module header hides (trace the live symbols, not the header):

The webapp solve is the STAGED backend. The Solve stage imports run_staged_backend_path from the stable pipeline.staged_runner compatibility facade, which delegates to pipeline.staged.orchestration. It does not run solve.py’s legacy CLI engine. _finalize_staged_backend_state copies one staged result bundle’s thickness, diagnostic, debug, and export contracts onto state, derives the separate SolvedMaterialPlan, and recomputes dE straight into state.diagnostics.
The preprocessing slot and the banded two-pass are the only optional orchestration expansions. The preprocessing slot is a legal no-op when config.preprocessors is empty. The swap-banding two-pass runs only when _swap_banding_requested(config) is true; when it does, the spine’s five reported stages expand to eight (load, scout, band_plan, prepare, lut, gamut, solve, stats). There is no post-solve grouping stage. Individual stages still branch on their many solve settings and provider type.

Observation vs solve grid
The runner is the single owner of target-cloud computation through compute_solve_target_cloud. observed_target_oklab lives on the observation grid (image_sample_pitch_mm); solve_target_oklab is projected onto the solve grid (solver_fine_pitch_mm) and is what the solve path and dE recomputation both consume. _apply_target_white_rescale and _apply_target_gamut_mapping replace solve_target_oklab, so it is not necessarily the original projection array.
Progress reporting
Progress is delegated to the generator.progress module — the old facade-level _ProgressTracker class is gone. run_pipeline calls coerce_progress_reporter(progress, stage_count=…) (a plain callback, an existing ProgressReporter, or None all coerce cleanly) and then carves per-stage child reporters through its local _phase helper. Each stage’s emit(...) sends a dict with stage, stage_index, stage_count, overall_pct, elapsed_s, and palette index/count; the reporter enforces monotonic overall progress and cooperative cancellation checkpoints. No callback means no reporter and no emissions. The per-run phase_specs select five versus eight stages and tune weights for spline versus photo-stack LUT work.

The module plugin contract (pipeline/base.py)
One abstract base class defines what a pluggable module is: PreprocessingModule. (The old GroupingModule ABC was deleted along with the pluggable grouping slot.) It is an ABC with one abstract method and a describe() that serializes the module for the UI.
PreprocessingModule (F1)
pipeline.base.PreprocessingModule represents one image preprocessing operator. Class attributes the slot runner reads:

































AttributeMeaningname, descriptionidentity / UI textparams: Dict[str, ParamDef]self-described tunablesdefault_enabled: booldefault on/offinput_domain / output_domain (ColorDomain)color-domain contract; the slot runner inserts conversions between adjacent operators whose domains differorder: floatposition in the chain; active operators use the 100–199, 200–299, and 300–399 ranges; ties resolve by fully-qualified class namerequired_context: FrozenSet[ContextKey]optional shared services (e.g. palette metadata) the runner resolves before apply()
Abstract method: apply(image, *, context, progress) -> PreprocessingResult. The live operators all live under preprocessing/operators/ and self-register — a1_bilateral_denoise, b1_printscale_bilateral, b3_tv_flatten, c1_achievable_tonemap, and c2_soft_gamut_compress. See generator.preprocessing.
Swap grouping is no longer a module
There is no GroupingModule base class, no greedy_optimize/group_budget implementations, and no grouping entry in the registry. AMS swap grouping is now the built-in two-pass swap-banding path run directly by run_pipeline (scout solve → choose_band_plan from grouping/band_plan.py → state.swap_grouping), engaged purely on AMS overflow. It is not toggled and not registered. The full mechanism is documented in AMS grouping and swap planning.

Worth knowing: pipeline.__init__ re-exports ParamDef, ProgressCallback, the state classes/presets, and run_pipeline / revalidate — but not PreprocessingModule or the preprocessing registry helpers. Preprocessing operators import the registry decorator directly from pipeline.registry.

ParamDef — parameter self-description
pipeline.base.ParamDef is a dataclass that lets a module describe one tunable to both the solver and the frontend renderer in one place. Core fields: name, label, type ("int" | "float" | "bool" | "choice" | "html" | "computed_text"), default, plus choices/choice_labels/min/max/description. UI-only fields include unit, tooltip, group, show_when (conditional visibility keyed on another parameter’s value), and order. to_dict() emits the JSON the API/UI consumes, omitting None-valued optional keys. This is why the Settings drawer can render preprocessing parameter forms without hand-written controls for each operator.

Registry and auto-discovery (pipeline/registry.py)
The registry is now a single module-level dict — _PREPROCESSORS — populated by @register_preprocessing at import time. The decorator stores each class under cls.name and adds its name to PREPROCESSING_MODULE_IDS. The grouping registry was removed with the grouping slot.
Preprocessing discovery is filesystem-driven. _discover_preprocessing_operators walks preprocessing.operators with pkgutil.iter_modules and imports every public, non-package submodule in lexicographic module-name order. That makes registration/listing deterministic; execution ties are separately resolved by fully-qualified class name in the facade. An empty operators/ package is legal — the slot becomes a no-op. Discovery runs lazily: _ensure_preprocessing_populated re-discovers whenever _PREPROCESSORS is empty, and _ensure_registry_populated is its wrapper.
Public accessors all call _ensure_registry_populated first: get_preprocessing, list_preprocessings, and list_all_modules, which instantiates each class via cls.__new__ and returns its describe() dict. _clear_registry is testing-only.

Module on/off persistence (pipeline/modules.py)
pipeline/modules.py reads and writes the JSON file of {module_name: enabled} flags. This is fully live — the generator server wires every endpoint to it. It now handles preprocessing operators only.





















FunctionBehaviorload_module_state(path)read JSON, fill missing keys with defaults, normalizesave_module_state(path, state)normalize then writetoggle_module(path, id, enabled)flip one flag, validate the id against _PREPROCESSORS, normalize, persist, return full state
One normalization rule remains, since preprocessing is the only slot:

Preprocessing is non-exclusive. _normalize_module_state fills defaults for every registered operator and drops retired keys; _get_all_defaults collects each module’s default_enabled. Operators each contribute independently and several may be on at once. The zero-enabled case is a legal no-op.

The server’s module-list, toggle_module_endpoint, and bulk-save endpoints all use the configured _MODULES_PATH; solve paths snapshot load_module_state into the run record. The facade’s _load_module_state feeds _resolve_pipeline_slots, turning the flag dict into the resolved preprocessors chain for PipelineConfig.

Dormant and test-only seams
One seam in this package is wired but not exercised by the production webapp solve, confirmed by tracing its callers.
revalidate() — a test/compatibility seam with no production caller
pipeline.runner.revalidate(state) recomputes __de__ from the current thickness maps against the solve-grid target, writing straight into state.diagnostics['__de__'] and not touching thickness_maps. It is a thin wrapper over _recompute_de_diagnostics.
Liveness: run_pipeline never calls the wrapper. The production solve path calls _recompute_de_diagnostics directly during staged finalisation. With the pluggable grouping slot deleted there is no post-grouping dE branch left. The public revalidate symbol is still re-exported, but its only current callers are tests. Status: test/compatibility seam; no production caller.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: What Actually Runs
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: every product solve enters through the facade and unconditionally reaches the staged backend; image ingress and filament policy now own the shared setup helpers, while fixed-budget scheduling research remains outside the production web-app path.

This is the liveness map for Generator. Status is based on current callers rather than module names, headers, or historical design documents.

LIVE — reached during an ordinary launched Generator workflow.
LEGACY — working compatibility or CLI code, but not the web app.
DORMANT — constructable and tested or script-driven, but without a production caller.
REMNANT — a retained hook/field from a removed product feature.
SUSPECTED INERT — no production caller was found, but the area should be re-audited before deletion.

Production solve path
The product server has one live facade solve call. The other facade entry point remains useful for repository evaluation:




















Facade entryCurrent usePresetsolve_previewrepository evaluation and focused testspreviewsolve_fullbackground production solvefull
Each resolves preprocessing, translates SolveConfig to PipelineConfig, and calls pipeline.runner.run_pipeline. After load, target, appearance-model, LUT, gamut, optional band-scout, and preprocessing preparation, run_pipeline imports run_staged_backend_path through the stable pipeline.staged_runner compatibility facade. That facade delegates directly to pipeline.staged.orchestration; no alternative solve engine is selected. The staged result is finalized onto PipelineState and then converted by the facade.
Liveness table








































SubjectStatusCurrent boundarypipeline.staged_runner.run_staged_backend_pathLIVE compatibility entrystable import used by pipeline.runner; delegates without numerical workpipeline.staged.orchestration.run_staged_backend_pathLIVE implementationunconditional Stage 0–5 orchestrator reached by every facade presetimage_ingress.load_image and image_ingress.apply_adjustmentsLIVEshared source-raster preparation for server solves and palette suggestionfilament_policy.validate_paletteLIVEauthoritative profile-presence and generation-availability gate called by pipeline.runner during Loadgamut and prediction helpers in solve.pyLIVE helperstarget-gamut mapping and fast forward prediction used by the current runner/facadescheduling/ fixed-budget policiesDORMANTself-contained research package with no production importer
Live helper ownership
The retired batch CLI and six-step orchestration are no longer present. Their product-facing helpers now have explicit owners:

image_ingress.load_image and apply_adjustments prepare the product source raster;
filament_policy.validate_palette protects the solve before LUT construction and staged execution;
hue-preserving and hull gamut helpers from solve.py remain part of target preparation; and
predict_image_fast remains the v1 forward-composition helper.

solve.py is now a focused helper module rather than an alternative solver. All product solves use the staged backend.
Live printability and export validation
Every normal solve uses Stage 2/4 printability enforcement and the read-only BlueprintPrintabilityDiagnostic produced by staged_printability.run_blueprint_printability_diagnostic. The server also records the separate material-exposure audit. Mesh export calls mesh.quality.check_mesh_quality plus path-specific validation and fallback code in mesh.post_solve_export and the white-cap/color builders. Printability three layers owns those boundaries.
Dormant scheduling package
The scheduling package explores fixed-budget per-layer ordering policies. It is not automatic AMS grouping. Live grouping is the runner’s two-pass band planner under grouping/band_plan.py and grouping/banded_export.py.
Published model ingress
The live appearance providers receive explicit artifacts from the launcher-selected published library:

v1 uses the library’s validated spline profiles and optional pair corrections;
v2 receives the validated published deployment directory/runtime bundle and optional correction layer; and
the library contract also requires a valid Camera Transform deployment.

Generator does not select a “live Calibration candidate,” read Calibration’s Workspace, or use a reference bundle as a fallback. Switching complete libraries is a launcher/restart operation.
Stale headers and ports
Several module headers still use historical lith_* or lithophane_generator/* names. The server header also contains an old port example. Neither is runtime truth. The launcher binds loopback and prefers 8010, but may select any free port through 8029. Liveness and startup claims must be traced from callers and launcher code, not copied from those headers.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: AMS grouping and swap planning
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: when a full solve has more color filaments than the selected printer can hold at once, Generator scouts actual use, chooses fixed-height Z bands and filament groups, constrains the final solve to that immutable plan, adds white fill to complete every band, and later renders slot changes plus OrcaSlicer M600 pauses from the persisted plan.

Swap banding is part of the solve, not an export-time optimization. Export validates and renders the plan that the solve already committed; it must not infer new band boundaries from thickness maps.
Slot capacity
PipelineConfig starts with four AMS slots and one white slot. The effective reservation depends on the chosen white filaments:

when base white and cap white are the same, effective_white_slots() returns the configured white-slot count;
when they differ, it reserves at least two white slots; and
color_slots() is total AMS slots minus the effective white reservation.

With the default four-slot, single-white configuration, three slots remain for color. A distinct cap white normally reduces that to two.
Trigger and supported scope
_swap_banding_requested is true only when:

the facade preset is full;
the run is not itself the internal scout; and
the canonical palette contains more filaments than color_slots().

Preview solves do not enter this route. An ordinary full solve whose palette fits uses no band metadata and needs no mid-print swap.
The exhaustive planner accepts at most ten color filaments. Overflowing that limit raises before the final solve. The current banded route supports both the historical spline and Photo Stack appearance providers; other provider kinds are rejected explicitly.
Scout, plan, final solve
The live sequence in pipeline.runner.run_pipeline is:

Scout: rerun the full pipeline with PipelineRuntime.swap_banding_scout=True, using a copy of the source limited to a 384-pixel long side. This prevents recursive banding while preserving the main solve’s source raster.
Measure: collect one scout thickness map for every palette filament, substituting a zero map only if a palette id is absent from the scout result.
Plan: call choose_band_plan with the canonical palette, actual scout maps, color-slot capacity, layer height, and effective_max_layers().
Persist: serialize the selected plan into state.swap_grouping.
Constrain: build band-aware LUTs and run the final solve with the groups and band heights fixed.

effective_max_layers() reserves the minimum white cap while calculating the available color-layer budget. After planning, the runner also computes:
cap_limit_mm = t_max - d_wb - sum(band_layers) × layer_height
That runtime limit participates in the Stage 4 boundary-cap ceiling, keeping the fixed color bands and white cap within the total thickness budget.
How choose_band_plan selects groups
The planner receives the palette in canonical dark-first order and computes ceil(palette size / color slots) groups.
_canonical_partitions enumerates every unlabeled constrained partition exactly once. Filaments retain canonical order within each group, and groups are ordered by the first canonical filament assigned to them. A group is not required to be a contiguous slice of the palette; for example, nonadjacent palette entries may share a band when their measured usage makes that partition cheaper.
For each candidate:

the active mask is any pixel with nonzero total color;
each group’s required height is the 0.99 quantile of its summed scout thickness over that active mask, rounded up to whole layers and floored at one layer; and
the objective is (total raw band layers, predicted white-fill volume, canonical group key).

This prioritizes minimum print height, then minimum fill, with deterministic tie-breaking.
If the winning raw heights exceed the color-layer budget, _clamp_band_layers scales each height down with a one-layer floor. It rejects a budget too small to give every band one layer. The final solve is still authoritative: later band_fill_maps rejects any actual solved color map that exceeds its committed band height instead of silently changing the plan.
The frozen BandPlan retains the groups, selected and unclamped layer counts, usage statistics, quantile, clamp flag, and predicted fill volume.
Fixed-height white fill
Each band must end at one constant Z height so a printer can pause and change filaments across the whole object. band_fill_maps therefore calculates, at every pixel:
white fill = band height - summed color thickness in that band
Negative fill beyond tolerance is a hard error because it means the committed plan is too short for the solved color. Otherwise the fill is clamped at zero.
These per-band white maps are used by prediction/rendering, Stage 4’s band-aware cap request, recipe/Explorer material descriptions, and mesh export. They are internal white structure; they do not create an additional user-selected filament identity.
Persisted swap_grouping
_swap_grouping_metadata writes the JSON-safe swap_banding_v1 block that survives run caching and Saved Run archival. Its main fields are:





















































FieldMeaningcanonical_palettesolve-owned palette ordergroupsone filament-id list per Z bandband_layerscommitted band heights in whole layersunclamped_band_layerspre-budget diagnostic heightsband_heights_mmcommitted physical heightspause_z_mmbase top plus cumulative completed band heights, excluding the final band toplayer_height_mm, d_wb_mm, quantilereconstruction constantsscout resolution and per-group useplanning diagnosticsclamped, predicted fill volumeplan diagnosticscap_limit_mmremaining white-cap budget added after plan selectionbanding_costfinal banded-LUT dE cost relative to the scout’s unconstrained LUT
The block is copied into runtime diagnostics and run metadata. A separate swap_plan_availability record can explicitly mark instructions unavailable.
Validation at export
banded_export_plan_from_metadata converts the saved block into a frozen BandedExportPlan. It validates:

nonempty, matching groups and layer counts;
at least one layer per band;
no filament assigned to more than one band;
exact palette membership and, when declared, exact canonical-palette agreement;
layer height and base thickness agreement with the solved export settings; and
declared pause heights against the recomputed band boundaries.

A partial or contradictory plan is a hard export error. For a banded run, materializing the post-solve export bundle also recomputes and stores band-fill maps, replaces the ordinary varying color ceiling with the fixed final band ceiling, and rebases the canonical white-cap upper-surface target onto it.
Slot tables and instructions
Export finalization calls _build_swap_instruction_payload for the selected solve card. The resulting slot plan, instructions, and G-code belong to the completed export response and its published swap_instructions.txt.
Geometry and band boundaries remain solve-owned. AMS capacity is deliberately read from the currently active printer so instructions reflect the hardware the user is about to use. If the current printer has fewer color slots than any solved group requires, instruction generation returns a conflict instead of rewriting the solve.
For a banded run:

band_slot_tables assigns each band’s colors to slots 1..N;
white slots remain fixed through every transition;
generate_swap_instructions renders physical dimensions, Z ranges, every slot table, and the unload/load differences at each boundary; and
generate_orcaslicer_pause_gcode emits one M600 per persisted boundary.

The approximate displayed layer number is round(pause_z / layer_height) with a minimum of one. The actual authoritative pause is the physical pause_z_mm value.
If no band plan exists, _build_static_swap_instruction_payload validates that the solved palette still fits the current printer, produces one all-print load table, and returns ; No filament swaps needed.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: Export request lifecycle and artifact ownership
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
POST /api/export/files/start is the export entry point. It starts a process-local background job that resolves one completed solve card, materializes the canonical export bundle in the clearable run cache, builds the meshes in a private directory under Generator/Exports, optionally packages them as 3MF, writes the manifest and swap instructions, and publishes the complete directory with one rename. Browser and direct API callers use this background lifecycle.
Request and solve-card selection
ExportFilesPayload accepts:

geometry_source: field_derived (default) or exact_raster;
field_scale: 2, 4, 8, or 16 (default 4);
output_format: 3mf (default) or stls;
validate_written_meshes: false by default; and
optional card_id.

The browser always sends the selected solved run’s card_id. _resolve_export_target first looks for that card in the process’s session["solve_cache"], then accepts the current completed solve when its id matches. A card displayed from an earlier process is not enough: after Generator restarts, its arrays must be restored by loading a Saved Run or recreated by solving again.
When a direct caller omits card_id, export instead targets session["solve"] and compares its captured solve-owned fingerprint with the current config. A mismatch returns HTTP 409. Supplying card_id intentionally uses that card’s captured config and bypasses this live-current-config check; changing Settings after a solve does not rewrite the solved card the browser selected.
Invalid payload options, absent/incomplete solves, stale direct-current targets, and missing thickness maps fail before a private output stage is created.
The cache materialization boundary
_prepare_export_materialization calls prepare_export_material_maps, which now shallow-copies the material-map dictionary and ordering. The historical translucent-underfill promotion is gone. Although this helper canonicalizes a temporary config copy before reading the palette, it does not retroactively change the cached solve’s geometry; mandatory product settings were already normalized on the ordinary config/solve path.
_materialize_post_solve_export_bundle_from_cached_solve validates the current export contract and writes these files under the selected run’s clearable post_solve_export_bundle cache directory:

arrays.npz;
run_template.json;
prediction_replay_metadata.json; and
stageA_field_bundle_summary.json.

The bundle requires the total, boundary, and detail white-cap maps; the canonical white-cap field target and metadata; physical geometry metadata; ordered color maps of one common shape; and a valid persisted swap plan when the solve is banded. A missing or obsolete contract returns HTTP 409 rather than reconstructing from unrelated legacy maps.
This run-cache bundle is not a user export and is not part of the publication transaction. A failure or process kill can leave it partially rewritten. Retrying the export rewrites its named files, and the full Clear Cache action removes the enclosing cache. Already published folders under Generator/Exports are independent of it.
Background state, polling, and cancellation
The start route reserves the export job family, creates a UUID job_id, initializes session["export"], and starts a daemon thread. A second export cannot start while that state is running or cancelling.
GET /api/export/files/status returns the job id, running / cancelling / complete / cancelled / error state, structured progress, elapsed time, cancellation flag, and the completed result. The frontend polls every 500 ms, keeps cancelling active, and rejects a status stream whose job identity changes.
POST /api/export/files/cancel is job-scoped:

a mismatched supplied id returns HTTP 409;
the first accepted request changes the state to cancelling and sets cancel_requested;
repeated requests while cancelling or after terminal cancellation are idempotent; and
a request with no active export reports cancelled: false.

Cancellation is cooperative. Checks occur between export stages and throughout the current rectilinear meshing, hybrid-cap, STL, 3MF, and quarantine-coalescence loops. Responsiveness is bounded by the next checkpoint, not the click itself.
The final directory rename is the publication commit point. The implementation deliberately performs no cancellation callback after that rename. If a request arrives too late to prevent publication, the terminal state is complete and its label says that completion occurred before cancellation took effect; a complete folder is not mislabeled or deleted as cancelled.
Private output stage and publication
After validation, _perform_export_files creates a hidden direct child of Generator/Exports named .export-stage-{export_id}-{8 hex digits}. All mesh files, the manifest, optional 3MF package, and optional swap_instructions.txt are produced there. Response paths are remapped to their future published locations before the manifest is finalized.
Ordinary HTTP failures, preparation failures, cancellation, ordinary exceptions, and other Python exits all pass through best-effort removal of that stage. Cleanup failure is logged, so the guarantee is not that no hidden directory can ever remain; it is that an incomplete stage is never exposed as the final export id. Immediately before publication Generator:

performs a final cancellation check;
refuses to replace a final directory that appeared concurrently; and
renames the stage to Generator/Exports/{export_id} on the same filesystem.

The success path after the rename contains no callback, cancellation check, or logging that could turn a committed export into an apparent failure.
If the process is killed before the rename, the hidden stage can remain. On the next launcher start, after acquiring the Generator Workspace lock, reconcile_interrupted_export_stages removes only direct-child ordinary directories that match the exact private-stage grammar and contain no symlinks, junctions, or other reparse points. Unrecognized or unsafe lookalikes are preserved and reported. A kill after the rename leaves the complete published export intact. Directly starting the server without the launcher omits this startup reconciliation.
Mesh serialization and manifest ownership
export_solve_bundle owns the in-memory ExportMeshBundle, build-time quality reports, optional per-object STL serialization, and the initial export_manifest.json. It does not know about the HTTP session or final publication rename.
For output_format == "stls", it writes one file for each nonempty mesh object under stls/. Optional written-mesh validation reloads those STLs; the browser no longer exposes that switch and sends false.
For output_format == "3mf", the server does not create intermediate STLs. It may coalesce a color parent with same-material quarantine bodies for packaging, writes one {export_id}.3mf from the in-memory bundle, and updates format_packaging["3mf"] in the staged manifest. The package report explicitly says that the package mesh is not revalidated after coalescence. Package-local one-based material slots are assigned in first-seen material order and are separate from the active printer’s AMS slot table.
Swap instructions and returned artifacts
Before publication, _build_swap_instruction_payload reads the solve’s persisted swap_grouping; it never recomputes band boundaries. AMS and white-slot capacity come from the printer selected at export time. A banded plan that no longer fits returns HTTP 409. A solve that explicitly records an unavailable swap plan produces an unavailable text/G-code payload instead. A non-banded solve receives a static one-load slot table and is also rejected if it exceeds current capacity.
When available, the human instructions are written as swap_instructions.txt inside the same private stage. The response also retains the structured plan and generated M600 G-code in memory for the browser.
The completed response contains the export id and selected card id, final output path, format/geometry settings, curated file records and URLs, ZIP URL, manifest, and swap payload. GET /api/export/files-zip packages only known deliverables from the selected final directory: stls/*.stl, export_manifest.json, swap_instructions.txt, and {export_id}.3mf when present. It returns 404 rather than creating an empty folder when no deliverable exists. File serving applies both a validated export-id slug and _safe_path containment. Open Folder validates that the final directory still exists before asking the operating system’s file manager to open it.
Browser export history versus durable files
After a background job reports complete, the browser appends an export record to the originating solve card. Different format, geometry-source, and field-scale combinations remain selectable under that solve during the current session; selecting a record controls Generated Files, Swap Instructions, and Mesh Report together.
These browser records are process/page state, not a durable index of Generator/Exports. Generator does not rescan completed export directories into solve cards after a restart. The actual export folders remain ordinary user-visible files and can be opened directly from Generator/Exports; the in-app history can only describe records created in the current UI session.
Source anchors

Request and target resolution: ExportFilesPayload, _resolve_export_target, _perform_export_files in generator/server.py
Cache materialization: _materialize_post_solve_export_bundle_from_cached_solve
Polling/cancellation: export_files_start, export_files_status, export_files_cancel
Publication: _discard_export_stage, _finalize_staged_export
Startup recovery: lib/export_stage_recovery.py and launcher.py
Mesh/manifest contract: mesh/post_solve_export.py
STL/3MF writing and coalescence: mesh/export_serializers.py
Frontend history/polling: handleExportFiles, appendExportRecordToRun, and renderExportRecordSelector in generator/app/features/solve/recipe-viewer.js
