prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
From solve to mesh: the export pipeline

In one sentence: export_solve_bundle loads a canonical solved-material bundle, builds a format-neutral set of base/color/cap mesh objects with exact-raster or field-derived cap geometry, audits and reports those objects, optionally writes STLs, and returns the in-memory bundle that the server can package as 3MF before directory publication.

This page describes the geometry/manifest integration point in generator/mesh/post_solve_export.py. HTTP target selection, background polling, private output staging, swap-instruction writing, and the final directory rename belong to Export request lifecycle and artifact ownership.
The format-neutral boundary
generator.mesh.export_mesh_bundle defines two frozen dataclasses.
MeshObject
A MeshObject contains:

unique object_key;
material_key used for filament/package assignment;
semantic role;
mesh_style describing its construction;
copied float64 vertices and int64 triangle faces;
optional 4×4 transform; and
free-form metadata.

MeshObject.from_trimesh copies arrays from a trimesh.Trimesh. to_trimesh reconstructs with process=False and applies the optional transform. A border shift is represented as an object transform and is therefore baked when a serializer calls to_trimesh.
object_key is an export-object identity, not always a source thickness-map key. Unsplit color objects commonly use the filament id, but quarantine/slab/adaptive parts receive distinct suffix-bearing keys while retaining the parent’s material_key.
ExportMeshBundle
An ExportMeshBundle groups all objects with physical dimensions, layer height, XY quantum, coordinate-frame name, build report, per-object quality, color-export details, and mesh-style metadata. object_by_key performs a linear lookup.
The dataclasses are structurally frozen: code creates replacement bundles for report or border changes rather than assigning fields. This is not deep immutability; contained NumPy arrays and mapping objects remain ordinary mutable Python objects if a caller deliberately modifies them.
The shared coordinate frame is x-left-to-right_y-bottom-to-top_z-build-plate-mm.
Input bundle contract
The web server first materializes a clearable cache bundle containing:

arrays.npz;
stageA_field_bundle_summary.json;
prediction_replay_metadata.json; and
run_template.json.

export_solve_bundle accepts an arrays.npz path, its directory, or a parent that resolves to exactly one bundle. NumPy loads with allow_pickle=False. The replay names the ordered color filaments; run/summary metadata carries the physical and white-cap contracts.
Required arrays include the color map stack and canonical white-cap data. Required metadata includes solve-grid pitch, layer height, white-base thickness, explicit solve mode, and the canonical white-cap field-target policy. Border values are read through a metadata-priority chain unless the caller overrides them. When border is disabled its resolved width and height are zero.
detect_solve_mode_from_metadata searches the top-level and nested export_metadata / physical_geometry / white_cap_field_target records for luminance_mode. The current implementation maps the canonical standard string to SolveMode.STANDARD and any other present value to SolveMode.LUMINANCE; absence raises ExportPreparationError. It no longer infers mode from array keys.
The ten internal stages
DEFAULT_EXPORT_STAGES drives ExportProgressReporter:




























































#StageCurrent ownership1load_bundleResolve and load arrays plus JSON metadata.2detect_solve_modeResolve mode, physical dimensions, and border.3prepare_material_mapsUnpack the ordered color stack, validate any band plan/fill maps, and construct the base rectilinear config.4build_geometry_sourceLoad exact cap data or reconstruct the field-derived cap.5build_color_base_meshesBuild one flat base and one or more same-material objects for each nonempty color.6build_white_cap_meshesBuild exact-raster or hybrid cap objects and merge band white fill into the cap material.7validate_banded_geometryAudit a persisted banded plan; explicit no-op event for an unbanded solve.8serialize_outputsWrite STL objects when requested; 3MF remains server-owned.9validate_meshesOptionally reload written STLs; otherwise record why disabled.10write_manifestBuild and write the initial export manifest.
The separate prepare_export_material_maps module is called by the server before this function. It now only shallow-copies the map dictionary and ordering. Internal stage 3 does different work: it unpacks and validates the already materialized arrays/config.
Geometry configuration and policy
RectilinearExportConfig carries white-base thickness, actual geometry XY pitch, canonical solve-grid pitch, layer height, optional physical image dimensions, numerical/welding controls, border settings, a test/internal forced-slab switch, and a cooperative cancellation callback.
Its export_policy() creates a GeometryExportPolicy with:

canonical solve-grid pitch;
actual geometry pitch;
layer height;
white-base thickness; and
a GeometryPrintabilityPolicy whose default minimum widths/areas derive from the solve-grid pitch.

For exact raster the actual and solve pitches match. For a field-derived cap the cap geometry pitch is solve pitch / field_scale, while printability thresholds remain anchored to the solve grid. Color objects use the solve-grid config in both modes.
Shared base and color construction
_base_and_color_objects owns the common lower stack.

generate_flat_plate creates __white_base__ from Z=0 through d_wb_mm.
A floor array begins at the base top.
Each ordered non-internal color map is meshed over that floor.
The floor advances by the material thickness before the next color.

For a banded solve, fixed band-white-fill volumes are also built according to the persisted plan. They belong to the white-cap material, not to a synthetic color filament, and are merged into the cap material objects later.
Each color first attempts one rectilinear interval body. It must pass both the ordinary build-time check and a strict processed/welded check. A failing nonempty body tries a topology-risk quarantine partition. If no tested partition is ready, constant-Z slab parts are emitted instead. The fallback report and every part’s quality remain in the bundle; a failed leaf is not silently reclassified as good.
Exact-raster white cap
build_exact_raster_mesh_bundle reads the combined cap thickness on the solve grid and places it over the final color floor.
The ordinary ladder is:

one rectilinear interval body;
topology-risk quarantine parts if strict quality fails; and
recursive adaptive Z partitions if the quarantine is not ready.

force_exact_white_cap_slabs=True selects a separate constant-Z slab route directly; the web request does not expose that config switch. Adaptive terminal ranges are emitted even when a one-level leaf still fails, with failure recorded in quality/report metadata.
After the cap route, band-white-fill meshes are concatenated or represented as cap-material objects as required, then _bundle_from_objects records the bundle report and optional border wrapping runs.
Field-derived white cap
The field path calls reconstruct_field_white_cap_from_arrays with the metadata-authorized target and requested scale. The result must be a 2D integer uniform multiple of the color grid. Export derives the actual scale from the returned shape rather than trusting the request blindly.
build_field_derived_mesh_bundle_mixed_resolution then:

builds base and colors at exact solve-grid pitch;
derives the final color-top witness, including persisted band fill when present;
nearest-neighbor upsamples only that witness to field resolution; and
calls build_overlap_white_cap_mesh with matching field/hybrid policies.

The hybrid builder emits guard and freeform cap geometry while preserving coverage over the color stack. Its validation and build time are copied into mesh_build_report["overlap_white_cap"]. The field reconstruction report is stored separately under field_white_reconstruction.
Banded geometry audit
When a valid persisted plan exists, audit_banded_export_geometry compares it with the emitted color floors/ceilings, pause planes, band fill, and total non-border upper surface. Failure raises ExportPreparationError, so that staged export is not published.
For field-derived geometry, the expected cap maximum is taken from the reconstructed field actually used for meshing rather than from the coarser solve-grid cap. This keeps the band/pause checks exact without rejecting a deliberately different field-derived top surface. The audit is embedded in the build report and manifest validation; no duplicate audit JSON is written.
Format serialization boundary
With write_stls=True, export_solve_bundle calls write_export_mesh_bundle_as_stls, which skips empty objects, derives a safe filename from each object key, converts the positioned object to trimesh, and writes one file. Returned output_paths map object keys to those paths.
With write_stls=False, no mesh file is written inside this function. The web server’s 3MF branch reuses the returned in-memory bundle, optionally coalesces same-material color quarantine objects, assigns package-local material numbers/display names, and calls write_export_mesh_bundle_as_3mf. Therefore 3MF construction, its manifest amendment, swap instructions, and the final directory publication are outside the ten internal stages and outside PostSolveBundleExportResult.output_paths.
Quality and manifest semantics
check_mesh_quality records watertightness, open edges, pinch/non-two-valence edges, winding consistency, and mesh counts. Rectilinear acceptance additionally processes/welds a copy and requires that strict representation to have no non-two-valence edges.
Stage 9 is a second, optional operation only for written STLs. If validate_written_meshes is true, each STL is reloaded and recorded under reload_quality; otherwise the manifest records disabled_by_default. With no written meshes (the 3MF path), it records no_written_meshes.
build_export_manifest writes schema post-solve-export-manifest-v1. Its top-level status is ready only when every recorded object is watertight and has no open or pinch edges; otherwise it is mesh_quality_failed. The manifest still exists in the latter case and the server may publish it with the files, allowing the UI to report the failure rather than hiding it.
The manifest also contains content/export footprints, border, grid/policy, objects and any STL paths, quality, build report, bundle identity, validation, and a performance block. Those timings cover export_solve_bundle itself. They do not include later 3MF packaging, swap-instruction generation, response assembly, or the final rename; the background job’s elapsed time is the end-to-end measure for those steps.
Return value and progress boundary
PostSolveBundleExportResult returns:

the in-memory ExportMeshBundle;
initial manifest dict and path;
written STL output_paths;
internal progress events; and
optional STL reload-quality results.

ExportProgressReporter.emit checks cancellation before constructing each event, and lower mesh/serializer loops receive the same callback for finer checkpoints. The web server converts the internal stage index/fraction into its polling payload.
The server emits additional events around 3MF packaging and final publication. Current source stamps 3MF packaging as stage 7/10 even though internal serialization is stage 8/10, and stamps publication as stage 10/10; this can make the displayed percentage regress during a 3MF export. That is a frontend/backend progress-index discrepancy, not a change in geometry order. The completed state ultimately sets progress to 100%.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: Robust rectilinear meshing
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: Prisma converts grid-aligned vertical material intervals into triangle shells with sector-aware contact topology, repair and strict welded-quality checks, then partitions a failing body into same-material quarantine or Z parts while preserving any remaining failure in the export report.

This page covers the live geometry engine under generator/mesh/: the interval mesher used by every color and exact-raster cap, the field-derived overlap cap, and the export-level fallback ladder.
Production call graph
The browser’s background export reaches _perform_export_files → export_solve_bundle. Both geometry sources call _base_and_color_objects for the flat base and exact solve-grid color stack.

















Geometry sourceLive white-cap pathexact_rasterbuild_exact_raster_mesh_bundle → mesh_interval_map, with quarantine/adaptive fallbacksfield_derivedfield reconstruction → build_field_derived_mesh_bundle_mixed_resolution → build_overlap_white_cap_mesh
build_overlap_white_cap_mesh is the live field-cap builder. It constructs rigid-guard and freeform submeshes, lowers the freeform floor by one printed layer at their contact cells, concatenates them into one physical white-cap MeshObject, and reports the component and combined quality. The older build_hybrid_white_cap_meshes function still emits separate rigid/freeform objects and remains covered by tests, but the product exporter does not call it.
Some source comments still call the overlap route a prototype. Callers and tests, not that historical adjective, establish its production status.
mesh_interval_map: vertical interval to shell
mesh_interval_map(floor, thickness, pitch_mm, ...) takes two equal H×W arrays in millimetres and returns a trimesh.Trimesh plus frozen RectilinearMeshStats. Each active XY column represents the half-open vertical material interval from floor to floor + thickness.
The function accepts a cooperative cancel_check, and its expensive construction/repair loops call it at bounded checkpoints.
Snapped Z levels and slab occupancy
When z_snap_decimals is set, floor and top values are rounded through integer units and top is clamped not below floor. Export uses six decimal places. Snapping makes nominally shared material boundaries exactly equal.
All distinct active floor/top heights become one global Z-level array. Consecutive levels define slabs, and _occupancy_by_slab uses vectorized searchsorted indices to produce an H×W×K occupied-cell grid. A thickness at or below eps is inactive.
Exposed faces
_neighbor_masks shifts occupancy in six directions. A face is exposed wherever an occupied voxel-slab has an empty neighbour. _append_quads records each face by its four (row, column, z-level, local-cell) corners; each quad becomes two triangles.
The Y coordinate is inverted during world-coordinate reconstruction so the mesh uses image-up orientation. X and Y are multiples of pitch_mm; Z comes from the snapped level table.
The 2×2×2 sector rule
At one grid corner, as many as eight occupied voxel-slabs can meet. _corner_patterns packs that neighbourhood into an 8-bit occupancy code. SECTOR_LOOKUP precomputes, for all 256 codes, the six-connected components among the occupied local cells. SECTOR_COMPONENT_COUNT records how many components a pattern contains.
A face vertex is keyed by (row, column, z-level, sector), not only its geometric coordinate. Therefore two same-material regions that touch only at a point or edge receive distinct topological vertices at the same location. Without this split, an STL reader could treat the contact as one edge/point incident to too many faces and create a non-manifold pinch.
The encoded integer key incorporates grid row/column, Z-level index, and one of eight sector slots. Unique keys produce the vertex array and inverse indices produce faces. The raw trimesh is constructed with process=False, then duplicate and degenerate faces are dropped.
Optional horizontal-face merging
Export enables merge_horizontal_faces. Side walls remain cell-aligned quads, but top and bottom masks are triangulated by connected plateau rather than emitting a pair of triangles for every cell.
The merge path:

labels four-connected components at each exposed horizontal slab plane;
traces exact grid boundary rings with trace_mask_grid_rings;
groups outer rings and holes by orientation/containment;
triangulates with Shapely constrained Delaunay triangles, falling back to mapbox_earcut; and
maps every polygon vertex back to the same sector-aware integer key used by side walls.

Ring coordinates deliberately retain collinear grid vertices. Simplifying them would let a large horizontal triangle edge skip vertices used by the cell-aligned wall and could open the shell.
The unmerged route remains supported. Because it uses only sector-keyed cell quads, it skips the initial overfull-fan repair that merged triangulation may need.
Repair pipeline
After raw construction, the interval mesher performs these operations in order:

Split overfull edge fans on the merged-horizontal route. At edges used by more than two faces, _split_overfull_edge_fans separates incident connected face fans by cloning vertices.
Stitch paired duplicate open edges. _stitch_duplicate_open_edges groups geometrically identical open edges at nine decimal places and union-welds only a group containing exactly two edges.
Re-split overfull fans after stitching on the merged route.
Separate remaining coincident topological vertices. _separate_duplicate_vertices moves duplicate vertices by a tiny XY-only offset toward their incident-face centroid.
Fill residual holes, for at most two passes. Added faces receive another fan split and, when a split occurred, duplicate-vertex separation.
Fix normals when requested.

Cancellation checkpoints exist before, between, and within the large vector/group loops.
Why coincident vertices are separated
STL stores triangles, not persistent vertex identity. A slicer may weld different vertices that have identical coordinates, undoing the sector split. Export’s default split_vertex_offset_mm is 0.001 mm. The offset changes X/Y only; Z and the layer planes remain unchanged. It introduces a minute physical separation exactly at already topologically separate touch contacts so a reload cannot recreate the pinch.
The freeform-cap mesher has an equivalent contact-separation step for its own diagonal corner cases.
Quality gates
check_mesh_quality counts unique-edge face references and reports:

vertices/faces;
watertightness;
winding consistency;
open edges (one incident face); and
pinch edges (other non-two-valence edges).

_quality_passes requires watertight, zero open edges, and zero pinch edges.
Rectilinear color and cap acceptance also uses _strict_processed_quality. It rebuilds a copy with trimesh(..., process=True), intentionally allowing normal vertex welding, then requires watertightness and zero non-two/open edges. Passing the first check but failing this one means the object is clean in its identity-preserving form but likely to pinch after a slicer-style weld.
Fallbacks are attempts, not a blanket success guarantee. Any emitted part that still fails remains in the bundle’s quality map and makes the final manifest mesh_quality_failed.
Topology-risk quarantine
topology_risk_column_mask uses the same snapped interval occupancy and SECTOR_COMPONENT_COUNT table to mark XY columns adjacent to multi-sector corners. _build_interval_topology_quarantine_parts tries six deterministic subsets of those columns:

even/odd rows;
even/odd columns; and
even/odd checkerboards.

For each candidate it meshes a main body with those cells removed and a quarantine body containing only those cells. The first candidate for which all nonempty parts pass both quality gates becomes ready. If there are no risk columns, it reports no_risk_columns; if all candidates fail, it returns the final candidate and a mesh_quality_failed report so the caller can escalate.
The split preserves which interval-map cells belong to the material and both objects retain the original material key. Each part still goes through the ordinary reload-safety separation, so the same deliberate 0.001 mm XY contact gaps can appear at topologically split vertices.
Exact-raster cap fallback
The ordinary exact-cap sequence is:

one combined interval body;
topology quarantine; and
adaptive Z partition.

The internal force_exact_white_cap_slabs switch bypasses that decision and immediately emits constant-Z slabs; it defaults false and is not an HTTP export option.
Adaptive partitioning builds the whole snapped Z range first. A passing range is accepted as one part. A failing range spanning multiple level gaps is bisected recursively. A failing one-gap leaf cannot split further, so it is still emitted with role white_cap_slab_failed and included in leaf_failures. Export thereby preserves all intended geometry and makes the unresolved defect explicit rather than dropping material.
Color fallback
For each ordered color material, _base_and_color_objects tries:

one interval body;
topology quarantine; then
one constant-Z body per occupied snapped level gap.

Every slab records ordinary and strict quality. Failed slabs are still emitted and reported. The white base does not use this ladder; it is one flat box from the build plate through d_wb_mm.
Live field-derived overlap cap
derive_hybrid_white_cap_intervals divides reconstructed white material into a rigid guard domain near color and a freeform domain elsewhere. The guard sits on color and extends laterally according to the GeometryPrintabilityPolicy. validate_hybrid_white_cap_intervals checks layer occupancy for exposed color and removed reference-white coverage.
build_overlap_white_cap_mesh then:

meshes the rigid guard through mesh_interval_map;
verifies exact guard/freeform contact;
lowers the freeform floor by one layer at contact cells, refusing to cross below the white-base top;
meshes the freeform top/bottom skins and walls;
concatenates both submeshes without a boolean union; and
returns one __white_cap__ object with component and combined quality.

The deliberate same-material overlap is what lets slicers receive one cap object without requiring an expensive CAD boolean. The object’s metadata records contact count, maximum contact delta, overlap depth, each component’s quality/strict-edge summary, and the combined result.
HybridWhiteCapMeshResult.status is mesh_quality_failed for any recorded open/pinch defect, coverage_review when interval coverage did not pass, otherwise ready.
Field reconstruction upstream
reconstruct_field_white_cap_from_arrays validates the canonical target top surface against the solve-grid color ceiling, bilinearly resizes both to the selected integer field scale, and reconstructs white occupancy one printed Z layer at a time.
For each layer, _cleanup_white_mask:

fills four-connected internal air holes smaller than the policy threshold;
removes four-connected positive-white components smaller than its threshold; and
removes any white/color overlap.

Thresholds convert solve-grid-derived physical areas to fine-grid pixel counts. The result is an integer-layer thickness map plus a detailed per-layer/total audit; mesh construction happens later.
Policy and audit records
GeometryPrintabilityPolicy defaults its minimum printable width and guard width to solve-grid pitch, maximum internal empty-hole area to 0.5 × width², and minimum positive feature area to width². A finer field mesh does not relax those solve-owned physical thresholds.
RectilinearMeshStats records active columns, Z levels/slabs, quads, vertices/faces, sector splits, fan splits, stitched open edges, separated vertices, filled faces, horizontal-merge totals, topology-risk summary, snap precision, and build time. Export copies these into per-object/fallback reports, together with the rejected single-body ordinary and strict quality summaries.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: Printability three layers
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: Generator uses three live printability layers—solve-time plan enforcement, a read-only diagnostic over the finished staged blueprint, and quality checks over the meshes actually emitted for export.

“Printability” is overloaded in the codebase. The current product map is:

























Abstraction levelImplementationWhat it ownsmaterial components while plans are authoredStage 2/4 gates using pipeline.staged_printability graderssolve-time repair and enforcementmaterial components in reconstructed print layerspipeline.staged_printabilityfinal read-only BlueprintPrintabilityDiagnosticemitted triangle meshesmesh.quality, mesh.post_solve_export, and white-cap/color buildersstrict per-object edge/coverage checks, fallback selection, and export manifest results
The server’s separate MaterialExposureAudit is also live. It records color-to-air exposure from the final thickness maps and publishes white_cap_exposure_safe; it is a non-blocking audit rather than a fourth plan/mesh enforcement layer.
Level 1: staged solve enforcement
The server builds SolveConfig with product printability forced on and thresholds derived from the active printer/nozzle. Minimum width is one nozzle diameter. Minimum length is the configured whole-number multiplier—2× through 10×—times that diameter, and minimum component area is their product. The backend resolves these values authoritatively; they are not Settings Profile fields.
Stage 2 uses those physical rules while accepting, repairing, or absorbing fine color-assignment components. Stage 4 applies related rules to the structural boundary cap and optional detail cap. The boundary gate may grow coverage or suppress optional material while preserving mandatory structural floors; the detail gate may suppress unprintable optional detail. The existing graders still convert physical thresholds onto the solve grid, so component dimensions and areas remain cell-quantized.
These passes change plans while they are authored. They are therefore the product’s preventive printability layer.
Level 2: final staged diagnostic
After the plans are finished, build_layered_blueprint_view reconstructs color, boundary-cap, and detail layer masks. run_blueprint_printability_diagnostic checks connected components for physical area, width, length, structural neck loss, and vertical support. It returns BlueprintPrintabilityDiagnostic.
The result is read-only. It is stored on the Stage 4 plan, summarized into performance/run metadata, and copied into persisted debug maps. Its browser diagnostic views have been removed, so these maps are not normal user-facing Preview overlays.
See The live staged printability diagnostic for the exact thresholds and audit semantics.
Level 3: export mesh quality
Mesh export validates the objects it actually emits. The live path is distributed across mesh.quality, mesh.post_solve_export, mesh.hybrid_white_cap, and the rectilinear mesh builders.
Each mesh object receives edge-face counts and strict quality checks. Depending on the geometry path, the exporter also verifies interval reconstruction, layer coverage, guard/freeform coverage, band geometry, or other path-specific invariants. These results select ordinary, quarantine, adaptive, or slab fallbacks as described in Robust rectilinear meshing.
The resulting manifest may be ready or mesh_quality_failed. A failed-quality mesh can still be written and published with its report; the current policy does not promise that every export is watertight and does not turn every quality failure into a block.
Optional reload validation exists, but normal product export currently passes validate_written_meshes=False. For 3MF, object coalescence happens later at the server packaging boundary and the combined package mesh is not revalidated there.
The export manifest and per-mesh quality dictionaries are separate from BlueprintPrintabilityDiagnostic: the diagnostic measures staged layer occupancy, while export records facts about emitted triangles and the fallback path selected for each object.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: The live staged printability diagnostic
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: every normal Generator solve enforces physical feature rules while building its color and white-cap plans, then runs a read-only layer-by-layer diagnostic over the finished staged blueprint; a separate non-blocking audit records whether any solved color material remains exposed to air.

This page separates three related mechanisms that are easy to conflate:

Solve-time enforcement changes Stage 2 color assignment and Stage 4 white-cap/detail geometry so they satisfy mandatory printer-derived rules.
BlueprintPrintabilityDiagnostic measures the finished staged blueprint and records remaining findings. It does not change or reject that blueprint.
MaterialExposureAudit counts color-to-air faces in the final thickness maps. The live caller records its result but does not reject the solve.

Mesh-export validation is a different live system with a separate result contract; see Printability three layers.
Product configuration and liveness
For a normal web-app solve, _build_solve_config in server.py forces both product enforcement and blueprint diagnostics on. These are not user-facing switches. One backend resolver validates the selected nozzle profile and canonicalizes the resolved physical values to six decimal places. Width is exactly the nozzle diameter; line length is the nozzle diameter multiplied by the profile’s whole-number min_line_length_multiplier, which must be from 2 through 10. Component area is width × length.






























Resolved valueProduct sourceFallback in resolve_blueprint_printability_settingsminimum extrusion widthactive nozzle diameter0.40 mmminimum line lengthactive nozzle diameter × min_line_length_multipliermax(0.40 mm, width + 0.10 mm)diagnostic pitchlive runner passes solver_fine_pitch_mm explicitlyconfig solve pitch, image pitch, then 0.20 mmlayer heightsolve setting0.08 mm
The fallback column describes lower-level compatibility callers. Product web solves always carry the active printer’s resolved values, and client-submitted millimeter thresholds cannot override them at solve start. The selected printer profile lives in the runtime Workspace, not in a Settings Profile.
emit_blueprint_printability still exists in the internal config contract, so tests and non-product callers can disable the final diagnostic. The browser and server both pin it on for ordinary solves.
The diagnostic is coordinated by pipeline.staged.postsolve_diagnostics near the end of pipeline.staged.orchestration.run_staged_backend_path: after the color, filler, boundary-cap, and detail plans have been built and enforced, but before the Stage 5 compatibility bundle is emitted.
Deriving the layered blueprint
build_layered_blueprint_view reads the final VisibleRecipeRawGeometryPlan and CapSynthesisPlan and produces a read-only LayeredBlueprintView with three surface families:

Color layers are reconstructed from each VisibleRecipe in declared palette order. Positive thickness is rounded to a layer count and is never allowed to become zero layers.
Boundary-cap layers use cap_height_mm - detail_height_mm, floored at zero, and begin at the color ceiling inferred from cap_boundary_top_mm.
Detail layers begin at the boundary-cap top and use detail_height_mm.

The result is a material-label stack for color and boolean mask stacks for boundary cap and detail. It is a diagnostic reconstruction, not the mesh-export representation.
Component grading
For every material mask on every reconstructed layer, run_blueprint_printability_diagnostic labels 4-connected components and grades each component in physical units.
grade_blueprint_component calculates:

























MeasureCalculationMinimumareapixel count × pitch²extrusion width × line lengthwidthshorter bounding-box side × pitchminimum extrusion widthlengthlonger bounding-box side × pitchminimum line length
Any failed check produces a hard_fail with tiny_component, narrow_width, or short_length reason flags.
All three measurements use whole solve-grid cells. Thresholds remain physical millimeter values, but bounding boxes and pixel counts are quantized by pitch_mm; there is no fractional occupied cell in this diagnostic.
Two additional checks catch conditions a bounding box cannot describe:

A square morphological opening sized to the minimum extrusion width finds sub-width material. Exterior-corner rounding is ignored; the loss is structural only when it destroys or splits the component.
A vertical-support map checks the three preceding color layers. Any component pixel with support below one is marked low_vertical_support. The diagnostic treats the boundary cap as fully supported and detail as supported wherever any boundary-cap layer exists.

The diagnostic also records center-clearance values and clusters projected hard-fail pixels so many nearby findings can be summarized as one affected region.
Diagnostic result and product visibility
The frozen BlueprintPrintabilityDiagnostic contains:

resolved physical thresholds and layer/mask counts;
component and pixel counts by failure type and surface;
worst-surface and worst-layer summaries;
up to 128 BlueprintPrintabilityComponentFacts records; and
float maps for hard failures, narrow/short components, center clearance, structural opening loss, low support, and color/cap/detail subsets.

The runner attaches this result to CapSynthesisPlan.blueprint_printability_diagnostic. Stage 5 copies its maps into CompatibilityBundle.debug_maps, and the server persists selected counters and debug-map files with the run.
Those debug maps are not exposed as normal Preview modes. The old printability diagnostic views are explicitly removed from the browser’s accessible view set. Treat the maps as persisted diagnostic/developer artifacts, not as a current user-facing overlay workflow.
The diagnostic appends an informational or warning planning entry, but it raises no exception and gates no later stage.
Relationship to solve-time enforcement
The diagnostic runs after enforcement, but its low-level physical graders are deliberately shared with the enforcement passes:

Stage 2 uses the same component and opening-width rules while gating and repairing fine recipe assignments.
Stage 4’s boundary-cap gate may grow structural cap coverage or suppress optional cap material while preserving the mandatory floor.
Stage 4’s detail gate suppresses optional detail material that fails its physical checks.

This shared implementation keeps “what the diagnostic flags” aligned with “what enforcement tries to prevent.” The two workflows still have different ownership: enforcement mutates plans while they are being authored; the final diagnostic is read-only.
Mandatory lateral shield floor
lateral_boundary_shield_floor_layers in pipeline/material_exposure.py computes a structural white-cap minimum before Stage 4. For every horizontal or vertical neighbor pair, the lower color stack must receive enough white layers to cover the taller neighbor’s color-height excess.
The live Stage 2 path computes this floor from the selected color-layer counts and passes the resulting millimeter map into _infer_implied_cap_heights as minimum_cap_height_mm. It is therefore enforced on every normal staged solve; it is not merely a diagnostic statistic.
Material exposure audit
After the solve result has been converted to final thickness maps, the server calls _run_material_exposure_audit. The audit sums every non-special, non-excluded material map as color and resolves white cap from either the combined white-cap map or the boundary-plus-detail pair.
It quantizes both to layer counts and reports three kinds of exposed color face:





















CountMeaninglateral internal facesa color stack rises above the total color-plus-cap height of a 4-neighbortop facesa pixel contains color but has no white cap above itexterior facescolor layers touch an outer edge of the image domain
MaterialExposureAudit.passes is true only when the total exposed-face count is zero. The live server stores the summary in run metadata and exposes the convenience boolean white_cap_exposure_safe.
The live audit is record-only. A failed audit is reported in metadata and through white_cap_exposure_safe; it does not reject the solve or export.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: The white cap
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: the live staged solver chooses a layer-quantized white surface above the committed color ceiling, constrained by minimum cover, total-height and cap budgets, with Color-mode boundary policies or Luminance-mode source guidance; it exports the resulting visible upper surface as a canonical field target.

The cap is not simply “all height left over.” Its thickness is selected within the remaining budget to preserve color appearance, provide a closed white viewing skin, and optionally encode luminance/detail. The white base and cap currently use the same user-selected eligible white filament.
Color ceiling and headroom
For a live staged solve, FillerGeometryPlan.color_ceiling_mm is the per-pixel upper surface of the white base, committed color layers, and any fixed band-white-fill geometry. Stage 4 builds the cap on that surface.
pipeline.height_budget expresses the total-height contract:

max_cap_height_for_color_thickness returns t_max - d_wb - color_thickness, optionally limited by a cap maximum and floored at zero.

t_max includes base, color, and cap. The scalar helper is live in Stage 2’s per-stack cap search: over-budget cap steps are assigned infinite cost and cannot be selected. Stage 4 separately computes and enforces its per-pixel remaining budget from the final color ceiling. That Stage 4 calculation remains live and is not routed through the scalar helper.
The ordinary defaults shared by the server/UI config and PipelineConfig are 0.08 mm layer height, 0.20 mm white base, 0.16 mm minimum cap (two layers), and 3.0 mm total maximum.
Cap ceilings
PipelineConfig resolves several related values:

effective_d_wc_max() uses an explicit cap maximum when present, otherwise t_max - d_wb - d_wc_min;
effective_boundary_d_wc_max() begins from that value, then applies any runtime Luminance authority, runtime swap-band cap limit, and explicit boundary_cap_authority_mm, while never returning below d_wc_min; and
effective_white_cap() falls back to the white-base filament if a separate internal cap id is absent.

Actual per-pixel headroom still depends on the color ceiling; these scalar accessors are not permission to exceed t_max over a tall color stack.
Color mode
The UI calls the ordinary standard configuration Color mode. Its default Boundary cap is Detail Aware (cap_mode="appearance_bounded_smooth"): Stage 4 keeps a structural boundary surface close to the raw optical solution and carries the remaining desired relief in the detail cap.
boundary_cap_de_budget (UI Appearance budget, default 0.004 dE) limits the model-domain appearance change allowed when the smoothed boundary candidate departs from the raw cap. Pixels that exceed the budget fall back toward the optical cap. The alternate Smooth mode (smooth_variable) allows the whole boundary surface to vary without that structural/residual split. Retired cap_mode="fixed" is rejected by config validation.
The structural split is enabled only for Detail Aware while the Luminance handler is off. In Luminance mode the server/frontend preset forces Smooth, so the structural split cannot run accidentally.
Luminance mode and the handler
The raw PipelineConfig.luminance_handler_enabled default is false. Selecting Luminance in the UI sets luminance_mode="luminance_detail", enables the handler, selects its boundary_ceiling mode, forces Smooth boundary mode, retains mandatory detail/printability gates, and sets the other Luminance preset values. Returning to Color mode through the UI disables the handler.
The handler is configured twice in pipeline.runner:

before LUT construction, to establish a provisional runtime boundary authority; and
after gamut mapping, to rebuild that authority against the final target.

LuminanceHandler.build_reference uses the source/target OKLab L channel, samples the active white-base/white-cap appearance curve over printable layer steps, and produces layer-quantized cap guidance. It uses the configured appearance provider; a requested photo-stack provider is not silently replaced by the spline provider. For a banded solve, fixed white fill is folded into the reference so guidance describes the actual stack.
The internal handler supports several response and blend modes. The product Luminance preset uses boundary_ceiling: broad source shading constrains the boundary request while the remaining desired response can be carried by detail. Other stored modes such as boundary_prior and absolute_optical remain implementation/config surfaces, not separate user Solve Mode buttons.
Boundary authority
The handler derives a scalar optical authority from the white sandwich’s achievable OKLab swing and the configured Shading balance fraction. It can also apply boundary-percentile or explicit-authority limits. That runtime value feeds effective_boundary_d_wc_max, limiting how much height broad boundary shading can consume while leaving the full cap/detail path its own budget.
Stage 4 guidance
LuminanceHandler.build returns:

boundary_cap_request_mm, a layer-quantized boundary request limited by the boundary authority; and
detail_cap_reference_mm, a per-pixel target at least as high as the boundary request, limited by the full cap maximum and remaining t_max headroom.

When the handler is disabled, Stage 4 instead proceeds from the solver-implied cap and the selected Color-mode boundary policy.
Boundary, detail, and the final visible top
_build_stage4_cap_plan owns the live composition. It resolves the desired boundary surface, optional Detail Aware residual or optical detail candidates, printability authoring/gates, smoothing, and hard budget clamps. The resulting CapSynthesisPlan carries:

cap_boundary_top_mm;
total cap_height_mm;
detail_height_mm; and
final_visible_top_mm.

The detail stage is mandatory as a pipeline stage, but Detail depth may be zero and no optional height is forced merely because the stage exists. Both modes author candidate detail under their respective policies, and final printability gates remain mandatory.
Detail-cap smoothing
_apply_stage4_detail_cap_smoothing operates only when all three conditions hold:

the Luminance handler is enabled;
mandatory detail_cap_enabled is true; and
detail_cap_smoothing_enabled is true.

Consequently its default-true switch is a no-op in ordinary Color mode.
The helper converts detail height to whole layer counts, calls smooth_detail_cap_layers, converts back to millimetres, and clamps the result to remaining cap budget and the desired final target. The smoother replaces exact-height speckles, removes small components, and fills small holes in cumulative detail masks. It never modifies color maps or the boundary cap. The current config-derived defaults are a maximum of 1 pixel for exact-height speckles and 2 pixels for cumulative components/holes, with the layer-depth bound supplied by the active Detail depth setting.
Canonical export contract
pipeline.staged_bridge writes the live cap into three thickness-map keys:

__white_cap__ for total cap thickness;
__white_boundary_cap__; and
__white_detail_cap__.

It also exports cap_plan.final_visible_top_mm under white_cap_field_target_upper_surface_map. Metadata schema white-cap-field-target-v1 records the field key, solve/cap modes, required quantized cover floor, effective cap limits, smoothing status, and one of three policies:

standard_smooth_variable_canonical;
standard_appearance_bounded_structural_split; or
luminance_detail_canonical.

Field-derived meshing requires and reconstructs from this target. Exact raster uses total cap thickness directly but still consumes the same explicit physical/mode metadata. Export does not guess a current cap from dormant helpers.
User-facing controls
The supported UI controls are:

Solve Mode: Color or Luminance;
Max Total Thickness and Layer Height in Essentials;
Min Cap Layers;
Boundary cap: Detail Aware or Smooth (hidden/forced Smooth in Luminance);
Appearance budget for Detail Aware;
Smoothing radius;
Shading balance in Luminance; and
Detail depth.

Internal flags and ceilings described above are useful for understanding persisted configs and the solver contract, but they are not all independent controls in the current drawer.
Related

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: SolveConfig and SolveResult reference
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: facade.SolveConfig is the public solve-request dataclass, while facade.SolveResult is the compatibility-facing result that carries material maps, staged/export artifacts, diagnostics, statistics, and forward-reconstruction helpers.

config.solve_settings.SolveSettings declares the 81 settings shared by facade requests and pipeline execution. SolveConfig inherits those fields and adds only preprocessing_params, for 82 fields total. Only palette and white_base are required; all other fields have dataclass defaults. Those defaults are not always the product defaults: for example, the dataclass uses cap_mode="smooth_variable", while the server’s ordinary session default is Detail Aware ("appearance_bounded_smooth").
PipelineConfig is the sibling execution wrapper. It inherits the same settings and adds the resolved preprocessor list, quality preset, and a non-constructor runtime carrier. Its bare de_threshold=0.05 remains an intentional lower-level compatibility override; facade compilation copies the request value, normally 0.01.
The source header still calls the module lith_facade.py. The file is now facade.py, and prediction is invoked separately by server callers after a solve.
Facade entry points and liveness




















FunctionPresetCurrent statussolve_previewPREVIEW_PRESETrepository evaluation and focused-test surfacesolve_fullFULL_PRESETlive production solve path
Both functions normalize a copy of the request, resolve the preprocessing module state, compile the shared fields into PipelineConfig, and call pipeline.runner.run_pipeline. The image is a separate argument; it is not stored on SolveConfig.
There is no separate batch-solver entry point: all supported solves use the solve facade, pipeline.runner, and the stage-owned backend reached through the thin pipeline.staged_runner compatibility facade.
Construction and resolution normalization
The inherited SolveSettings.__post_init__ performs two actions:

canonicalize palette order through the active published library’s filament registry; and
invoke config.resolution_schema._apply_resolution_backstop.

The backstop treats image_sample_pitch_mm and solver_fine_pitch_mm as one coupled pair. If both are absent it assigns 0.20; if only one is present or their values disagree it raises a schema conflict. color_region_target_mm remains independent and defaults to 0.60 when absent. Retired external aliases such as pixel_size_mm, mesh_xy_pitch_mm, and color_pixel_mm are rejected earlier by the ingress schema and do not exist on either runtime dataclass.
SolveConfig field families
Defaults below are facade-dataclass defaults unless otherwise stated.
Materials and model

































FieldsContractpalette, white_base, white_cap=NoneOrdered color ids and white identities; a missing cap reuses the baseprofiles_dir=NoneDirect/developer override for historical spline profilesappearance_model_provider="photo_stack_bundle"Active forward-model lanephoto_stack_bundle_path=NoneExplicit bundle path for direct callers; the server supplies the active published library’s candidateuse_corrections=True, corrections=NoneHistorical correction toggle/payload; v2 owns its correction artifact inside the bundlemodel_domain_ingress=True, model_domain_ingress_lut_path=.../camera_transformCamera Transform source ingress; the product server forces the active library path
Physical and layer budget


















































FieldDefaultMeaninglayer_height0.08physical layer height in mmd_wb0.20fixed white-base thicknessd_wc_min0.16minimum final white-cap thickness (two default layers)d_wc_maxNoneoptional final-cap maximumboundary_cap_authority_mmNoneoptional tighter ceiling for the boundary-cap lanet_max3.0maximum total stack heightk_max3maximum distinct colors in an ordinary per-pixel stackmax_layersNoneoptional explicit color-layer limit, propagated to pipeline execution
Resolution and Stage 1 regions
The canonical pitch fields are image_sample_pitch_mm and solver_fine_pitch_mm, both 0.20. Stage 1 additionally uses stage1_coarsening_factor, lattice offsets, color_region_target_mm, color_region_target_from_printability, its width multiplier, cell_mode, smooth_boundaries, and boundary_smooth_radius.
The server forces printability-derived color-region sizing on for product solves. The user-facing Region Method selects felzenszwalb, slic, or grid; the low-level helper treats any unrecognized direct value as SLIC.
Gamut and color objective
de_threshold defaults to 0.01, chroma_weight to 1.0, and gamut_white_rescale to false.
The product server accepts:

hull: convex-hull projection; and
hue_preserving: hue-preserving chroma contraction.

pipeline.runner._apply_target_gamut_mapping accepts chroma as a compatibility alias for hue_preserving, and direct lower-level callers can disable mapping with none/off/disabled. The server normalizes chroma to hue_preserving, but rejects the three mapping-disabled values. The legacy solve.py engine’s separate chroma implementation is not the product route.
Stage 2 and printability
The stage2_* family covers zone continuity, area weighting, pressure/frontier rescue, source-edge subzones, fine overrides, seam handling, boundary mutation, and printability gating/repair. emit_pressure_diagnostics and emit_geometry_attribution gate expensive developer diagnostics.
Printability inputs include the active nozzle diameter, minimum extrusion width, minimum line length, enforce_printability, and emit_blueprint_printability. The server forces product safety settings including enforcement, fine-override gate/repair, final substrate repair, Stage 4 detail gating, and blueprint diagnostics. It does not force the optional fine-override feature or boundary mutation themselves on; those remain settings.
Stage 4 cap synthesis









































Field familyCurrent rolecap_modesmooth_variable or appearance_bounded_smooth; the server rejects retired fixedboundary_cap_de_budgetappearance budget for the Detail Aware structural splitcap_continuity_cleanuppinhole cleanup; forced true by the product serverdetail_cap_enabledmandatory true in product requests and facade translationdetail_cap_max_layersmaximum authored detail layers; zero is alloweddetail_cap_smoothing_*luminance-detail smoothing controlsluminance_handler_*optional luminance guidance, authority, response, and detail behaviorluminance_detail_authoring_printabilitypreventive detail filtering used by the product luminance preset
smooth_kernel is the live Stage 4 boundary-surface policy.
Preprocessing
preprocessing_params defaults to an empty dictionary. It stores only parameter overrides that have been supplied, keyed by preprocessing module id. The UI materializes descriptor defaults when it builds or normalizes settings; a direct facade call with a missing or empty parameter block constructs an enabled operator with that class’s constructor defaults. Module enablement lives separately in the Workspace module-state file. The facade consumes the dictionary while constructing the resolved ordered operator list; PipelineConfig receives the instantiated operators, not another parameter copy.
AMS and swap bands
ams_slots defaults to four and white_slots to one. A distinct base and cap force at least two white slots through effective_white_slots; color_slots subtracts that value from the AMS capacity without clamping.
SolveConfig contains no grouping object. For a full-preset solve whose palette exceeds the ordinary color-slot budget, the runner chooses a swap-band plan and stores it on PipelineState.swap_grouping; result conversion deep-copies that plan to SolveResult.swap_grouping.
Resampling
source_resample_kernel is a live session/profile setting, not a SolveConfig field. It defaults to lanczos; area chooses cv2.INTER_AREA. The server consumes it while preparing the source raster before the facade solve begins, so it does not need a later SolveConfig or PipelineConfig carrier.
Facade compilation
PipelineConfig.from_solve_settings copies every canonical field using the authoritative SolveSettings dataclass inventory, so adding a shared field cannot silently omit it from the handoff. This includes max_layers. The facade still applies its explicit mandatory-detail policy to a copy of the request before compilation, leaving the caller’s object untouched.
The preset is an additional execution ceiling: FULL_PRESET imposes no extra limit, while PREVIEW_PRESET limits the configured or physically derived budget to at most 15 layers. The server does not expose an ordinary max_layers setting.
Derived helpers





































MethodResulteffective_white_cap()white_cap when supplied, otherwise white_baseeffective_max_layers()explicit max_layers, otherwise int((t_max - d_wb - d_wc_min) / layer_height); the pipeline wrapper additionally applies the preset ceilingeffective_d_wc_max()explicit d_wc_max, otherwise t_max - d_wb - d_wc_mineffective_boundary_d_wc_max()shared static cap ceiling narrowed by boundary_cap_authority_mm; the pipeline wrapper additionally applies runtime luminance and swap-band limitseffective_detail_cap_max_layers()zero if detail is disabled, otherwise the nonnegative configured counteffective_white_slots()at least two when base and cap differ, otherwise white_slotscolor_slots()ams_slots - effective_white_slots()
Runtime-derived limits live in PipelineConfig.runtime, a declared PipelineRuntime value rather than hidden attributes. Swap-scout copies receive a fresh carrier, so authority calculated by one execution cannot leak into another.
SolveResult
_state_to_solve_result converts the finished PipelineState into a facade result. SolveResult.__post_init__ wraps a raw thickness-map mapping in ThicknessMaps; when the state already supplies a ThicknessMaps, the exact object is retained.
Primary fields





















































FieldContractthickness_mapsper-filament material rasters plus total/boundary/detail white-cap mapscolor_profiles, wb_profile, wc_profilehistorical spline data retained for prediction and band-fill compositionappearance_provideractive forward-model providerconfignormalized facade config actually compiled for the result; the caller’s request object is not mutatedresolved_max_layersactual execution layer budget, including the preview ceiling; optional only for directly constructed legacy/test resultsstatsSolveStats aggregate dE, gamut, coverage, size, height, and FilamentStats usagereference_imagecopy of the solve-grid image after enabled preprocessing and before target-cloud model-domain ingresssolved_planin-memory recipe/stack plan for Explorer and recipe artifacts; not current mesh inputstaged_resultcomplete Stage 0–5 lineageswap_groupingdeep-copied band plan when presentimage_domain_width_mm, image_domain_height_mmsolve-owned physical extent
Diagnostics and export fields
diagnostics is annotated as Dict[str, np.ndarray], but runtime state also stores nested metadata dictionaries such as solve identity, provider/cache information, and swap-plan diagnostics. Result conversion shallow-copies the dictionary, so contained arrays/dicts remain shared with state.
debug_maps is also shallow-copied as a dictionary; its arrays remain shared. preprocessing_metrics and cap_quality receive shallow dictionary copies. By contrast, result export_maps receive new float32 arrays, export_metadata is deep-copied, and swap_grouping is deep-copied.
The read-only blueprint printability diagnostic lives on staged_result.cap_plan and in derived debug/counter fields.
ThicknessMaps and convenience accessors
ThicknessMaps normalizes enum and string keys to the exact historical strings. Current reserved keys are:

__white_cap__
__white_boundary_cap__
__white_detail_cap__
__de__
__gamut_mask__

The live staged result keeps dE and gamut in diagnostics, not in material maps. de_map and gamut_mask prefer the diagnostics dictionary and fall back to thickness-map sentinels for diagnostics-less legacy/test objects. cap_map, boundary_cap, and detail_cap read the material container directly. filament_ids returns keys that do not begin with __.
Palette-fit diagnostics
_compute_palette_fit_diagnostics runs only for FULL_PRESET. It re-queries the LUTs for the best independently attainable recipe at each target and produces:

palette_fit_image
palette_fit_de
palette_fit_rms_de
solver_loss_map = max(final_de - best_de, 0)
solver_loss_rms_de

The best-fit rendering uses the active appearance provider and includes derived swap-band white fill when the solve is banded. The preview preset returns these fields as None.
Forward reconstruction
predict_image
predict_image(max_layers=None, *, thickness_maps=None) returns an (H, W, 3) uint8 reconstruction. An override mapping lets diagnostics reuse the exact prediction path with modified material maps.
For a historical spline result, predict_image_fast composes the base, color, final cap, and optional band-fill transmissions. For a non-spline provider, the provider predicts from thickness maps; banded v2 results additionally fold the derived fixed white fill into model-linear RGB before the common gamma-2.2 uint8 conversion.
When max_layers is omitted, this method uses resolved_max_layers populated from the finished pipeline. Directly constructed legacy/test results without that value fall back to the facade config’s effective_max_layers(). An explicit method argument remains the highest-priority override.
The live server calls this method after a full solve to create UI reconstruction artifacts. Repository evaluation and focused-test callers may also reconstruct results from solve_preview; there is no live compare-solve path. Display Camera Transform baking happens after this method; the method itself returns the model-domain encoded reconstruction.
predict_image_color_only
_cap_zeroed_thickness_maps shallow-copies the ThicknessMaps container and replaces total, boundary, and detail final-cap arrays with zeros. Color arrays remain shared. predict_image_color_only passes that override to predict_image.
The backend meaning differs slightly:

In the historical spline lane, zero thickness gives [1,1,1] transmission, so the final cap is a multiplicative identity.
In photo-stack v2, zero cap changes the evidence geometry. The vector evaluator deliberately delegates those rows to the canonical row provider; the model predicts the base-plus-color, no-final-cap stack rather than relying on a generic multiplicative-identity assumption.

For a swap-banded solve, fixed band white fill remains because it is part of the printable color-band plan and is derived from swap_grouping, not stored in the final-cap keys. “Color only” therefore means without the final luminance-shaping cap, not without mandatory band fill.
The full-solve server path saves this reconstruction for the Recipe viewer’s color-region presentation.
Stable source and test anchors

Prisma/generator/config/solve_settings.py: canonical shared fields, normalization, extraction, and pure derived helpers
Prisma/generator/facade.py: request wrapper, compilation boundary, result conversion, diagnostics, and prediction methods
Prisma/generator/pipeline/state.py: execution wrapper, presets, and declared runtime state
Prisma/generator/server.py: _build_solve_config, request normalization, mandatory product settings, cache identity, and facade callers
Prisma/generator/config/resolution_schema.py: external schema and dataclass backstop
Prisma/generator/thickness_maps.py: material-map key/container contract
Prisma/generator/appearance_model.py and photo_stack_lut.py: provider reconstruction and zero-cap behavior
focused config, facade, prediction, staged-result, and settings tests under tests/generator

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: Stage 1 and 2 solver kernels
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: pipeline/staged_solver_helpers.py contains the array-oriented segmentation, stack encoding, cap-color precomputation, and candidate-scoring helpers used by the live staged solver.

The module is a low-level toolbox, not a complete Stage 1 or Stage 2
implementation. Stage 1 plan construction lives in
pipeline/staged/stage1_zones.py. Stage 2 is divided by implementation family
under pipeline/staged/stage2/: the service composes candidate construction,
objective evaluation, optimization, pressure analysis, fine-grid refinement,
printability, and diagnostic projection. The helpers nevertheless encode real
policy: the segmentation algorithms and constants, height-budget masks, and
the candidate-score definition all live here.
Most helpers do not own workspace or job state. They are not literally side-effect-free, however: _predict_transmission_batch reaches lib.transmission._get_splines, which lazily caches built splines inside the supplied profile dictionary.
pipeline.runner always dispatches a product solve through run_staged_backend_path; the old engine in solve.py is not the web application’s backend. The helper module participates in that live path, although individual prediction helpers are model- and data-dependent.
Current helper surface























































SymbolRoleLive caller boundarygenerate_stage1_zone_labelsBuild the planning-lattice zone labelsbuild_zone_plan_smooth_label_mapOptional majority-vote boundary smoothinggenerate_stage1_zone_labels_relabel_contiguous_labelsRemap arbitrary labels to dense 0..n-1 integerssegmentation and smoothing helpers_vectorized_stack_idsEncode per-pixel color-layer stacks and recover unique recipeslive Stage 2 path_predict_transmission_batchEvaluate a historical spline profile over many thicknessesspline cap precompute and the spline luminance handler_precompute_cap_oklabsHistorical-spline cap-color gridspline Stage 2 branch, ordinary or banded_precompute_cap_oklabs_vectorizedPhoto-stack v2 cap-color scoring and dense gridsv2 Stage 2 branch, ordinary or banded_score_candidates_batchScore multiple stack candidates against a zonelocal and borrowed-neighbor candidate scoring_score_stack_for_cellMemory-bounded single-candidate scorerfallback inside _score_candidates_batch
_precompute_cap_oklabs_vectorized is explicitly imported and live even though it is accidentally absent from the module’s __all__ list. __all__ therefore must not be used as the liveness inventory.
Stage 1 zone-label generation
build_zone_plan prepares the inputs before it calls the helper. It can
downsample the runner’s prepared image and OKLab target cloud by
stage1_coarsening_factor, apply a configured lattice offset, resolve the
effective physical color-region target, and sometimes supply an explicit cell
scale. generate_stage1_zone_labels receives that planning image and returns
a same-height-and-width integer label map; it does not compute zone means,
adjacency, pixel counts, or commitment decisions.
If no explicit scale is supplied, the helper calculates:
scale = max(1, round(color_region_target_mm / solver_fine_pitch_mm))
pixels_per_cell = scale²
The live caller supplies an override when the Stage 1 planning lattice is coarsened or when the printability-derived color-region target is active. In the latter case the caller uses a ceiling rather than the helper’s round-to-nearest fallback.
The helper supports three implementation branches:





















cell_mode valueBehaviorgridDeterministic axis-aligned scale × scale tilesfelzenszwalbFelzenszwalb segmentation with scale=max(1, 0.8 × pixels_per_cell), sigma=0.8, and min_size=pixels_per_cellevery other valueSLIC with roughly one segment per 4 × pixels_per_cell pixels and compactness=10
The current settings UI supplies the intended SLIC value through that final branch, but the helper itself does not reject an unknown string; an invalid direct caller value also falls through to SLIC.
Labels are made contiguous after segmentation. When boundary smoothing is enabled, _smooth_label_map performs up to boundary_smooth_radius passes. Each pass identifies four-neighbor boundary pixels, chooses the most frequent label in the corresponding 3×3 window from a snapshot of the prior pass, and stops early if there are no boundaries. The result is relabeled contiguously again.
Stage 2 stack encoding
Stage 2 first queries query_luts_batch for a visible color recipe at every solve-grid target. _vectorized_stack_ids compresses those per-filament thickness arrays:

Iterate filaments in the supplied palette order.
Quantize each thickness with rint(thickness / layer_height).
Encode the layer counts as base-(max_layers + 1) digits in a signed 64-bit integer.
Use np.unique(..., return_inverse=True) to produce the per-pixel unique-stack id map.
Decode each unique integer into a thickness dictionary, omitting zero-layer filaments.

The Stage 2 service passes the already-canonicalized cfg.palette order in
both appearance-model lanes. That order is physically significant to
photo-stack v2. The helper returns the unique integer codes as well as the
pixel ids and decoded dictionaries, but the live service ignores the raw
codes.
The positional encoding assumes that the full code fits in int64. The product’s swap-band planner currently rejects palettes over ten colors, which keeps the normal supported route inside that bound for current layer budgets; the helper itself does not perform an overflow check.
Historical-spline cap grid
_precompute_cap_oklabs constructs cap steps from zero through cfg.effective_boundary_d_wc_max() at the configured layer height. _predict_transmission_batch evaluates the white-cap spline over those steps:

thickness at or below zero returns unit transmission;
thickness inside the measured knot range uses clipped PCHIP evaluations; and
thickness above the last knot uses the shared Beer–Lambert extrapolator.

For each unique color stack, the cap-grid helper composes the fixed white base and color layers, multiplies that transmission by every variable-cap transmission, and converts the result to OKLab.
An ordinary run computes the legal cap ceiling from the stack’s total color thickness, white-base thickness, total-height limit, and boundary-cap maximum. A banded run instead prices the band’s derived fixed white fill in the optical stack and bases cap headroom on the fixed sum of band-layer budgets. Cap rows above the applicable ceiling are set to inf, preventing the Stage 2 score minimization from selecting them.
The returned grid is both the spline scoring grid and the later dense lookup grid. Unlike the v2 branch, spline processing does not keep a separate unmasked color grid.
Photo-stack v2 cap grids
_precompute_cap_oklabs_vectorized derives a deduplicated, layer-indexed cap grid from the current LUT entries and calls photo_stack_lut.predict_unique_stack_cap_oklab_grid once for the unique Stage 2 stacks.
It returns:





















ArrayContractcap_valuescap thickness corresponding to each cap-grid columnscoring_oklabscopy of the dense predictions with cells outside the height budget set to infdense_oklabsmodel prediction for every representable stack/cap cell, including cells that Stage 2 may not select
Stage 2 candidate scoring receives the masked view. Stage 4 receives the dense view so its own cap planner can enforce cap authority without needing another prediction call. A cell remains non-finite even in the dense view if its stack cannot be represented on the evaluator’s per-filament max_layers grid; live unique stacks originate from compatible LUT recipes.
For a banded solve, the evaluator uses the fixed band-layer budgets for the height mask and folds the derived commutative white fill into each stack’s predicted transmission. For an ordinary solve, the budget uses the actual sum of color layers.
The cap grid is not reconstructed from only the LUT rows that survived color pruning. It is freshly evaluated on the LUT’s cap-step domain. This normally uses the vector evaluator, but zero-cap rows deliberately fall back to the canonical row provider because a missing cap changes the physical evidence class. The previous blanket claim that this route never invokes the row-shaped provider was therefore false.
Candidate scoring
For one proposed stack and a set of zone pixels, _score_stack_for_cell computes each pixel’s Euclidean OKLab distance at every cap step, retains the best cap distance for that pixel, and then averages those minima. It is a mean per-pixel optimal-cap distance; it does not force the entire zone to share one cap value.
_score_candidates_batch applies the same calculation to several candidates. A single-pixel fast path avoids constructing a pixel axis. Otherwise it broadcasts the full pixels × candidates × cap_steps × 3 difference tensor when that tensor contains fewer than 50 million scalar elements. At or above that threshold it loops over candidates through _score_stack_for_cell to bound peak memory.
The runner uses the scorer when a zone has multiple local candidate stacks and when it prices selected neighboring zones’ local-best stacks for augmentation. A zone with only one local candidate is assigned a local score of zero without invoking the helper.
Because the scorer minimizes over the cap axis, the inf cells in the scoring
grid act as structural exclusions. The later Stage 2 phase modules—not this
helper—own neighbor selection, beam/local optimization, fine override,
seam/printability repair, and final recipe commitment.
Live Stage 2 sequence
_query_stage2_pixel_stacks
  -> query_luts_batch
  -> thickness arrays, nearest-LUT dE, gamut mask
 
_vectorized_stack_ids
  -> per-pixel stack ids, unique stack dictionaries
 
_precompute_cap_oklabs              (historical spline)
or _precompute_cap_oklabs_vectorized (photo-stack v2)
  -> cap values, masked scoring colors, dense lookup colors
 
_enumerate_zone_candidates
  -> _score_candidates_batch for multi-candidate zones
 
_augment_zone_candidates_with_neighbor_local_bests
  -> _score_candidates_batch for borrowed candidates
 
stage2-owned recipe optimization and printability phases
The Stage 2 service records separate timings for LUT query, stack encoding,
cap-grid precompute, candidate enumeration, and neighbor augmentation under
the stage2_*_s performance keys. These are diagnostic fields, not separate
user-visible jobs or cancellation boundaries.
The implementation families are intentionally separated:









































ModuleOwnershipstaged/stage2/candidates.pyLUT query, candidate enumeration, augmentation, pruning, and rescuestaged/stage2/objective.pylocal weights and objective termsstaged/stage2/optimization.pybeam seed, coordinate descent, pair repair, and objective summarystaged/stage2/pressure.pyrecipe-pressure analysis used during the Stage 2 solvestaged/stage2/refinement.pyfine-grid assignment and boundary refinementstaged/stage2/printability.pyvisible-geometry enforcement and repairstaged/stage2/metrics.pystable Stage 2 diagnostic projectionstaged/stage2/service.pystage boundary and ordered composition
Shared geometry, cap-prediction, and physical-component primitives live in
named stage-neutral modules under pipeline/staged/. Stage 2 does not reach
into Stage 4 internals.
Secondary luminance-handler use
LuminanceHandler._sample_white_luminance_curve also calls _predict_transmission_batch when the active appearance lane is historical spline. It combines the fixed base transmission with each sampled cap transmission and converts both full white-stack and cap-only colors to OKLab. A non-spline provider instead uses provider.sample_white_cap_oklab and does not call this helper.
