prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: Staged artifacts and the SolvedMaterialPlan contract
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: the live staged backend returns its Stage 0–5 artifact lineage, then runner finalization copies Stage 5’s raster/export contracts into runtime state and separately derives a SolvedMaterialPlan used by recipe and Explorer artifacts; current mesh export consumes the raster/export bundle, not that plan.

This page describes the current ownership boundary among three result families:

























FamilyRuntime homeCurrent purposestaged plans and bookkeepingPipelineState.staged_resultcomplete internal lineage of the Stage 0–5 solvecompatibility and export mapsPipelineState.thickness_maps, diagnostics, debug_maps, export_maps, export_metadatapreview, run-cache persistence, prediction replay, and mesh-export inputcanonical recipe planPipelineState.solved_planstack/recipe identity, Explorer Rich, and recipe-breakdown artifacts
These representations are produced from the same final Stage 2–4 plans, but they are not interchangeable and do not have a general two-way synchronization mechanism.
Stage 0–5 result lineage
pipeline.staged.orchestration.run_staged_backend_path builds the following
primary artifacts. The stable pipeline.staged_runner import is a thin
compatibility facade over that implementation:








































StageArtifactSelected contents0QuantizedDirectiveSetcompiled directives, planning pitch, solve shape1LateralZonePlanzone labels, membership indices, adjacency, target statistics2VisibleRecipeRawGeometryPlanzone/fine recipe labels, recipe table, raw color ceiling, implied cap, mandatory lateral shield floor, Stage 2 diagnostics3FillerGeometryPlanraw ceiling, filler height, final color ceiling4CapSynthesisPlanboundary top, total/detail cap heights, final visible top, repair/suppression summaries, final blueprint diagnostic5CompatibilityBundlethickness, diagnostic, debug, and export maps; export metadata; label maps; physical domain size
The runner also maintains DirectiveReceiptBook, PlanningDiagnosticsStream, and StagedPerformanceProfile. Together those nine fields form StagedBackendResult.
Each stage service owns the construction of its artifact. Cross-stage
post-solve diagnostics receive completed Stage 2–4 artifacts and attach their
existing diagnostic results without calling another stage’s private
implementation. Stage 5 alone projects those artifacts into consumer-facing
compatibility maps.
The source dataclasses do not share one blanket immutability guarantee. Some leaf records are frozen, while the main plan and bundle containers are mutable dataclasses holding mutable NumPy arrays and dictionaries. “Authoritative plan” describes ownership and sequencing, not structural deep immutability.
Stage 2 recipes
VisibleRecipeRawGeometryPlan.recipe_table is a tuple of VisibleRecipe records. Each recipe contains positive (filament_id, thickness_mm) pairs. When a filament order is supplied, VisibleRecipe.from_mapping preserves that declared order and appends otherwise-unlisted ids deterministically.
recipe_label_map is a property:

it returns fine_recipe_label_map when the fine map exists;
otherwise it expands zone_recipe_labels through zone_label_map.

That final map indexes recipe_table and is the common color source for both Stage 5 thickness maps and the later SolvedMaterialPlan projection.
Do not equate VisibleRecipe with StackDefinition. VisibleRecipe is the staged, order-aware representation. StackDefinition is the canonical-plan representation and sorts its positive entries so content-equivalent stacks compare equal regardless of insertion order.
Stage 5 compatibility and export contract
build_compatibility_bundle projects the final Stage 2–4 plans into consumer-specific data:
thickness_maps

one float32 map for every palette filament;
__white_cap__ for total white-cap thickness;
__white_boundary_cap__ for boundary-cap thickness; and
__white_detail_cap__ for detail thickness.

These maps are the material input used to construct the post-solve export bundle. They also support preview rendering, exposure auditing, swap-band fill, and saved-run replay.
diagnostics and debug_maps
diagnostics currently carries the gamut mask. debug_maps contains the recipe/zone/ceiling/cap fields plus whichever optional Stage 2, Stage 4, smoothing, attribution, and blueprint-printability maps were produced.
The presence of a debug map does not imply a normal browser view. Several old diagnostic Preview modes, including the printability modes, are deliberately inaccessible in the current UI.
export_maps and export_metadata
The export map contains the canonical final white-cap upper-surface target. Export metadata records:

physical geometry settings such as pitch, layer height, base thickness, total thickness, and solve/cap modes; and
the white-cap field-target schema, policy, solve mode, effective cap limits, required cover floor, and whether detail smoothing was applied.

When the server materializes a run’s post-solve export bundle, it requires the total/boundary/detail thickness maps, the canonical field target, and matching export metadata. Missing modern fields cause a fresh-solve error rather than a guessed reconstruction. A banded run rebases the canonical target onto its fixed band ceiling and persists the band-fill maps alongside it.
Runner finalization
_finalize_staged_backend_state performs the one-time runtime handoff:

retain StagedBackendResult on state.staged_result;
derive state.solved_plan from the final recipe map/table and total cap map;
copy domain dimensions, thickness maps, diagnostics, export maps, and export metadata into state-owned containers, and merge the Stage 5 debug-map arrays into state.debug_maps;
recompute dE diagnostics; and
summarize cap quality.

Thickness, diagnostic, and export-map arrays are copied, and export metadata is deep-copied. Debug maps are the exception: state.debug_maps.update(bundle.debug_maps) retains the bundle’s array objects. Runtime debug consumers are expected to treat them as read-only, but the type and handoff do not enforce that convention.
SolvedMaterialPlan
build_solved_material_plan_for_export has a historical name. It does build SolvedMaterialPlan on every live solve, but the current STL/3MF exporter does not read it.
Fields

































FieldMeaningsegment_id_mapdense recipe-label identity map, converted to segment idssegment_stack_idcurrent stack-table assignment for each segmentstack_tablede-duplicated StackDefinition tuplecap_height_maptotal Stage 4 cap thicknessdomain/pitch fieldsphysical dimensions and solve-grid pitchcolor_region_target_mmcolor-region target recorded with the solve
For every distinct recipe label present in the final map, the bridge creates one segment and paints every pixel carrying that label with the same segment id. A “segment” here is therefore a label class, not necessarily one spatially connected component. Different recipe labels with identical color content can point to the same de-duplicated stack.
The bridge currently sets both plan pitch fields to solver_fine_pitch_mm, because it is projecting an already solved fine-grid map.
Enforced invariants
For a plan with at least one segment assignment, SolvedMaterialPlan.__post_init__ requires:

2-D segment_id_map and a same-shaped cap map;
a 1-D assignment array;
dense segment ids from zero through n_segments - 1;
valid stack-table indices; and
only StackDefinition entries in the stack table.

The constructor does not currently reject a nonempty segment_id_map paired with an empty segment_stack_id; its dense-id and assignment checks are guarded by n_segments > 0. The live staged bridge cannot produce that malformed combination because it starts from a validated, nonempty recipe map, but direct callers do not receive the blanket invariant implied by the older documentation.
It then marks segment_id_map read-only. That is the only array-level write protection imposed by this class. segment_stack_id and cap_height_map remain mutable arrays, while StackDefinition itself is frozen.
That array mutability is an implementation property and should not be mistaken for a live post-solve repair workflow.
Current consumers of the plan
The product currently uses SolvedMaterialPlan to create:

the stack-label binary and stack table used by Explorer Rich;
per-recipe footprint/cookbook artifacts; and
plan-shaped metadata while the solve remains in memory.

committed_stack_label_map(plan) performs segment_stack_id[segment_id_map] and is the live plan-to-raster helper used by those artifacts.
project_observation_to_solve_grid is also defined in pipeline.derived_views; it is live target-preparation code placed in the same module for historical reasons and does not read a plan. The separate fixed-budget scheduling.model research package also reads plans, but is not part of the product pipeline.
Export and restart boundary
Current mesh export reads the cached solve’s thickness maps plus export maps/metadata, writes a canonical post_solve_export_bundle, and then lets mesh.post_solve_export consume that bundle. It does not recover mesh geometry from SolvedMaterialPlan.
Saved-run archives persist the maps, export contract, swap metadata, and derived Explorer/recipe artifacts needed after restart. Rehydrating an archived run deliberately sets solved_plan to None; re-export and swap planning still work from the persisted raster/export contracts. A fresh in-memory solve is required for code that specifically needs the plan object.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: The Joint LUT building and querying
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: Prisma enumerates layer-quantized cap-and-color candidates under the current height rules, predicts their model-OKLab colors, prunes near-duplicates, and queries KD-trees to choose a recipe for each target pixel.

This page covers the builders, cache, query functions, and compatibility helpers in Prisma/generator/lut.py. The numerical role of the LUT in the solve is described on The Joint LUT and Staged Solve, and the photo-stack grid evaluator has its own page at The vectorized photo-stack LUT evaluator.
What “joint” means
An ordinary unbanded LUTEntry represents one nonempty subset of the active color palette. Its rows vary white-cap thickness and every color thickness in that subset together. The predicted color already includes the fixed white base:
OKLab(T_white-base × T_white-cap × T_color-1 × … × T_color-k)
For a three-color palette with k_max=3, the ordinary builders create seven subset entries: three singles, three pairs, and one triple. Each entry owns:








































FieldShape or typeMeaningfilamentstuple of IDsordered color subset represented by the row columnsthicknesses(N, k) float arraycolor thicknesses in millimetrescap_thicknesses(N,) float arrayboundary white-cap thickness in millimetresoklab(N, 3) float arrayunweighted model-OKLab predictiontreeSciPy KDTreenearest-neighbor index built in the configured matching metricchroma_weightfloatmetric scaling recorded with the entry
Banded entries add exact physical-plan fields: per-candidate color-layer counts, per-band white-fill counts, the ordered filament groups, and their fixed layer budgets. Unlike an ordinary build, a banded build returns one entry spanning the full grouped palette rather than one entry per subset.
Ordinary candidate enumeration
_enumerate_combos_budget(k, max_steps) generates every nonnegative integer tuple of length k whose sum is at most max_steps. It uses recursive stars-and-bars generation; the photo-stack evaluator contains a deliberately local copy.
For each cap step, the ordinary builders:

subtract cap thickness from the post-base height budget;
convert the remainder to a layer count, capped by max_layers;
enumerate all color-count tuples for the current subset;
convert counts to millimetres; and
predict the complete white-base, color, and cap stack.

If a lower-level caller omits t_max, the builder uses d_wc_max + max_layers × layer_height. The live runner does not rely on that fallback: it passes config.t_max - config.d_wb, because the fixed white base is already outside the LUT’s variable-height budget.
Prediction paths
The runner selects by appearance-provider kind and whether the final solve has a swap-band plan.






























Runtime situationBuilderPrediction modelHistorical spline, unbandedbuild_lutsmultiplicative spline transmission with optional v1 pair correctionsPhoto-stack v2, unbandedbuild_luts_with_providervectorized photo-stack grid evaluatorHistorical spline, bandedbuild_banded_lutsspline transmission plus exact per-band white fillPhoto-stack v2, bandedbuild_banded_luts_with_providerphoto-stack pricing plus commutative white-fill attenuation
The ordinary provider builder also contains a generic row-provider fallback. Current product model selection uses the separately handled historical spline or photo-stack bundle, so that fallback is compatibility code rather than the normal web-app route.
Historical spline and pair corrections
build_luts precomputes white-base, cap-step, and per-filament color-step transmission tables. For two-color subsets only, _build_pair_corr_cache restructures the optional fitted correction artifact by ordered (overlay, base) pair. Curves with anything other than one base are skipped; multiple curves for the same ordered pair are interpolated and averaged. If both A-on-B and B-on-A corrections exist, the builder averages their factors; otherwise it uses the available direction. Single- and three-color subsets are not corrected by this mechanism.
build_banded_luts applies the same rule only to candidates with exactly two active colors across the complete banded plan.
Photo-stack provider
For the default v2 model, build_luts_with_provider consumes photo_stack_lut.iter_photo_stack_lut_arrays. That evaluator mirrors the row provider over regular count grids and returns one raw array set per ordinary filament subset.
The live runner gives provider LUTs a cap range large enough for both the Stage-2 boundary authority and the permitted Stage-4 detail layers. _provider_lut_d_wc_max clamps boundary authority plus detail height to the effective total-cap ceiling. The historical spline route instead builds to effective_boundary_d_wc_max; its later cap work can evaluate splines directly without precomputing the extra provider grid.
The appearance-named projection seam called by the photo-stack builder is currently an exact pass-through. Camera/display appearance is applied only at the ingress and baked-view boundaries, not inside LUT pricing.
Banded enumeration
A banded final solve receives ordered, disjoint groups that exactly cover the active palette and a fixed positive layer budget for each group. _enumerate_banded_group_choices generates every allocation of zero or more color layers within a group and assigns the unused layers to white fill. It performs a first deterministic prune in linear-transmission space before _cartesian_banded_choices expands choices across all groups.
Both banded builders then:

reserve the fixed total band height before choosing cap steps;
refuse a plan that cannot fit the minimum cap;
reject projected Cartesian expansions above 50,000,000 pre-prune rows rather than silently subsampling;
predict every retained band/cap candidate;
perform the ordinary final OKLab prune; and
retain the exact color/fill geometry beside the chosen optical result for later staged-plan and export use.

The provider banded builder is intentionally restricted to photo_stack_bundle. It prices the contiguous color stack with the vectorized provider, then applies total white-fill attenuation through the cap spline. See AMS grouping and swap planning for how the groups and budgets are selected.
Deterministic near-duplicate pruning
_prune_entry_indices bins each OKLab axis at width 0.005. Inside a bin it keeps the row with:

the lowest total color thickness; then
the lowest cap thickness.

The builders therefore enumerate the budget-constrained candidate set but do not retain every enumerated stack. Pruning deliberately trades exact recipe multiplicity for a smaller search surface with a material- and cap-based deterministic representative.
Chroma-weighted indexing and honest dE
When chroma_weight > 1, builders divide the OKLab L coordinate by that value before constructing each KD-tree. This reduces lightness’s influence relative to a and b during recipe selection. The stored entry.oklab remains unscaled.
query_luts_batch applies the same L scaling to targets. After selecting winners, it recomputes the returned distance in unweighted Euclidean OKLab whenever the weight differs from one. Matching can therefore prefer chroma while the reported dE remains in the ordinary model-OKLab space.
All builders in one solve use one weight; the query functions read it from the first entry.
Live query surfaces
query_luts_batch
This is the production batch query. It scans every entry tree, retains the global winning row per target, and returns:

one (N,) float thickness array per color filament;
the reserved __white_cap__ array; and
one unweighted dE value per target.

Colors absent from a target’s winning subset remain zero. With more than one entry and more than 1,000 targets, the default parallel path queries entry trees through a ThreadPoolExecutor; reduction and result extraction remain deterministic NumPy operations. An optional callback reports each completed entry.
Live consumers include the staged Stage-2 per-pixel seed, swap-band cost diagnostics, and full-result palette-fit diagnostics.
nearest_sample_de_unweighted
The runner uses this separate batch helper to classify raw nearest-sample gamut distance independently of recipe chroma weighting. It reuses an entry’s normal tree at weight one and lazily attaches an unweighted tree when necessary.
Query-surface boundary
query_luts_batch is the sole recipe-query API. Scalar callers use a one-row target batch and select row zero. The former scalar, fixed-cap, and fixed-color wrappers were tied to retired orchestration or tests and have been removed.
Cache contract
All LUT caches live in <Generator Workspace>/cache/luts. _save_luts_to_cache writes arrays and optional metadata to compressed NPZ; KD-trees are never serialized. _load_luts_from_cache rebuilds trees using the current weight and also restores band geometry when present.






























Builder familyFilename prefixIdentity and validationordinary splinelut_spline builder version, ordered filament list, physical/search parameters, profile checksums, correction checksum, and chroma weight in the key; no metadata blockordinary providerlut_provider_provider fingerprint, builder version, ordered filaments, white identities, physical/search parameters, and chroma weight; photo-stack cache metadata is verified on loadbanded splinelut_banded_ordinary spline identity plus ordered groups/budgets; band metadata verified on loadbanded providerlut_banded_provider_provider and surrogate-profile identity plus exact groups/budgets; complete metadata verified on load
Filament order is hashed as supplied, not sorted wholesale. The server canonicalizes the product palette before building, which keeps ordinary runtime keys stable. Profile contents are hashed by sorted filament ID inside the spline key.
The generic non-photo-stack provider fallback checks for provider metadata but currently saves its rebuilt NPZ without that metadata. A subsequent load rejects that file and rebuilds it; this does not affect the current photo-stack product route.
Hull and cap-range helpers
build_hull_from_luts stacks unweighted entry.oklab, rounds to four decimals for deduplication, and constructs the SciPy convex hull used by live hull-mode gamut mapping.
derive_d_wc_max remains live for historical spline building and palette-suggestion sampling. It steps the white-cap spline until mean transmission falls below the configured threshold or the search ceiling is reached. The obsolete one-dimensional cap-curve helpers have been removed.
Stable source and test anchors

Prisma/generator/lut.py: LUTEntry, ordinary and banded builders, pruning, cache helpers, batch query, hull, and cap-range helpers
Prisma/generator/photo_stack_lut.py: iter_photo_stack_lut_arrays, predict_combo_model_linear_rgb, predict_unique_stack_cap_oklab_grid
Prisma/generator/pipeline/runner.py: _provider_lut_d_wc_max, builder dispatch, gamut mapping, band-cost diagnostics
Prisma/generator/pipeline/staged/stage2/candidates.py: Stage-2 query_luts_batch consumer

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: The solve target cloud
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: the solve target cloud is the shared lower-level conversion that takes an already prepared source raster into model-domain OKLab on the observation and solve grids; the solve runner calls it after F1 preprocessing, while palette suggestion calls it without running F1.

What it owns
pipeline.target_cloud.compute_solve_target_cloud centralizes three operations that solving and palette suggestion must interpret identically:

source sRGB to the active model’s target linear-RGB domain;
linear RGB to OKLab; and
observation-grid to solve-grid projection.

It deliberately does not load, crop, adjust, or preprocess an image. Its input is whatever raster the caller has already prepared.
The returned frozen SolveTargetCloud carries:

































FieldMeaningobserved_oklab(H*W, 3) targets on the input raster’s observation gridsolve_oklabtargets projected onto the configured solve gridobservation_shapeinput raster height and widthsolve_shapeprojected solve-grid height and widthdomainalways "model_oklab"model_domain_ingresswhether Camera Transform ingress was requested
The caller boundary
The two live direct consumers do not supply identical pixels:

pipeline.runner.run_pipeline loads profiles, resolves and executes the enabled F1 preprocessing chain, and then builds the target cloud from the resulting raster. With no enabled preprocessors, it passes the ordinary loaded/adjusted raster through unchanged.
palette.suggest.solve_target_oklab_for_signature builds the same kind of cloud for palette scoring. The server supplies a framed, resampled, ordinarily adjusted source raster capped to an 80 mm longest dimension, but it does not execute the F1 module chain.

This means the two paths share the color-domain conversion, grid projection, and optional white rescale. It does not mean an enabled noise-reduction, smoothing, tone-fit, or saturation-fit module changes automatic palette suggestions.
Repository evaluation and focused-test preview solves reach this helper indirectly through the same facade and runner as the live server’s full solve. There is no separate direct “gamut preview” caller.
Conversion steps
1. Source pixels enter the model domain
model.image_to_target performs the ingress conversion selected by model_domain_ingress:

On, as forced by the current product path: load the Camera Transform inverse LUT and apply its trilinear source-sRGB-to-model-domain mapping.
Off, for lower-level legacy callers: apply the historical gamma-2.2 srgb_to_linear conversion.

The normal runtime resolves the LUT from the active published model library’s camera_transform directory. _build_solve_config replaces stale saved/profile paths with that active-library path.
image_to_target still defaults its own ingress argument to False, but the server and typed runtime configuration explicitly use True. Its wb_profile and d_wb parameters remain for API compatibility and are unused: the modeled white sandwich is already represented in the gamut/LUT data to which the target will be compared.
2. Linear RGB becomes model OKLab
model.to_oklab converts the flattened target array with lib.transmission.linear_to_oklab. solve_target_domain always reports MODEL_OKLAB_DOMAIN, regardless of which ingress branch produced the target.
The ingress flag therefore selects a source conversion, not a second nearest-neighbor comparison domain. Solver targets and palette gamuts are both tagged as model OKLab.
3. Observation pixels project to the solve grid
pipeline.derived_views.project_observation_to_solve_grid compares image_sample_pitch_mm with solver_fine_pitch_mm:

when they agree within tolerance, it returns the original flat array object;
otherwise it reshapes the OKLab array and bilinearly resamples it with scipy.ndimage.zoom(order=1) using the physical-pitch ratio.

The helper and the separately recorded solve_shape use the same rounded dimensions. The normal Settings contract couples these two pitch fields, so ordinary browser-driven solves normally take the identity branch.
Optional paper-white rescale
apply_gamut_white_rescale_to_targets is a separate helper, not part of compute_solve_target_cloud. It returns the targets unchanged when gamut_white_rescale is off, the targets are absent, the provider is absent, or the computed paper white makes the operation a no-op.
When enabled:

solve.compute_paper_white_rgb asks the active appearance provider for the thinnest printable white-only stack: configured white base plus one minimum-cap thickness of the effective cap filament.
solve.rescale_oklab_targets converts targets back to linear RGB, multiplies each channel by that paper-white RGB, and returns to OKLab.

The runner applies this only to state.solve_target_oklab; state.observed_target_oklab remains the unrescaled observation-grid cloud. Palette suggestion applies the same helper to its solve-grid cloud before clustering.
The web-app default is gamut_white_rescale=False.
Live ownership and liveness




















ConsumerStable source anchorResultSolve runnerPrisma/generator/pipeline/runner.py: run_pipeline, _apply_target_white_rescaleowns observation- and solve-grid targets for the staged solvePalette suggestionPrisma/generator/palette/suggest.py: solve_target_oklab_for_signaturecreates the target cloud and provenance used to cluster the suggestion signature
The server’s suggestion route calls the palette helper, and its live full-solve route calls the facade, which delegates to the runner. Repository evaluation and focused-test tooling also calls the facade’s preview entry point. The compare-solve path and retired alternate batch engine are no longer present.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: The staged backend (Stage 0-5)
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: every product solve reaches one staged engine that compiles directives, builds color zones and recipes, reserves a filler seam, constructs and enforces the white cap, runs a final printability diagnostic, and emits the raster/export contracts used by the rest of Generator.

pipeline.runner.run_pipeline unconditionally calls
pipeline.staged_runner.run_staged_backend_path after it has loaded the model,
prepared targets, built LUTs, and applied gamut handling. staged_runner.py is
now a compatibility facade: the implementation lives in
pipeline.staged.orchestration. The obsolete alternate batch engine has been
removed; this is the only solve orchestration.
The stage-owned orchestrator requires a prepared PipelineState with:

state.image defining the solve-grid shape;
state.solve_target_oklab containing one target per solve-grid pixel;
loaded filament profiles and appearance provider; and
LUTs compatible with the selected palette and thickness budget.

The source files still use “experimental” language in several headers. Caller liveness, not those headers, establishes this as the production engine.
Pipeline summary





















































StagePrimary builderPrimary artifactResponsibility0compile_directivesQuantizedDirectiveSetpin the solve shape, planning pitch, and quantized cap-floor directive1build_zone_planLateralZonePlansegment the planning grid and measure zone targets/adjacency2build_visible_planVisibleRecipeRawGeometryPlanchoose and physically gate visible color recipes on the fine grid3build_filler_planFillerGeometryPlanprovide the geometry-filler seam; currently zero-height pass-through4build_cap_planCapSynthesisPlansynthesize boundary and detail cap under optical, physical, and total-height limitsdiagnosticrun_blueprint_printability_diagnosticBlueprintPrintabilityDiagnostic on Stage 4 planmeasure the finished layered blueprint without changing it5build_compatibility_bundleCompatibilityBundleemit thickness, diagnostic, debug, and canonical export fields
StagedBackendResult retains those artifacts plus directive receipts, planning diagnostics, and performance counters/timings.
The main artifacts are not uniformly frozen or deeply immutable. They are stage-owned data contracts, many containing mutable arrays and dictionaries. Later stages are expected to read the earlier completed contracts, but the Python types do not enforce that rule globally.
Implementation ownership
The Stage 0–5 sequence is intentionally visible in the short
pipeline/staged/orchestration.py module. Its dependencies point in one
direction:
staged_runner facade
  -> staged/orchestration
       -> named stage services
       -> cross-stage post-solve diagnostics
       -> Stage 5 compatibility bridge
 
stage services
  -> their stage-owned phase modules
  -> shared, stage-neutral numerical services
Stage 2 owns candidate construction, objective projection, optimization,
pressure analysis, fine-grid refinement, and visible-material printability
under staged/stage2/. Stage 4 owns cap requests, boundary shaping, detail
authoring, cap printability, and diagnostic projection under
staged/stage4/. Stage 2 and Stage 4 do not import one another. The optional
geometry-pressure attribution and final blueprint diagnostic consume multiple
completed stage artifacts, so they live in staged/postsolve_diagnostics.py
rather than being falsely assigned to either stage.
Progress adaptation and the stage-level timing/counter ledger live in
staged/telemetry.py. Stage-specific diagnostic projection lives beside its
stage in stage2/metrics.py and stage4/metrics.py. Numerical helpers retain
one implementation owner; staged_runner.py does not re-export the old
private helper surface.
Stage 0: directives
compile_directives records two image-scoped requirements:

planning-lattice pitch = solver_fine_pitch_mm × effective stage1 coarsening factor; and
visible minimum cap quantized to whole layers.

It also fixes solver_shape from state.image.shape[:2] and creates held receipt entries for both directives. The directive set is deliberately narrow; most solver settings remain on PipelineConfig rather than being duplicated here.
Stage 1: lateral color zones
Stage 1 optionally downsamples the image and target cloud by stage1_coarsening_factor, respecting the configured lattice offset. generate_stage1_zone_labels then builds the planning-grid zone labels from the effective physical color-region target and cell/boundary settings.
The effective target can be enlarged from the requested value by printer-derived minimum feature width when color_region_target_from_printability is enabled. Product solves force that policy on.
LateralZonePlan records:

planning shape, pitch, and coarse-to-fine scale;
dense zone labels and flat membership indices;
4-neighbor adjacency and shared-edge lengths; and
per-zone OKLab means, variances, and pixel counts.

Stage 2: visible recipe plan
Stage 2 is the main color assignment stage.
If Stage 1 was coarsened, its zone labels are projected back to the fine solve lattice. Optional source-edge subzones and fine overrides can further divide the effective recipe map.
The solver queries the LUTs for candidate color stacks, canonicalizes stacks using palette order, builds zone candidate frontiers, and balances local color error against shared-boundary continuity and retaining-wall penalties. Beam seeding, coordinate descent, boundary-pair repair, fine assignment, printability gating/repair, substrate absorption, and boundary mutation all contribute before the plan is finalized.
Product configuration forces the Stage 2 physical gates on. The active nozzle’s minimum line width/length and solve pitch determine the component rules.
Before returning, Stage 2:

materializes VisibleRecipe records and the final recipe label map;
computes raw color-ceiling and implied cap-height fields;
calculates the mandatory lateral white-shield floor from color-height cliffs; and
records applicable rejection, repair, mutation, guard, pressure, and objective diagnostics.

VisibleRecipe preserves declared filament order. It is not the same type as canonical-plan StackDefinition, which sorts content for equality/de-duplication.
Stage 3: filler seam
build_filler_plan is live but currently adds no geometry:

filler_height_mm is all zero; and
color_ceiling_mm equals Stage 2’s raw color ceiling.

This stage remains an explicit seam so Stage 4 and consumers use one stable color-ceiling contract. Swap-band white fill is handled separately by band-aware LUT/prediction, Stage 4, and export code; it is not written into this general filler map.
Stage 4: boundary cap and detail
Stage 4 works within the per-pixel headroom t_max - color_ceiling, the overall cap ceiling, and the possibly tighter boundary-cap ceiling.
The normal product modes are:

Detail Aware (appearance_bounded_smooth): build a minimal structural boundary cap and carry eligible residual relief in the detail cap under the appearance budget; and
Smooth (smooth_variable): allow the boundary request itself to carry the broader height variation.

Luminance mode forces the Smooth boundary policy and adds its own runtime authority limit. The retired fixed mode is rejected.
Stage 4 also:

preserves the Stage 2 lateral shield floor within available boundary budget;
applies boundary-cap physical repair while distinguishing mandatory from optional material;
authors and physically gates optional detail;
smooths detail in the Luminance path when enabled; and
clamps final boundary/detail results to remaining total-height budget.

detail_cap_enabled is mandatory in product config, but the active Detail depth may be zero and no optional detail height is guaranteed.
The result records total cap height, boundary top, detail height, final visible top, edge-guard weights, detail zones/facts, and the Stage 4 repair/suppression summaries.
Final layered diagnostic
After Stage 4 is complete, ordinary product solves reconstruct color, boundary-cap, and detail layers and run BlueprintPrintabilityDiagnostic. This uses the same component-grading concepts as the enforcement passes but is read-only: it records warnings, counters, facts, and debug maps without repairing or rejecting the result.
The diagnostic’s internal config flag can be disabled by tests/direct callers, but the browser/server force it on for normal solves. Its maps are persisted diagnostic artifacts and are not current normal Preview modes. See The live staged printability diagnostic.
Stage 5: compatibility and export fields
build_compatibility_bundle projects the final plans into:

per-palette color thickness maps;
total, boundary, and detail white-cap thickness maps;
gamut and optional debug maps;
the canonical final white-cap upper-surface target;
physical/policy metadata required to interpret that target; and
recipe/zone label maps and physical domain dimensions.

Runner finalization copies the material, diagnostic, and export arrays into state-owned containers, recomputes dE diagnostics, and summarizes cap quality. Stage 5 debug-map arrays are the exception: the runner merges their existing objects into state.debug_maps, so those views alias one another and must be treated as read-only. Finalization also separately derives SolvedMaterialPlan for Explorer/recipe artifacts.
The current STL/3MF exporter consumes the cached thickness maps plus export maps/metadata. SolvedMaterialPlan does not drive mesh construction despite the historical bridge function name. See Staged artifacts and the SolvedMaterialPlan contract.
Progress and diagnostics
Inside the staged orchestrator, progress is reported as one child solve stage
with local milestone percentages. The outer pipeline wraps that child in its
own load/LUT/gamut/solve/stats phases and, for banded solves, scout and plan
phases.
StagedPerformanceProfile records detailed substage timings and counters. PlanningDiagnosticsStream and DirectiveReceiptBook retain notable decisions and held requirements. User-facing recipe and preview artifacts are created later from the final result; they do not trigger a second solve.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: The vectorized photo-stack LUT evaluator
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: photo_stack_lut.py mirrors the photo-stack v2 equations over NumPy grids so bulk LUT, palette-gamut, cap-grid, banded-fill, and image-prediction work can reuse the calibrated model without paying the DataFrame row-provider cost for every candidate.

The canonical row-shaped implementation is PhotoStackBundleAppearanceProvider.predict_stack_model_linear_rgb_batch. It turns StackRequests into pandas rows, invokes the published bundle predictor, and optionally applies the learned correction artifact. That route remains the oracle for isolated and unsupported-grid cases.
The vectorized implementation is _PhotoStackGridEvaluator. It uses the same provider bundle, predictor object, material classifier, correction artifact, imported model constants, and low-level color/OD helpers, but reorganizes the equations around array columns. Local vector helpers handle row normalization, hue math, grouping, and broadcasting.
PHOTO_STACK_LUT_BUILDER_VERSION is part of ordinary provider cache identity. It must change when evaluator behavior changes in a way that invalidates cached colors.
Runtime shapes








































SurfaceShapeRoleRow providerarbitrary StackRequest sequence → one RGB row per requestsource-of-truth fallback and cross-check_PhotoStackGridEvaluator.predict_subsetone ordered nominal subset, many layer-count rows, indexed cap gridcore bulk evaluatoriter_photo_stack_lut_arraysall budgeted count/cap rows for each ordinary subsetunbanded v2 LUT constructionpredict_unique_stack_cap_oklab_gridevery unique solved color stack × every cap valueStage-2 candidate scoring and Stage-4 cap lookupPhotoStackPaletteGamutBackendsparse single, pair, and triple count/cap samplesautomatic palette suggestionpredict_combo_model_linear_rgbarbitrary grid-aligned color-count rowsshared solve/render/banded hot path
Precomputed model tables
The evaluator constructor validates that configured base and cap are model-white, then precomputes:

base OD at the fixed base thickness;
cap OD for every supplied cap value;
a combined base-plus-cap OD table when both whites are the same filament;
per-filament OD tables at every integer color-layer count through max_layers; and
compiled correction groups and lazy single-color profile grids.

predict_subset groups rows by an active-filament bitmask. Every row in one group therefore has the same present color IDs and takes the same distinct-color branches, while its layer counts and cap index remain vectorized.
OD composition and OKLab refinements
For nonzero-cap rows, the evaluator first builds optical density:
total_od = latent color OD
         + base/cap white OD
         + white-context OD
         + cap-attenuation OD
         + multi-color interaction OD
It clips OD to [0, 20], converts once to linear RGB with the predictor’s transmission floor, and converts that RGB to OKLab. Later refinements operate in OKLab rather than by adding OD:





























StageApplies whenordered tint retentionat least two distinct colorssingle-color cap transferexactly one distinct colorsingle-color measured-profile blendexactly one distinct colortwo-color endpoint corridorexactly two distinct colorslearned residual correctiona matching training context exists
The underlying OD terms also use the predictor’s material gates, tint-authority scales, overlayer attenuation, cap response, and interaction parameters. Three-or-more-color rows receive the general multi-color and ordered-tint behavior but not the exactly-two endpoint corridor.
Learned correction parity
_compile_correction_artifact validates the artifact’s model-white classifier and groups training rows by canonical unordered colors, canonical white pair, and evidence class. _apply_corrections builds the same scaled feature vector used by the correction layer, performs distance-cutoff Gaussian local averaging inside the matching group, and limits the residual by support, authority, and norm.
The residual can change L, a, and b. Only L is explicitly clipped to [0, 1] before conversion back to RGB.
Evidence classes are white_only, single_color_sandwich, and cross_color_multilayer_sandwich.
Model domain and the retired projection seam
predict_combo_model_linear_rgb returns model-domain linear RGB. LUT and cap-grid callers then invoke provider.project_model_linear_rgb_to_appearance before OKLab conversion, but that provider method is currently an exact array pass-through retained for compatibility. It is not an active camera conversion.
Camera Transform ingress maps source pixels into the model domain. Forward Camera Transform baking maps solved model-domain predictions to display appearance. See Model-domain ingress and display conversion.
Zero-cap and same-white correctness guards
Rows whose selected cap is zero bypass the vector equations and are sent to the canonical row provider. Zero cap changes the evidence geometry from a white sandwich to color-over-white, so delegating avoids extrapolating cap-transfer and white-context behavior across the absent-cap boundary. This route is particularly relevant to color-only reconstruction, which deliberately asks for zero variable cap.
When no color separates a same-filament white base and cap, _latent_parts samples the nonlinear white OD curve at their combined thickness rather than summing two independently sampled white curves. That mirrors the provider’s physical-layer collapse.
Dense versus budgeted cap grids
predict_unique_stack_cap_oklab_grid returns two arrays:

dense: (n_stacks, n_caps, 3) OKLab, finite for every representable stack/cap cell;
within_budget: a boolean mask marking which representable cells also fit the current height rule.

A stack is unrepresentable if any color’s layer count exceeds max_layers; those dense cells remain inf. For an ordinary solve, the budget mask compares total color layers with the height left after each cap. For a banded solve, it uses the plan’s fixed total band layers and separately folds each stack’s computed white fill into the optical prediction.
pipeline.staged_solver_helpers._precompute_cap_oklabs_vectorized keeps the dense view for Stage-4 cap lookup and creates a scoring copy with disallowed cells set to inf. Candidate scoring cannot choose an over-budget cap, while later cap planning still has model colors for every representable cell and enforces its own cap authority.
Commutative band white fill
apply_commutative_white_fill multiplies provider model-RGB rows by the historical cap spline’s transmission at the total white-fill thickness. This represents the fixed white occupying unused layers across swap bands without asking the photo-stack predictor to treat separated fill as another ordered color layer.
It is live in:

provider banded-LUT pricing;
banded cap-grid precomputation;
final dE recomputation;
palette-fit diagnostics; and
full and color-only solved-image reconstruction.

The helper validates RGB shape, scalar/per-row fill cardinality, and nonnegative thickness, and returns the original values unchanged when every fill is zero.
On-grid acceleration and fallback
PhotoStackBundleAppearanceProvider._predict_unique_combo_model_linear_rgb deduplicates image recipes before prediction. Color thicknesses that are nonnegative, within max_layers, and aligned to layer_height use predict_combo_model_linear_rgb. Off-grid or out-of-range color thicknesses fall back to row-shaped StackRequests.
Cap values are not subjected to that color-grid check: the vector evaluator builds a local cap OD table from the supplied unique cap values, so an otherwise valid row can use an arbitrary cap thickness.
Liveness

































SymbolCurrent use_PhotoStackGridEvaluatorordinary LUT construction, palette suggestion, combo prediction, cap grids, and parity testsiter_photo_stack_lut_arrayslive ordinary photo-stack LUT builderpredict_combo_model_linear_rgblive provider dedup, banded builder, cap-grid and rendering hot pathspredict_unique_stack_cap_oklab_gridlive staged cap precompute, ordinary and bandedapply_commutative_white_filllive banded pricing, diagnostics, and reconstructioncompare_vectorized_provider_predictionstest-facing parity helper; no product caller
Stable source and test anchors

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: Filesystem layout, caching, and the recipe cookbook
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: the launcher owns Generator’s portable visible folders, immutable model-library store, private Workspace, and recovery startup; cache clearing is constrained to Workspace cache, while recipe artifacts preserve the physical banded stack but classify and roll it up by colored filaments.

This page covers the ownership boundary shared by lib/runtime_layout.py, generator/data_paths.py, generator/cache_admin.py, generator/run_naming.py, and generator/recipe_cookbook.py.

Portable filesystem contract
Generator does not discover its files relative to server.py. The launcher first resolves a RuntimeLayout, prepares the folders, selects a published library, and supplies every required root through an explicit environment contract before importing the server.
Packaged launches anchor the tree beside the executable and ignore inherited developer path overrides. Source launches use the --app-root passed to Prisma.launcher and may deliberately use supported environment overrides. The application root itself must already exist; the launcher creates its owned descendants, not an arbitrary missing root.




























































Runtime constantPortable locationOwnership and lifetimeUPLOAD_DIRGenerator/Imagesuser-facing source artwork; never cleared as cacheOUTPUT_DIRGenerator/Exportsuser-facing completed exports; never cleared as cachemodel-library storeGenerator/Model Librariesinstalled immutable published bundlesMODEL_LIBRARY_DIR / DATA_DIRthe selected UUID-named library inside that storeread-only model input for the running processCONFIG_DIRGenerator/Workspace/configmutable settings and printer configurationRUN_CACHE_DIRGenerator/Workspace/cache/runssolve working directories, artifacts, and private loaded-run source snapshotsLUT_CACHE_DIRGenerator/Workspace/cache/lutsderived model/LUT cacheAUTO_RUNS_DIRGenerator/Workspace/cache/auto_runsdisposable automatic run archivesSAVED_RUNS_DIRGenerator/Workspace/saved_runsuser-curated run archives; intentionally outside cacheLOG_DIRGenerator/Workspace/logslogs; not swept by cache actions
data_paths.py requires the launcher-supplied model library, Workspace, Images, and Exports roots. Importing it without those paths raises a clear “Start it through the Prisma launcher” error instead of guessing a checkout-relative or %LOCALAPPDATA% location.
Startup and recovery
Before server import, the launcher:

creates and write-probes Generator’s visible folders and Workspace;
acquires the Workspace lock, reopening an already-running instance instead of starting a second owner;
clears every direct child under Workspace/cache except the exact real source-images directory, without following links or junctions;
removes only exact ordinary .export-stage-* directories whose trees contain no links or reparse points, preserving and reporting unrecognized/unsafe lookalikes;
removes only staging names recognized as abandoned model-library installation/state stages;
installs the bundled seed library only when no active selection exists and a seed is present; and
resolves and validates the selected library.

Startup cleanup happens only after a new process owns the Workspace lock.
Reconnecting to an already-running Prisma instance does not clear anything.
Individual transient deletion failures are retried once, reported prominently,
and retried again at the next process start rather than preventing launch.
If the active selection is absent, unreadable, incompatible, or invalid, Generator starts against Generator/Workspace/Recovery/No Active Model Library. That root exists only to let the UI and model-library manager start. Model-dependent routes remain blocked until the user installs/selects a valid library and restarts. Generator never falls back to Calibration’s live model data and never combines partial libraries.
The selection record is Generator/Workspace/active-model-library.json; it contains the selected library id for the next launch. The currently running process keeps its original active library. Activating another library validates and records the choice, then requires a launcher-managed restart. The store will not remove either the library in use by the process or the library selected for the next launch.
An installed directory name must be the same canonical lower-case UUID as the manifest’s library_id. Manually copying a valid library under a different folder name therefore produces an invalid store entry; installing the ZIP through the manager stages, validates, and names it correctly.

Export publication boundary
Completed export directories appear directly under Generator/Exports. Export first writes to a hidden sibling .export-stage-* directory, updates every deliverable and manifest there, and publishes it with a same-filesystem rename only after preparation succeeds. Ordinary failure or cooperative cancellation attempts to remove the stage; cleanup failure is logged without exposing the directory under a final export id. A process kill may prevent cleanup, so the next launcher run performs the same conservative stage reconciliation after it owns the Workspace lock.
Read and download routes do not create missing export directories. Cache clearing does not touch completed Exports or export staging.

Run, export, and save identifiers
Three related ids have different owners:

A run-cache directory is cache/runs/{card_id}. The UI supplies the card id; the server accepts only letters, digits, _, and -. A request without one uses current.
make_export_id creates a timestamp-first, Windows-safe export directory name from the source-image stem.
make_save_id creates the corresponding stable id for a saved or automatic run archive. Its display label is metadata and does not determine identity.

Slugging lowercases names, replaces separator/punctuation runs with -, avoids Windows device names, caps the result at 64 characters, and appends -2, -3, and so on when the relevant destination already exists. Save collisions check both the .zip archive and .json sidecar. Export and ordinary manual-save callers use %Y%m%d-%H%M%S; promotion from automatic to saved normally preserves the original automatic-run timestamp while minting an id in the saved tier.
Saved and automatic runs are {save_id}.zip plus {save_id}.json pairs. Their publication, deletion, and promotion limits are documented in Saving, loading, and auto-capturing runs.

Source-image identity cache
SourceImageService keeps its disposable manifest and normalized working PNGs
under Generator/Workspace/cache/source-images. Normalized entries record the
digest of the original HEIC/HEIF/HIF/AVIF or HDR gain-map JPEG bytes. Native JPEG, PNG,
TIFF, BMP, and WebP entries also record a SHA-256 digest plus size,
modification time, change time, dimensions, and detected source format.
Library discovery validates and indexes a native file once. Later discovery
and saved-run matching reuse that entry while all three filesystem identity
values remain unchanged; a changed file is inspected and hashed again before
it can be considered ready. Exact saved-run lookup first selects digest-index
matches, then applies same-name-first deterministic ordering. It does not
rehash every ready library image on each run load.
The prepared-source cache is the sole startup-cache exception, so its manifest
and normalized conversions survive ordinary process restarts and continue to
use fingerprint, normalization-version, integrity, size-limit, and orphan
pruning rules. Clear Temp Files removes it; the next Library discovery
rebuilds the index from the untouched originals in Generator/Images.

Cache administration
cache_admin.safe_clear_dir(target, root=CACHE_DIR) deletes a target’s contents without following a symlink or Windows junction outside the cache. It uses lexical containment checks, rejects linked/junction ancestors, removes an in-cache link itself rather than traversing it, and treats a missing target as an empty no-op. saved_runs is structurally outside the permitted cache root.























ActionFiles removedIn-memory state removedPreservedNew Prisma process startupevery cache child except source-images, including unsaved run/batch artifacts, Auto Runs, LUTs, and temporary importsnone yet; cleanup precedes server importprepared source conversions and manifest; all persistent data outside cacheClear Temp Files / POST /api/cache/clear-allrun cache (including private loaded-run sources), automatic-run tier, LUT cache, prepared source images, and the source digest manifestsolve cache, solve/export history in the frontend, and palette backend cachesaved runs, Images, Exports, durable config, logs
This is the only user-facing cache-clear action. If the current image is a
private loaded-run source, the endpoint clears both image_path and the
runtime-only image_source_ref; the UI explains that the saved run can be
loaded again. Ordinary Image Library selections are preserved. The action is
serialized behind pending configuration publication, returns the exact cleared
source reference and authoritative configuration, and force-reconciles local
history only after backend success. It is refused while solve, export,
suggestion, or image preparation is active, and
it is excluded from model-library mutation/restart transitions through the
shared resource-coordination guard. This is an admission rule, not a claim
that every different long-job kind is globally serialized; see Driving the
Generator.

Recipe breakdown and cookbook
The solve artifact builder first converts the solved stack-label map into flat recipe-breakdown entries. build_recipe_cookbook then rolls those entries into the tree used by the recipe viewer:
colored-filament count → unordered colored-filament combination → exact physical recipe

The distinction between classification and physical content is important for banded solves.
What a recipe contains
An ordinary recipe contains its ordered color-filament entries. A banded recipe can additionally contain white-cap filament entries whose material_role is white_fill, because empty space in a fixed-height color band is physically filled with white. The recipe node and its recipe_key preserve those white-fill intervals. Banded keys include their band index so two physically different band placements are not collapsed.
The white base and final variable white cap are not recipe entries. Swap-band white fill is different: it is part of the fixed banded color-stack structure and remains in the physical recipe.
How taxonomy and rollups treat white fill
For the family and combination taxonomy, the cookbook filters material_role == "white_fill" and counts only colored filaments:

n_colors is the number of colored recipe entries;
the combination key is the sorted colored-filament id tuple;
the per-filament rollup counts only colored filament participation; and
the nested recipe still exposes the full ordered recipe, including white fill.

This lets the UI describe a recipe as, for example, a two-color family without pretending that its necessary white-filled band intervals do not exist.
Base-only pixels
The breakdown calls a pixel base-only when its stack has no non-white-fill colored material. A banded stack that contains only white fill therefore contributes to excluded_empty_recipe_pixels rather than becoming a zero-color physical recipe entry. The cookbook exposes that count as a synthetic Base only family when it is nonzero.
total_image_pixels is the complete solved-plan pixel count. Every area_fraction divides by that same total, returning 0.0 for an empty image. color_pixels is the sum of nonzero-color family counts.
Stable ordering

Base only, when present, comes first.
Other families sort by ascending color count.
Combinations sort by descending pixel count, then id tuple.
Recipes sort by descending pixel count, then recipe key.
Filament rollups sort by descending pixel count, then filament id.

The cookbook performs counting only. The color-only prediction, contour maps, and interactive rendering are separate server/frontend artifacts.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: Saving, loading, and auto-capturing runs
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: Prisma can package a completed solve as a self-contained ZIP, keep it deliberately as a saved run or temporarily as one of the 20 newest autosaves, and either restore the whole run into a new card or use only its captured settings.

This page describes the current saved-run archive, its two storage tiers, the browser workflows that consume it, and the actual interruption guarantees. The archive is portable; the neighboring JSON file is local list metadata. See also Run cache and per-card artifacts, The staged backend (Stage 0-5), generator.run_archive, generator.run_store, generator.auto_run_store, and generator.run_naming.
Two storage tiers



































Saved runsAutosavesDirectoryGenerator/Workspace/saved_runs/Generator/Workspace/cache/auto_runs/Created byExplicit Save actionBest-effort capture after a successful solveRetentionUntil explicitly deletedTargets the newest 20 listed entries during one Prisma process; startup clears the tierFull Clear Cache actionPreservedRemovedCan become a saved runAlready savedYes, through Save in the Saved Runs window
Both tiers use the same {save_id}.zip plus {save_id}.json layout. auto_run_store delegates ordinary storage work to run_store, then applies autosave retention. GET /api/runs/saved merges both lists and sorts them newest-first.
The ZIP and its sidecar
For each run:

{save_id}.zip is the portable artifact. It contains the source image, solve data, and cached review artifacts.
{save_id}.json is local list metadata. list_saves discovers runs from these sidecars without opening every ZIP; renaming edits only this file.

The sidecar records save_id, display label, saved_at, source_image_name, palette, compact mean_de and max_de statistics, archive schema version, and tier.
Per-file replacement is safe; the pair is not transactional
run_store.write_save first writes .zip.tmp and .json.tmp, then calls os.replace for the ZIP followed by the sidecar. Each published file is therefore replace-safe: readers do not observe a partially written ZIP or partially written JSON file. The two replacements are not one atomic transaction and there is no recovery journal.
A hard process stop can consequently leave:

hidden temporary files if it occurs before publication; or
a published ZIP with no listed sidecar if it occurs between the two replacements.

Because the sidecar drives the list, an orphan ZIP is not shown in the Saved Runs window. This is an interruption boundary, not evidence that archive bytes were partially written.
Stable identity and labels
make_save_id derives a Windows-safe identifier from the timestamp and source-image stem. It caps the identifier at 64 characters and adds -2, -3, and so on when either candidate file already exists. The display label is independent of that identifier, so renaming does not rename the on-disk pair.
The store accepts only identifiers matching ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ before building
a path. The Save dialog requires a nonblank display name. Names matching
^run\s+\d+$ after trimming, case-insensitively—such as Run 7, run 7, or
Run 007—are reserved for Generator’s automatic live-card labels. Save and
Rename reject new writes using that form in both the UI and API. Existing or
uploaded archives with a legacy Run N label still load and display normally.
The backend still falls back to the generated identifier if another caller
sends an empty label.
Archive contents
run_archive.pack_run_archive builds the ZIP from supplied bytes and arrays without changing server state.



































MemberRequiredContentsrun.jsonyesSchema header, identity, full config and palette, image-domain dimensions, result/statistics, sanitized export metadata, and optional durable run_metadatathickness_maps.npzyesCompressed tm__* thickness maps, dbg__* debug maps, and ex__* export mapsimage/<file>yesExactly one nonempty source image; conversion-required sources are embedded as their solve-time normalized PNGsolve_state.jsonoptionalThe solve-owned fingerprint used by review-tier staterun_cache/<relpath>optionalThe portable per-card cache subtree, including review images/data and any export bundle already present; Prisma’s private loaded-source namespace is excluded
When the per-card run.json is readable, the packer also copies it into the optional top-level run_metadata field. This preserves newer solve-start diagnostics and recipe/profile snapshots while keeping older schema-version-1 archives loadable. The original file is still present inside run_cache/ because the whole cache tree is copied.
For HEIC, HEIF, HIF, AVIF, and recognized HDR gain-map JPEG sources, solve start snapshots the exact normalized PNG used by that solve. Save and autosave embed that snapshot rather than re-reading a possibly changed original or disposable cache. Optional source_asset provenance records the original filename/format, semantic source variant when needed, source digest, normalized member name, and normalization version. Schema version remains 1. Builds predating HDR gain-map JPEG support may reject the new normalized-JPEG provenance shape even though its image member is an ordinary PNG.
The packer applies the same 4,096-member and 512 MiB total-uncompressed-size ceilings as the reader. Save therefore cannot intentionally create an archive that violates those two reader limits.
Saved Runs window
The Load action on the Solve and Export sidebars opens one combined list of saved runs and autosaves. Each row includes:

a preview derived from the archive-owned source image;
display label and Saved/Autosave tier;
source filename; and
saved timestamp.

The preview routes read and validate the archive, apply EXIF orientation, convert the image to RGB, fit it within 320 × 320 pixels, and return a JPEG. Preview generation does not extract files into the Generator workspace.
The selected row controls these actions:

Load restores the complete run into a fresh solve card.
Use Settings reads the archive’s captured configuration into a session-only TEMP settings profile without restoring its image or run cache.
Download streams the original ZIP.
Rename changes a saved run’s sidecar label; autosaves cannot be renamed.
Delete removes either tier after the UI’s two-click confirmation.
Save promotes an autosave into the durable saved tier.

The ordinary Saved Runs mode can also load an uploaded ZIP. Upload is hidden in settings-only mode because uploaded archives currently use the whole-run rehydration route rather than the read-only settings route.
Saving and auto-capture
Explicit save
POST /api/runs/save requires a completed solve still present in the in-memory
solve cache. The card’s Save action remains disabled until completion and
becomes busy during the request so repeated clicks cannot create duplicate
submissions. The live card is renamed only after a successful response, using
the server-returned label as authoritative; card identity and persisted
identity remain card_id and save_id, never the display label. Native source
images from an ordinary live solve must still exist in Generator Images.
Conversion-required sources use the solve-owned normalized snapshot, so their
archive remains stable if the original changes after the solve. A card loaded
from an archive instead reads the exact private archive snapshot retained for
that card; changing or deleting a same-content library match cannot change a
re-saved archive’s embedded image name or bytes. The server packages the
current cached solve and writes it to saved_runs/.
Best-effort autosave
After a successful staged solve has populated the completed-solve cache, _maybe_write_auto_run packages the same archive shape under auto_runs/. Failures are logged and do not turn a successful solve into a failed solve.
After writing, evict_old_auto_runs lists sidecars newest-first and deletes
entries beyond the retention limit of 20. Auto Runs are session-temporary:
after the launcher acquires the Workspace lock for a newly launched Prisma
process, startup cache cleanup removes the entire automatic tier. Reconnecting
to an already-running process does not. Retention and the full Clear Cache
action also treat autosaves as disposable cache.
Promotion
POST /api/runs/auto/{id}/promote is refused while a solve, export, or palette-suggestion job is active or cancelling. Promotion:

validates that both autosave files exist;
mints a fresh identifier in saved_runs/;
stages a rewritten saved-tier sidecar;
moves the unchanged ZIP into saved_runs/;
publishes the saved sidecar; and
removes the old autosave sidecar.

Ordinary exceptions during the ZIP or sidecar publication steps trigger compensating cleanup or a ZIP move back to the autosave directory. This is useful rollback, but it is not a process-kill transaction. A hard stop between filesystem operations can leave an orphan ZIP, a listed autosave whose ZIP has moved, or both old and new sidecars listed against the one moved ZIP. There is no startup promotion journal that converges those states automatically.
Loading a complete run
Both a selected local entry and an uploaded ZIP pass through read_run_archive. Loading is refused while a solve, export, or palette-suggestion job is active or cancelling. A successful load never overwrites the original card; it creates a fresh loaded-<timestamp> card.
The backend then:

validates the archive and its current configuration contract;
rejects retired preferred-length/soft-warning artifacts, configurations that disable the now-mandatory detail cap, contradictory native/normalized source metadata, and archive members in Prisma’s reserved private-source cache namespace;
stores the exact archived image bytes under _loaded_source/ inside the fresh card’s private run cache;
compares a verifiable archived source digest with the persistent Image Library digest index, preferring an exact same-name match and then the case-insensitively sorted first differently named exact match;
separates the tm__, dbg__, and ex__ arrays;
writes every portable archived run_cache/ member under the fresh card directory;
recursively rebases cached ?run=<old> URLs to the new card identifier; and
adds a synthetic complete solve entry to the current server session.

The synthetic cache preserves the archived maps, result, export metadata, image-domain dimensions, and fingerprint. Objects that were not serialized as reconstructable runtime objects—such as solved-plan, grouping, and live profile objects—are left None. Review consumers use the restored cache files and rebased result URLs.
The exact archive snapshot always remains attached privately to the loaded
card. If the digest search found a library match, the frontend selects that
ordinary library item for new work. Otherwise it selects the private source
through the opaque runtime reference loaded-run:<card_id> and shows Saved
run source; the temporary source is not added to the Image Library or its
count. The reference contains no filesystem path and is accepted only while
the loaded card cache exists.
For native image members, the backend always derives identity from the
embedded bytes. A schema-version-1 normalized member is a solve-time PNG, so it
cannot prove which original HEIC/HEIF/HIF/AVIF or HDR gain-map JPEG bytes produced it. Local saved
and automatic runs may use the Prisma-authored original-source digest retained
with their managed archive; uploaded schema-version-1 normalized archives do
not trust that editable provenance and therefore remain private. This is a
deliberate false-negative match rather than a risk of activating an unrelated
Library image.
The frontend creates a new history card using the archive label, selects the
resolved active image, applies the captured frame and image-adjustment state,
uses the archived config as the basis of the live session, and restores the palette by
reusing a matching deck card, loading a matching saved palette, or creating an
ad-hoc card. The loaded card keeps its historical resolved printability values,
but live synchronization overlays the currently active printer’s nozzle-derived
width and length before any new solve. It never writes archived thresholds into
the printer profile.
A new solve uses the currently selected library match or private source.
Preview, palette suggestion, and luminance recommendation use that same
selection. The loaded result and any later re-save continue to use the private
snapshot even if a matched library file changes or disappears.
Client application is compensating-transactional: if final configuration
synchronization fails, the prior card list, image, frame, adjustments, palette
deck, and live configuration are restored and Prisma attempts to republish that
restored configuration before reporting the load failure.
Rehydration interruption boundary
Whole-run rehydration writes the private image and cache files before
publishing the in-memory solve-cache entry. Image validation failures remove
the fresh private directory, but later write errors and hard process stops
have no filesystem journal. They can therefore leave a partial run-cache
directory that is not attached to a live card. Clear Temp Files removes
that cache. Rehydration never writes the archive image into Generator/Images,
so repeated loads do not create visible loaded-* images. Legacy loaded-*
files made by older versions remain ordinary user-managed library files and
are not moved, hidden, or deleted.
Loading settings only
POST /api/runs/settings validates the selected saved/autosave ZIP and returns its config, palette, label, optional durable metadata, and solve-start diagnostics. The route itself does not write the archived image, restore run-cache files, or add a solve card, and it does not use the active-job gate. The frontend subsequently applies the resulting TEMP profile through the ordinary live config and module-state synchronization paths.
The frontend reconstructs a settings snapshot with explicit compatibility fallbacks:

broad archived config;
optional run_metadata.config;
server-resolved solve-start settings; and
the durable recipe/profile settings snapshot, when present.

Later sources in that sequence override earlier ones. Diagnostic module parameters are merged into preprocessing parameters. Module toggles prefer the durable recipe/profile snapshot, fall back to diagnostic module state, and use older active-module diagnostics only as a compatibility fallback.
The result is a single session-only profile identified in the UI with a TEMP badge and the source run’s label. Loading another run’s settings replaces the prior TEMP profile. TEMP can be modified and used for solves, but cannot become the startup profile or be overwritten in place; Save routes to Save As to create a normal named profile. The same TEMP flow is available from a live solve card’s display-only Settings panel.
Applying a profile is coordinated but not one backend transaction. The frontend first applies settings and module state locally, sends the config, and then sends the module snapshot. If either synchronization step fails, it tries to restore the previous local state and, once config publication has begun, sends compensating config/module updates. A rollback request can itself fail, in which case the console records the failure and the next server refresh is authoritative.
Rename and delete interruption behavior
rename_save stages a new sidecar and replaces that one file atomically. It does not edit the ZIP.
delete_save unlinks the ZIP and then the sidecar. Missing files are benign; an ordinary Windows file-lock error becomes a clean HTTP 409. The two deletions are not journaled. If the ZIP is removed and the process stops or sidecar deletion fails, the list can retain a sidecar whose download/load target no longer exists. Autosave eviction uses the same deletion primitive.
Untrusted-archive checks
The reader never calls extractall; it reads explicitly named members after validation. It rejects:

more than 4,096 members;
duplicate member names;
more than 512 MiB total declared uncompressed data;
names outside the closed archive allow-list;
empty, absolute, drive-letter, backslash, ./.., or traversing paths;
symlinks and other explicitly marked non-regular members;
missing required JSON/NPZ members;
archive schemas outside accepted version 1; and
anything other than exactly one nonempty source image;
non-boolean normalized-source provenance; and
source display/member formats that contradict their declared native or
normalized state.

The upload route separately reads multipart data in 1 MiB chunks and rejects compressed uploads beyond 512 MiB before parsing. This does not trust the client’s Content-Length.
Operational guarantees summary








































OperationOrdinary error handlingHard-stop guaranteeSave/autosave writeTemp files plus per-file os.replaceNo pair journal; hidden temp or orphan ZIP is possibleRenameTemp sidecar plus os.replaceExisting or new complete sidecar; a temp file may remainDelete/evictMissing files tolerated; locked-file error surfacedNo pair journal; one member may be removed firstPromoteCompensating rollback for caught failuresNo convergence journal between move/replace/unlink stepsWhole-run loadValidates the archive, privately retains its source, and removes the fresh directory after source-validation failureNo cleanup journal for later private-cache writesSettings-only archive readValidates without image/cache/card rehydrationThe later profile application still updates ordinary live config/module state
