prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: The preprocessing evaluation harness
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: an offline A/B bakeoff that solves two images through the production pipeline under one shared config and reports a fixed metric bundle (mean/p95 dE, out-of-gamut pixels, small-component count, cap total-variation), optionally dropping predicted-PNG + heatmap + report.json artifacts to disk.

This page documents the developer-only tools.generator.evaluation package: how to drive it from the CLI or a Python caller, and what each metric means. The package sits outside Prisma/generator and is not part of the shipped product or generated product-module graph. It exists to answer “did this preprocessing operator (or solver tweak) actually help?” with comparable numbers instead of eyeballing two renders.
What it is for
The harness compares two versions of an image — a baseline and a candidate — by running each through the full generator solve and diffing the results. It is corpus-agnostic: both images are passed in as explicit arrays, so the difference between baseline and candidate can be anything the caller wants (a preprocessing operator applied to one, a different denoise setting, etc.). It does not generate the candidate; you do that, then hand both to evaluate_pair.
Both arms run through the same SolveConfig, so any metric delta is attributable to the image difference, not config drift.
The contract: evaluate_pair
The single public entry point is evaluate_pair(request, *, modules_path=None, module_state=None) in tools/generator/evaluation/preprocessing_harness.py. It takes an EvaluationInput and returns an EvaluationResult.





























SymbolRoleEvaluationInputFrozen dataclass: case_id, baseline_image, candidate_image, solve_config, optional out_dir.EvaluationMetricsFrozen dataclass holding all 11 metric fields (see below).EvaluationResultCarries both SolveResult objects, the metrics bundle, and artifact_paths.EvaluationRunErrorRaised (not swallowed) when either arm’s solve fails; tags .arm ("baseline"/"candidate") and .original.evaluate_pairRuns both arms, aggregates metrics, optionally renders artifacts.
Flow

Two solves. _run_arm calls solve_full (from generator.facade) once per image. solve_full runs run_pipeline under FULL_PRESET, i.e. the staged production backend — not the legacy 6-step CLI engine in solve.py. If either solve raises, it is wrapped as EvaluationRunError(arm, exc) rather than crashing silently.
Metric aggregation. _compute_metrics reads the two SolveResult objects and builds the EvaluationMetrics bundle.
Optional artifacts. Only when request.out_dir is not None does it lazily import render_evaluation_artifacts and write files. The lazy import is deliberate: in-memory metric callers never pull in PIL.

Metrics are always returned in memory; artifacts are opt-in.
Where the metrics come from
_compute_metrics reads these SolveResult accessors (defined in generator.facade):



































Source fieldAccessorContractdE mapresult.de_mapPrefers diagnostics[MapKey.DE], then falls back to thickness_maps.Gamut maskresult.gamut_maskReads the standardized gamut diagnostic.Per-filament thicknessresult.thickness_mapsReturns the color-material maps exposed by the facade.White-cap mapresult.cap_mapReads MapKey.WHITE_CAP.Predicted renderresult.predict_image()Reconstructs the predicted image through the active appearance provider.
The solver pitch used for area scaling is config.solver_fine_pitch_mm, read off the baseline’s SolveResult.config.
The metric bundle
EvaluationMetrics holds eleven fields — for the five base metrics, both arms plus one delta where relevant:



































MetricBaseline / candidate fieldsHow computedMean dEbaseline_mean_de, candidate_mean_de, delta_mean_dede_map.mean() per arm; delta = candidate - baseline. Empty map → 0.0.p95 dEbaseline_p95_de, candidate_p95_de95th percentile of the dE map via _p95 and np.percentile(arr, 95.0). Empty → 0.0.Out-of-gamut pixelsbaseline_oog_pixels, candidate_oog_pixels_oog_pixels counts True cells in the boolean gamut_mask with int(mask.sum()).Small-component countbaseline_small_component_count, candidate_small_component_countcount_small_components over the thickness maps (see below).Cap total-variationbaseline_cap_total_variation, candidate_cap_total_variationcap_total_variation over cap_map (see below).
Note dE is the only metric with a precomputed delta_* field; for the rest the caller diffs the two arms.
Metric primitives — preprocessing_metrics.py
Two metrics are non-trivial and live in tools/generator/evaluation/preprocessing_metrics.py:
count_small_components in preprocessing_metrics.py counts speckle. For each per-filament thickness map (keys starting with __ are diagnostics and skipped):

Mark a pixel “occupied” if its thickness exceeds 5% of that map’s max (_SMALL_COMPONENT_REL_THRESHOLD = 0.05).
Run 8-connectivity connected-component labeling with a 3×3 structuring element of ones through scipy.ndimage.label.
Convert each component’s pixel count to physical area as pixel_count × pixel_pitch_mm².
Accumulate the count of components whose area is below min_area_mm2.

The min_area_mm2 threshold is derived in the harness, not hard-coded: feature_scale_mm², where feature_scale_mm comes from resolve_feature_scale_mm. That helper returns 2.0 × nozzle_diameter (_FEATURE_WIDTHS_PER_NOZZLE = 2.0), i.e. 0.40 mm at the default 0.20 mm nozzle, so min_area = 0.40² = 0.16 mm². This is the value the retired cleanup_min_area_mm2 carried.
cap_total_variation measures how “busy” the white-cap surface is. It returns the anisotropic L1 total variation Σ(|Δx| + |Δy|) over the 2-D cap map: abs(diff(axis=1)).sum() + abs(diff(axis=0)).sum(). It is a grid-space sum, not a per-mm integral; a non-2-D or empty map returns 0.0. Lower means a smoother cap.
Artifacts — preprocessing_render.py
When out_dir is set, render_evaluation_artifacts in tools/generator/evaluation/preprocessing_render.py writes exactly four files:

























FileContentbaseline_predicted.pngBaseline predict_image() as RGB PNG.candidate_predicted.pngCandidate predict_image().delta_de_heatmap.pngSigned candidate − baseline dE heatmap.report.json{"case_id": ..., **asdict(metrics)}.
The heatmap (_save_delta_de_heatmap) is signed: it normalizes delta = candidate − baseline by its peak absolute value, then puts positive delta (candidate worse) in the red channel and negative delta (candidate better) in the green channel. Mismatched shapes are defensively cropped to the smaller grid, though they are expected to match.
report.json’s schema is locked to the EvaluationMetrics dataclass via asdict; the drift-regression test in tests/generator/test_preprocessing_evaluation_metrics.py guards it.
How to drive it
CLI wrapper status
tools/generator/evaluation/preprocessing_eval_cli.py contains a thin parser that loads two images, builds a shared SolveConfig, calls evaluate_pair, and prints the report. Required parser fields are --case-id, --baseline, --candidate, --profiles, --palette, and --white-base; artifacts are optional through --out-dir, and --solver-preset accepts only full.
The canonical developer invocation is python -m tools.generator.evaluation.preprocessing_eval_cli .... Package import and --help are runtime-independent: Generator and harness imports are deferred until after argument parsing. An actual evaluation still enters the live facade and therefore needs an intentionally selected developer runtime plus an explicit published-library profile directory; the old checkout-relative Prisma/data/filaments/profiles example no longer exists. This remains a developer tool, not an end-user launch path.
From Python
from tools.generator.evaluation.preprocessing_harness import EvaluationInput, evaluate_pair
 
result = evaluate_pair(EvaluationInput(
    case_id="my_case",
    baseline_image=baseline_u8,   # np.ndarray HxWx3 uint8
    candidate_image=candidate_u8,
    solve_config=cfg,             # facade.SolveConfig
    out_dir=None,                 # set a Path to also write artifacts
))
print(result.metrics.delta_mean_de)
The namespace package markers are intentionally inert. Import explicit submodules such as tools.generator.evaluation.preprocessing_harness or tools.generator.evaluation.preprocessing_metrics; there is no compatibility package or eager re-export surface under Prisma.generator or bare evaluation.
Liveness

evaluate_pair / tools.generator.evaluation — live developer/test API. It is imported by the wrapper and exercised by focused tests, but not called by a normal web-app request.
render_evaluation_artifacts — live harness implementation, reached when out_dir is supplied and exercised end to end by tests.
count_small_components / cap_total_variation — live evaluation primitives called by _compute_metrics and covered independently.
preprocessing_eval_cli.py — developer parser retained under tools.generator.evaluation; namespace import and --help are clean without runtime selection, while real evaluation still requires an explicit runtime/profile context.

Caveats

Production solve path. Both arms go through solve_full → run_pipeline / FULL_PRESET — the staged backend, the same engine the webapp uses. The metrics reflect production solver behavior, including grouping/cleanup, not the legacy solve.py CLI engine.
Wrapper surface versus implementation. preprocessing_eval_cli.py exposes --solver-preset, but accepts only full and does not pass the value separately because evaluate_pair always selects solve_full. Argument parsing and help are runtime-independent; solve execution is not.
Shapes must match. Metrics assume baseline and candidate solved to the same grid (same config, same image dimensions). The heatmap renderer crops defensively, but the dE mean/p95 do not align grids — feed same-sized images.
Cap-TV is grid-space. cap_total_variation is a raw grid sum; it is only comparable between two solves at the same resolution. Do not compare TV across differing solver_fine_pitch_mm.

Related

generator.facade — SolveConfig, SolveResult, solve_full
The staged backend (Stage 0-5) — what run_pipeline / FULL_PRESET actually does
Preprocessing operators — the image-conditioning operator kernels
Delta E and the gamut mask — what de_map and gamut_mask mean
generator.thickness_maps — MapKey, ThicknessMaps, the __-prefixed diagnostic keys

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.filePath: Prisma Lithophane Generator/Technical Reference/Using/Automatic palette suggestion.md
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: Automatic palette suggestion
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: Generator summarizes the prepared source as weighted model-OKLab colors, estimates the single-, pair-, and selected triple-filament colors the active model can reproduce, and searches for distinct filament sets with low nearest-gamut error.

This page explains the target signature and gamut machinery. Search selection
and ranking are detailed on Palette suggestion search and ranking.
What the browser starts
The Suggest Palettes button sends POST /api/palette/suggest. The server reserves a background job, returns a job_id, and exposes progress through GET /api/palette/suggest/status. Cancellation is a job-ID-qualified request to POST /api/palette/suggest/cancel; the browser keeps polling until a terminal state and rejects stale-job results.
PaletteSuggestPayload forbids unknown fields. Its API defaults are:



































FieldAPI defaultMeaningimage_pathrequiredImage in the active Generator Images foldern_filaments7Exact number of colored filaments in every returned palette; base/cap is separatetop_k5Maximum number of distinct alternatives to returnfilament_idsall eligibleRestrict the candidate poolpalette_modestandardstandard or luminance_detail
n_filaments accepts 2–16 and top_k accepts 1–10. A request fails rather
than silently shrinking the palette when fewer than n_filaments supported,
eligible candidates remain. Explicit candidate IDs must be unique and must not
include the reserved base/cap filament.
There is no current max_swaps, improvement_threshold, force_all_tiers,
search_mode, or quality_weights request. Unknown and retired request fields
receive 422 rather than being ignored.
Step 1—build the image signature
The server loads the selected source with the same framing/resampling and ordinary image-adjustment path used for a run, capped to an 80 mm longest dimension for suggestion work. It then calls solve_target_oklab_for_signature, which shares compute_solve_target_cloud with the solve runner and applies the same optional gamut-white rescale.
One important boundary: palette suggestion does not run the enabled F1 preprocessing chain. It shares target-cloud conversion with solving, but a solve calls that helper after F1 while suggestion calls it directly on the prepared source raster.
The resulting ColorSignature contains model-OKLab centroids, normalized weights, pixel count, and domain="model_oklab". _assert_signature_gamut_domain_match rejects any attempt to score it against a differently tagged gamut.
Standard target
extract_color_signature_from_oklab clusters the cloud into up to 100 centroids in the web path. _kmeans_oklab uses deterministic k-means++ initialization (seed 42), up to 30 Lloyd iterations, a KDTree for assignment, and vectorized centroid accumulation.
Luminance-detail target
The web path asks extract_luminance_residual_signature for up to 120 clusters. It scales L by 0.15 during clustering and weights cluster centroids/contributions by source chroma importance. Low-chroma regions therefore carry less influence while vivid colors dominate.
Scoring has a separate L-axis weight. In standard mode it is 1 / chroma_weight; in luminance-detail mode it is 0.15 / chroma_weight. This metric scaling is independent of the clustering transformation.
Deeply saturated inverse-LUT corners are extrapolated beyond measured Camera Transform evidence. Suggestion deliberately follows the same ingress conversion rather than promising generation-independent accuracy there.
Step 2—choose the gamut provider
server._build_palette_suggestion_model follows the active appearance provider:




















Appearance providerGamut implementationRanking modehistorical_splineIn-module spline transmission samplingmeanphoto_stack_bundlePhotoStackPaletteGamutBackendrobust
Photo-stack v2 is the current default product provider. Its backend and sampled gamut caches are keyed by the selected bundle, corrections, white sandwich, layer/height budgets, and sampling settings. A missing required photo-stack bundle is a request error rather than a silent spline fallback.
For both providers, the fixed white base is multiplied into predictions while the search height budget represents cap plus color above that base. White base/cap are not candidate palette colors. Model-excluded whites block suggestion; model-excluded colors and v2-unsupported colors are filtered from the pool.
The browser nevertheless renders the active base/cap filament in the candidate library with is-base-cap-reserved, aria-disabled="true", a BASE/CAP label, and an explanatory tooltip. It is excluded from candidateSelection; showing it is an accounting affordance, not a change to the search pool.
Step 3—sample reachable colors
Single colors
For each candidate filament, the sampler evaluates all color-layer counts from zero through the configured maximum across a cap grid sampled every fourth cap step. Combinations exceeding the cap-plus-color height budget are removed.
Pairs
Every unordered pair is sampled on a coarser cap grid (every eighth step) with ten thickness samples per color. Pair clouds capture mixed colors that neither single filament reaches. Nearest distances from every signature centroid to every single and pair cloud are precomputed once; palette trials then reduce those arrays instead of rebuilding KDTrees.
Sparse triples
The initial search remains single/pair-based. The exact-size finalists already
selected for the requested top_k are then rescored with every three-filament
combination inside those finalists. Triple clouds use four thickness samples
per color and every eighth cap step. This sparse pass can reorder the bounded
result set without paying the cost of triple clouds for the entire candidate
space.
The response metadata records whether that rescore ran and how many finalists it processed.
Score and response
For a palette, each signature centroid takes the minimum distance over all available single, pair, and—after finalist rescore—triple clouds. Metrics are:

weighted mean distance;
worst centroid distance;
weighted 90th percentile;
percentage of signature weight above 0.02 OKLab distance;
coverage, reported as 100 - percentage above threshold.

The photo-stack path ranks with the robust combination described on Palette suggestion search and ranking; the historical spline path ranks by mean.
The ordinary browser receives a flat candidates list containing no more than
top_k exact-size palettes, plus palette_mode, model provenance, and
signature provenance. The frontend adds those records to the temporary
Suggested Palettes staging area. It names them Color suggested N or
Luminance suggested N from the returned palette_mode. A user action then
promotes a staging card into the persistent Palette Deck.
The requested size is not clamped to the printer’s simultaneous color
capacity. The browser’s AMS diagram fills only the physical color slots and
shows the excess in a distinct Additional colors row. Filament swaps may be
required, but the row is not a second AMS, a load tier, or a predicted
grouping. Auto-Suggest cannot know the exact number of swaps because solve-time
recipe use determines the grouping plan; the completed solve is the authority
on actual swaps.
Suggested cards and Palette Deck cards share the compact title/action/chip
structure. Both render colored filament chips plus a separate support chip for
the active white base/cap filament. That support chip is presentation context,
not an additional candidate color and not part of filament_ids.
Palette suggestion stops after staging palette records. It does not start a
solve, own batch orchestration, or transfer solved results. Users promote any
desired suggestions into the Palette Deck with Add to Deck. The main Solve
control owns both single and deck-selected batch execution; see Driving the
Generator for that separate API and job contract.
Stable source anchors

Prisma/generator/server.py: PaletteSuggestPayload and the suggestion start/status/cancel routes
Prisma/generator/app/features/palette/suggestions.js: suggestion request, polling, and staging
Prisma/generator/palette/suggest.py: signature extraction, gamut backends, distance precomputation, and sparse triple rescore
Prisma/generator/pipeline/target_cloud.py: shared target-domain conversion

Related: Palette suggestion search and ranking, Model-domain ingress and display conversion, The Transmission Model, The photo-stack v2 model, and Appearance provider.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.filePath: Prisma Lithophane Generator/Technical Reference/Using/Command-line entry points and filament availability.md
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: Command-line entry points and filament availability
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: the supported way to run Generator from source is the Prisma launcher, which establishes the portable filesystem and active-library contract before importing the server; evaluation and palette-suggestion CLIs are internal developer tools, while new palette and solve work is gated by the active published library and the user’s per-library filament selection.

This page distinguishes three things that are easy to conflate: starting the actual product from source, invoking internal command-line modules, and deciding which published filaments may enter new work.
Related: Driving the Generator · Settings, resolution, and the config contract · How a Solve Works · generator.facade · generator.filament_policy

Supported source entry point
The product entry point is Prisma.launcher, not uvicorn server:app and not either of the solver-oriented scripts below. The launcher:

resolves and prepares a portable application root;
acquires the Generator Workspace lock;
conservatively removes exact, ordinary abandoned export stages while preserving unrecognized or link-like lookalikes;
validates the selected published model library or enters Library Recovery;
supplies the explicit Images, Exports, Workspace, model-store, and active-library environment contract;
starts the local FastAPI server on the first available port beginning at 8010; and
connects the in-app restart action to a fresh launcher process.

Use the current commands in the repository README.md. The --app-root directory must already exist; the README creates it before invoking the launcher. Directly importing generator/server.py, running Uvicorn from the Generator folder, or importing data_paths.py from a clean shell fails deliberately because no launcher-selected Workspace or published library has been supplied.
In a normal source launch, switching libraries can use the in-app restart action because the launcher installs the restart callback. A hand-started Uvicorn server has no callback and can only tell the user to close and reopen Prisma.
Internal command-line modules
The repository contains two command-line-shaped developer modules, but neither is an alternative end-user distribution path.




















ModulePurposeProduction statustools.generator.evaluation.preprocessing_eval_cliA/B evaluation wrapper around the live facade/staged solverDeveloper/evaluation harness onlygenerator/palette/suggest.pyPalette-suggestion development CLIDeveloper tool; the web app calls the suggester through server routes
The evaluation module defers Generator imports until after argument parsing, so python -m tools.generator.evaluation.preprocessing_eval_cli --help works from a clean repository shell without selecting or writing a runtime. A real evaluation still imports the live facade and needs an intentionally selected developer runtime and explicit published-library profiles. The palette-suggestion module likewise remains developer tooling rather than an alternative product launch path.
Shared product helpers
The shared helpers formerly embedded in the retired batch CLI now have product-specific owners:





















OwnerLive roleimage_ingress.load_imageEXIF-aware image load, framing, transforms, and resampling for solves and palette suggestionimage_ingress.apply_adjustmentsExposure, contrast, saturation, tint, highlight, shadow, and temperature adjustmentsfilament_policy.validate_paletteProfile-presence and generation-availability validation in pipeline.runner’s Load stage, before LUT construction and staged execution
The obsolete batch parser and its alternate solve orchestration have been removed. The sole product solve path is facade.solve_full() → pipeline.runner.run_pipeline() → the staged backend.
Preprocessing evaluation harness
tools.generator.evaluation.preprocessing_eval_cli builds a real SolveConfig and delegates to tools.generator.evaluation.preprocessing_harness.evaluate_pair. It solves a baseline and candidate image under one configuration and can optionally write predicted images, a delta-dE heat map, and report.json. The harness itself is tested and is also called by evaluation scripts; the wrapper is a developer leaf outside the shipped product package, not a UI or release entry point.

Published-library filament contract
Generator reads one immutable published library selected by the launcher. A standard library is valid only when its manifest, exact file set, hashes, filament registry, v1 spline artifacts, v2 photo-stack deployment, and Camera Transform deployment all validate together. A profile file copied into some other folder is not enough to make a filament usable.
Each public filament record currently carries both:

exclude_from_model, the calibration/publication policy flag; and
generation_available, a public convenience field emitted as the inverse of that flag.

The current Generator policy implementation still treats exclude_from_model as authoritative and derives the API’s generation_available value from it. In libraries produced by Calibration the two values agree. The stored convenience field is therefore redundant today; it is not an independent override.
Backend gate for new work
filament_policy.py defines the common rule used by validation, suggestion, and solving:

exclude_from_model: true means unavailable for new Generator work;
profile presence is checked separately;
an unavailable fixed white base or cap is a hard error for suggestion and solving; and
color candidates that are unavailable are removed from suggestion before search.

POST /api/palette/validate reports missing profiles and policy-unavailable filaments separately, but it is only an advisory pre-check. The staged solve validates again before doing work. Existing saved-run arrays are not destroyed merely because a filament later becomes unavailable; any new solve is evaluated against the currently active library.
Unknown filament ids are not made safe by the policy helper’s permissive default. They still fail the profile and active-library checks before a solve can use them.
Browser-side Active Filaments gate
The Active Filaments control is a second, user-owned filter over the library’s eligible color filaments. It determines which filaments appear in palette-building and suggestion surfaces; it does not mutate the published library.
The browser stores this choice in localStorage, keyed by the runtime active library id:

the first time a library is seen, all eligible filaments are enabled;
a user’s disabled subset persists through reloads and relaunches for that library;
if a previously seen runtime library id presents additional eligible ids, those newly eligible ids are enabled by default; and
ids no longer eligible are removed from the saved selection.

The frontend accepts a color filament only when it has a profile, is not excluded, is not reported unavailable, and is in the enabled set. The base/cap selectors are stricter: their candidates must additionally have white_cap_eligible: true. The backend remains authoritative and revalidates when work starts, so stale browser storage cannot bypass the model policy.
Two unrelated exclusion helpers
Generator’s filament_policy.excluded_filament_ids(registry) gates new generation from a published registry. Calibration’s fitting.filament_exclusions.excluded_filament_ids(store) removes excluded evidence from model fitting. They read the same conceptual flag but accept different inputs and protect different workflows.
Source-truth boundary

Use Prisma.launcher to run the application from source.
Treat evaluation wrappers as developer harnesses: clean help is runtime-independent, but actual evaluation requires an explicitly bootstrapped runtime.
Treat the active published library as model truth.
Treat Active Filaments as a per-browser, per-library palette filter, not as a model mutation.
Expect every new solve and suggestion to be revalidated by the backend.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.filePath: Prisma Lithophane Generator/Technical Reference/Using/Driving the Generator.md
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: Driving the Generator
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: Generator is a local, single-process four-step web app whose launcher establishes one portable runtime and one active model library, while the server keeps process-global UI/job state and coordinates independently admitted solve, suggestion, export, and model-library workflows.

This page follows the browser-to-server contract. For the staged solve itself see How a Solve Works and The Joint LUT and Staged Solve; for export internals see Exporting Print Files.

Starting the application
In either a packaged Generator release or the Suite, start Prisma Generator.exe on Windows or Prisma Generator on Linux. The platform-specific executables enter the same Python launcher contract:

anchors the portable Generator tree beside the executables;
takes the Workspace lock;
reconciles interrupted export/model-install stages;
validates the selected immutable model library or enters Library Recovery;
starts FastAPI on loopback only; and
opens the browser.

Port 8010 is preferred, not guaranteed. If it is occupied, the launcher reserves the first available port through 8029 and prints/opens the actual 127.0.0.1 address. A second launch against the same Workspace reopens the owned instance rather than starting a second server.
From source, use python -m Prisma.launcher --app-root <existing-runtime-folder> after installing the declared Generator runtime group. The repository README gives the exact Windows and POSIX commands. Do not start uvicorn server:app as the normal source path: the server imports require launcher-provided model-library, Workspace, Images, and Exports roots, and direct Uvicorn also lacks the in-app restart callback.
Current evidence is platform-qualified: the source launcher and active-library selection have been health-smoked under Ubuntu 24.04/WSL2 as well as Windows, and the Linux x86-64 package is built in that environment. The POSIX lock, loopback socket, browser fallback, and macOS open branches have been statically audited, but no Mac has run Prisma and no macOS support is claimed.
The launcher treats Ctrl+C as a normal shutdown and prints Prisma stopped.. Closing the console stops the server. The app is bound to the local host and is not designed as a remotely hosted multi-user service.
Interface structure
The main workflow is:

Image — choose or upload source artwork.
Palette — enable candidate filaments, request suggestions, or build one manually.
Preview — run the full solve and inspect predicted, cap, surface, thickness, contour, and recipe data.
Export — select a solved run and generate one or more print-file variants.

The left rail owns infrequent configuration and persistent working controls: Palette Deck, Model Library, Active Filaments, and Printer/nozzle configuration. Model Library → Manage installs complete published bundles and selects the library for the next launch. Active Filaments is only a per-browser filter over eligible filaments in the runtime library.
The static shell loads one native-module entrypoint and an ordered stylesheet manifest. Feature modules own their state, events, and asynchronous lifecycles; the Theme controller is browser-local and does not enter server configuration. See Frontend architecture for the maintained browser-code map.

Process-global state
server.py creates one module-level session dictionary. It contains the editable config, current solve, in-memory solved-run cache, and separate job slots for suggestion and export. This state is not keyed by browser or user.
Consequences:

two tabs see and mutate the same session;
a job started in one tab is visible from the other;
in-memory current/solved-run state disappears when the process restarts; and
disk-backed settings, caches, Images, Exports, and saved-run archives survive according to their own lifecycles.

This makes Generator single-user, but it does not mean the backend globally serializes every different long-job type.
Background jobs and admission
The UI uses start-then-poll workflows for solve, palette suggestion, and export. A start route validates input, reserves its job slot synchronously, assigns a job id, launches a daemon worker thread, and returns. A status route is a read-only snapshot; it does not advance work.















































WorkflowStartPollUser cancelTerminal statesImage importPOST /api/images/import or /api/images/refreshGET /api/images/imports/{batch_id}No; it completes the bounded current filecomplete, partial, failedSolvePOST /api/solve/startGET /api/solve/statusPOST /api/solve/cancelcomplete, error, cancelledPalette batchPOST /api/solve/palette-batch/startGET /api/solve/status plus per-item result retrievalPOST /api/solve/cancelcomplete, partial, error, cancelledSuggestPOST /api/palette/suggestGET /api/palette/suggest/statusPOST /api/palette/suggest/cancelcomplete, error, cancelledExportPOST /api/export/files/startGET /api/export/files/statusPOST /api/export/files/cancelcomplete, error, cancelled; cancelling is an active state
Image preparation uses one worker, and repeated folder refreshes coalesce into the active scan. It pauses queued conversion work while solve, export, suggestion, or model-library operations need priority. Each numeric job kind refuses another active job of the same kind. Solve and suggestion also use separate worker locks to prevent two workers of that same implementation from executing simultaneously. There is no one global numeric-work lock across different kinds: for example, the current admission model can allow a solve and a suggestion to overlap.
All registered background-job kinds reserve against model-library
mutation/restart. A palette batch is the stricter comparison workflow: it
exclusively reserves solve, suggestion, export, image import/refresh, and
model-library resources while it freezes one source/configuration snapshot and
runs its explicitly selected deck items sequentially. Other start endpoints reject direct
API attempts during that ownership period. Cache clearing and saved-run loading
use the same active-job check.
Cancellation
Cancellation is cooperative. It does not terminate a Python thread:

Solve and suggestion cancel requests are tied to the active job id and set a flag checked at progress/safe checkpoints. The browser remains attached until a terminal status arrives.
Export changes immediately from running to cancelling, reports Cancelling after current safe point, and becomes cancelled after the worker acknowledges it. If publication finished before the request could land, it may validly report Completed before cancellation took effect.

The practical latency is therefore bounded by the next checkpoint, not the button click. Export cancellation also owns cleanup of its hidden stage; hard process termination is recovered on the next launcher start.

Step 1 — Images
GET /api/images lists only ready files in Generator/Images. Native sources are single-frame PNG, JPEG/JPE/JFIF, TIFF, BMP, and WebP. HEIC/HEIF/HIF, AVIF, and JPEGs with a semantically identified auxiliary HDR gain map are conversion-required sources: generator.source_images validates their signatures and frame roles, applies EXIF orientation and supported ICC/NCLX color information to the primary still, then atomically caches a lossless 8-bit sRGB PNG under Workspace/cache/source-images. Originals are never rewritten. General MPO, animated PNG/WebP/HEIF/AVIF, multi-page TIFF, and HDR-only PQ/HLG sources are rejected.
The UI sends multi-file additions to POST /api/images/import; uploads stream into private staging, are validated independently, and are published into Images only after successful preparation. Collision suffixes preserve every accepted original. POST /api/images/refresh discovers copied files, while GET /api/images/imports/{batch_id} exposes the bounded single-worker batch status. The legacy POST /api/images/upload remains a synchronous single-file compatibility route.
Previews are JPEG thumbnails made from the resolved working image. The selected original filename remains the session identity; preview, suggestion, solve, and archive creation all resolve it through the same service. Cache entries are keyed by source stat, SHA-256, and normalization version, recover from corruption, and are capped by LRU size. The UI can open the visible Images folder through the local-only folder-opening route.
Step 2 — Palette work
All new palette work is limited by the active published library and the user’s Active Filaments subset. See Command-line entry points and filament availability.
Validation
POST /api/palette/validate separates missing profiles from policy-unavailable filaments. It is advisory; suggestion and solve validate authoritatively again.
Suggestion
Suggestion is a background job that returns up to the requested number of
distinct palettes, all at the exact requested color count. The requested size
may exceed AMS/white-slot capacity; the suggestion path warns about that fact
but leaves actual grouping and swap planning to the solve. An unavailable
fixed base/cap is rejected before search, while unavailable color candidates
are filtered out. Cancellation is durable at the job level: the UI polls until
the backend reports a terminal state.
Suggestion ends after producing temporary staging cards. It neither owns nor
starts batch work. The browser promotes desired cards into the Palette Deck;
manual, suggested, saved, and loaded cards all enter the same solve workflow.
Persistent deck cards expose a browser-owned action menu. Create Variant
copies the card’s ordered colored-filament IDs into an ephemeral Manual-builder
draft; it never mutates the source or its saved record. Committing inserts a
new unsaved card beside the source. In Single Solve it becomes active; in Batch
Solve it remains unselected so explicit batch membership and order do not
change.
Deck-selected batch solve
The split top-bar Solve action changes only the browser interaction mode.
Single Solve uses the active deck card. Batch Solve lets the browser
submit 2–10 explicitly checked deck cards in deck order. Equivalent palettes
on distinct cards remain distinct items, and palette sizes may differ.
PaletteBatchStartPayload is independent of PaletteSuggestPayload. It
contains the current image identity, ordered deck_palettes records
(deck_card_id, display name, and filament_ids), profile provenance, and a
display recipe snapshot. Unknown suggestion-search fields receive 422.
Before reserving resources, the server validates every requested card against
the authoritative model library and ordinary solve requirements. It then
freezes one source copy, configuration, preprocessing state, active
printer/nozzle printability, model-library identity, base/cap filament, and
profile context. Only the colored palette changes between sequential calls to
the production full-solve operation. Batch items do not create Auto Run
archives.
GET /api/solve/status returns compact item state (position, result_id,
source deck id, label, palette, state, elapsed time, result availability, and
concise error). Completed artifacts are fetched once through
GET /api/solve/palette-batch/{job_id}/results/{result_id} rather than being
retransmitted in every poll. A failed item does not stop later items. Shared
preparation failure settles every queued item, cancellation preserves
completed and failed runs while removing unfinished Preview cards, and active
reload recovery temporarily owns the Batch Solve toolbar until terminal
status.
Step 3 — Solve and review
POST /api/solve/start requires a valid active library, source image, and nonempty palette. It snapshots the current config before starting so later UI edits cannot mutate the running solve. Before that request, the browser detects a solve pitch below the active nozzle diameter and offers to set both canonical pitch fields to the exact diameter through the normal synchronization path. Accepting preserves the physical cap-smoothing radius while recalculating its solve-grid cell representation; declining changes nothing. The server independently blocks any unresolved mismatch before reserving a job.
The server canonicalizes filament order, constructs a typed SolveConfig, assigns the card/job identity, and runs facade.solve_full() through the staged backend. Structured progress covers source preparation, pipeline stages, and artifact publication.
On success, the run cache receives predicted/reference/source images, error and gamut maps, per-filament and cap/surface fields, contour binaries, recipe breakdown/cookbook data, and export-owned solved arrays/metadata. The canonical total, boundary, and detail cap thickness artifacts use the shared Inferno renderer and absolute scale. Staged debug maps are written under a debug_ filename namespace so boundary_cap_height cannot overwrite the canonical Boundary Cap artifact. The result payload exposes cache-busted URLs plus physical and diagnostic metadata. A completed card is also best-effort auto-archived; failure to auto-save does not fail the solve.
The server captures a solve-owned settings fingerprint. Changing solve-owned settings after completion does not mutate the solved arrays, but it can make the current result stale for actions that require the current settings to match. A selected saved/loaded solved card owns its archived solve data separately.
Step 4 — Export
The browser uses the background export start/status/cancel workflow. Export operates on a selected completed solve, stages all output outside the visible completed-export namespace, then publishes one completed directory. Different format/method/detail variants of the same solved run remain separate export records in the session UI.
The export result owns its generated files, mesh report/checks, and swap instructions. The UI can open the visible Exports folder or download the selected export as a ZIP. Full geometry, 3MF/STL, cancellation, and process-kill semantics are audited in Exporting Print Files and the Output reference pages.

Model-library lifecycle
GET /api/model-libraries distinguishes:

the library loaded by this running process;
the library selected for the next launch;
whether restart is required; and
installed-but-invalid directories with their validation errors.

Install uploads to Workspace cache, extracts/copies into a hidden UUID staging directory, validates compatibility and the complete standard-library contract, then renames it to its manifest UUID. Activating a library atomically writes the next-launch selection but does not hot-swap model objects. Restart is allowed only when the selected entry is valid and different from the runtime library.
The running library and selected-next-launch library cannot be removed. The frontend asks for confirmation before removal. Library Recovery opens the manager automatically because model-dependent work is unavailable until a valid selection has restarted successfully.
Saved runs and cache actions
Saved and automatic runs can be listed, previewed, downloaded, renamed, deleted, promoted, or loaded according to their tier. Whole-run loading validates and rehydrates archived arrays into a fresh session card; settings-only loading creates a non-persisted TEMP profile and does not restore solved arrays. Active long jobs block loading and promotion.
On each newly launched Prisma process, after the Workspace lock is acquired
and before Generator server import, the launcher removes every child of
Workspace/cache except the exact real source-images directory. This makes
unsaved solves, batch artifacts, Auto Runs, LUTs, and temporary imports
session-temporary. Reconnecting to an already-running process does not run the
cleanup. User-curated saved runs, Images, Exports, settings, palettes, and model
libraries live outside that cache and are unaffected.
Clear Cache remains the stronger manual cache-administration action. It
also removes prepared source-image conversions and their manifest, plus
in-memory solved cards and palette-backend cache. It is refused while any
coordinated long job or image import is active. Prepared images rebuild on the
next explicit refresh or on-demand resolution.
Operational caveats

Use one browser session; tabs share state.
Expect one job per kind, not one job globally.
Wait for terminal acknowledgement after cancellation.
Use the launcher so paths, locking, recovery, and in-app restart work.
Treat the local console as the lifetime of the server.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: Exporting Print Files
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: export converts one completed solve card’s physical thickness maps into STL or 3MF geometry, a manifest and mesh report, and printer-capacity-specific swap instructions, then publishes the complete artifact set under Generator/Exports.

The browser workflow
The Export page is card-oriented. Select a completed solve in the left sidebar, inspect its solve preview and solved dimensions, choose the export settings, and press Generate Print Files.
The preview reports the solved image area in millimetres and solve-grid pixels. When the solve has a border, it separately reports the total physical footprint, including the border on both sides. These values come from the solved card, not the original source image dimensions.
Three settings define the ordinary export identity:

Output format: one 3MF package (default) or separate STLs;
Mesh method: field-derived white cap (default) or exact solved raster; and
Mesh detail: 2x, 4x, 8x, or 16x for a field-derived cap. Exact raster ignores this scale.

The browser always sends the selected card id. This means changing current Settings after a solve does not silently reinterpret that card; export uses the config and arrays captured for the selected solve. A card whose cached arrays disappeared after Generator restarted cannot be exported until the user loads its Saved Run archive or solves again.
Export is a polled background job. Its progress bar can request cancellation, which remains in a cancelling state until the backend reaches a safe checkpoint. The format and mesh controls remain locked while the job is active. See Export request lifecycle and artifact ownership for job identity, cancellation, private staging, and process-kill recovery.
Multiple exports of one solve
Finishing an export appends a record to the selected solve card. Generating the same solve with another format, mesh method, or field scale does not replace the earlier record. Select a record in Generated Exports to change all three subordinate views together:

Generated Files;
Swap Instructions; and
Mesh Report.

Each record shows its completion time and export duration. Open Folder opens that record’s published directory; per-file Download links and Download .zip serve the durable artifacts.
The record list itself is browser-session state. Generator does not reconstruct it by scanning Generator/Exports after a restart, although the completed folders remain plainly accessible on disk.
What a published export contains
The permanent folder is Generator/Exports/{export_id}. It contains:

either {export_id}.3mf or an stls/ directory;
export_manifest.json; and
swap_instructions.txt when a swap payload is available.

The object set always includes a flat white base, the color material volumes, and the white-cap material volume. An enabled border adds a white-cap-material frame. A difficult color or cap volume may be split into multiple same-material objects to avoid welded topology failures, so there is not necessarily exactly one mesh object per filament.
The manifest records the geometry source and detected solve mode, content and total footprint, border, coordinate frame, material/role for every object, build reports, quality summaries, validation details, and performance timings. It is the authority for interpreting the object files.
Field-derived versus exact-raster geometry
Both methods use the same exact solve-grid white base and color thickness maps. The setting changes how the white cap is created.
Field-derived white cap
The default path reconstructs the solve’s canonical white-cap field target at an integer multiple of the solve-grid resolution. field_scale controls that multiple. The color-top witness surface is nearest-neighbor lifted to the finer grid, while the hybrid cap builder creates the guard/freeform cap geometry there. Color material is never invented at the finer cap resolution.
This produces a smoother, potentially more detailed viewing surface. Increasing the scale can greatly increase work and output size; the UI asks for confirmation above 4x.
Exact solved raster
Exact raster meshes the combined white-cap thickness directly on the solve grid. It first tries one rectilinear interval body. If strict post-weld quality fails, it tries a topology-risk quarantine split and then recursive adaptive Z partitions. A forced constant-Z slab mode exists for internal/test use but is not the ordinary fallback selected by the web UI.
Color bodies follow a related policy: one interval body first, then same-material topology quarantine, then constant-Z slabs if the quarantine report is not ready. All of these preserve the physical thickness field while changing the object partition.
The detailed algorithms are in From solve to mesh the export pipeline and Robust rectilinear meshing.
Export contract and geometry ownership
Export reads the solved material plan; it does not run the color solver again. The server validates and materializes:

ordered color thickness maps;
total, boundary, and detail white-cap maps;
the canonical white-cap field target and its policy metadata;
solve-grid pitch, layer height, and white-base thickness;
physical image dimensions; and
the persisted swap-grouping plan when present.

Missing or obsolete canonical fields return HTTP 409. prepare_export_material_maps currently only shallow-copies the maps and order; the retired translucent-underfill promotion is not part of export. Mandatory product settings are normalized on the config/solve path, not retroactively applied as new geometry during export.
Solve mode is detected from required metadata. Standard and Luminance Detail are not user-selectable export modes, and current export does not infer the mode from whichever array names happen to exist.
Border geometry
If the solved card has a border, export translates all content objects inward by the configured border width and appends a __border__ frame object printed with the white-cap material. The content-domain dimensions remain the solved image area; the export footprint grows by twice the border width in X and Y. The border height participates in total print height but does not alter the solved content maps.
Mesh quality and fallbacks
Each built mesh receives a check_mesh_quality summary: watertightness, open edges, pinch/non-two-valence edges, winding consistency, and counts. Rectilinear color/cap paths also test a strictly processed, welded representation because a mesh that is clean before welding can acquire a non-manifold pinch when duplicate vertices merge.
Fallback partitioning attempts to turn a failing single body into clean same-material bodies. The manifest does not pretend success if a fallback still contains a problem: its top-level status becomes mesh_quality_failed whenever any recorded object is non-watertight or has open/pinch edges. The Export page’s Mesh Report displays those results. Export can therefore produce files with an explicit failed-quality report; publication itself is not a guarantee that every mesh passed.
validate_written_meshes optionally reloads written STL files and records that second check. It is false by default and the current browser has no control for enabling it. 3MF packaging may coalesce same-material color quarantine bodies; the package manifest explicitly records that the post-coalescence package mesh is not revalidated.
STL and 3MF ownership

STL writes one file per nonempty mesh object under stls/. Material and role mappings live in the manifest, so the slicer assignment is manual.
3MF writes one package directly from the in-memory mesh bundle without creating temporary STLs. Object transforms are baked into vertices. Package-local material slots are one-based and share a slot when base and cap use the same filament.

Those 3MF material numbers are packaging metadata. They are not the active printer’s AMS slot table and do not replace the separate swap instructions.
Swap instructions and M600
Swap geometry belongs to the solve. Export reads the persisted consecutive band plan and validates it against the printer selected at export time:

ams_slots determines total slots;
white_slots reserves the fixed white capacity; and
the remaining color slots must hold every persisted band.

Export assigns current slot tables but never regroups the solved palette or changes pause heights. A changed printer profile can therefore make an old solved plan unexecutable and produce HTTP 409. If the solve records that no valid swap plan was available, the export carries an unavailable explanation rather than inventing one. A non-banded solve receives a one-load table and is still capacity-checked.
For a banded solve, each pause is the preceding band’s stored upper Z plane. N bands require N-1 pauses. The response includes human instructions and generated M600 G-code; the published text file contains the human instructions. When everything fits in one load, there are no pause commands.
Routes

































RouteOwnershipPOST /api/export/files/startStart the browser’s background export and return its job id.GET /api/export/files/statusPoll job identity, state, progress, elapsed time, and terminal result.POST /api/export/files/cancelRequest cooperative, job-scoped cancellation.GET /api/export/files-zip?dir={export_id}Download the selected final directory’s known deliverables.GET /api/export/files/{path}?dir={export_id}Serve one contained exported file.POST /api/export/files/open-folderOpen one existing final export directory in the system file manager.
Swap instructions are generated as part of a completed export and belong to that export result and its published swap_instructions.txt; there is no separate pre-export instruction route.
See also

Export request lifecycle and artifact ownership — private staging, cancellation, and durability.
From solve to mesh the export pipeline — bundle stages and mesh construction.
AMS grouping and swap planning — how the solve chooses a persisted band plan.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: Settings, resolution, and the config contract
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: the Generator keeps a mutable session dictionary, accepts partial updates through a POST endpoint, normalizes its coupled solve-pitch fields, force-restores mandatory product safeguards, snapshots the resolved dictionary at solve start, and translates that snapshot into SolveConfig and then PipelineConfig.

This page describes the contract between the Settings UI, settings profiles, the server session, and the staged solver. For the user-facing controls, see the pages under Settings. For the solve path, see Pipeline Map and generator.facade.
The three live representations





























LayerTypeOwnerRoleFrontend configJavaScript objectapp.state.settings.config, initialized in app/core/application-context.js and synchronized by app/features/settings/profiles.jsMirrors the current Settings UI and the last server response.Session configplain Python dictsession["config"] in server.pyMutable state for the running server process.Typed solve configshared SolveSettings, wrapped by SolveConfig then PipelineConfigconfig/solve_settings.py, facade.py, pipeline/state.pyOne canonical setting inventory plus request-only and execution-only data.
POST /api/session/config has partial-update semantics: fields omitted from the request retain their current session values. The endpoint validates the submitted ConfigPayload, merges it over the existing session dictionary, normalizes resolution, applies the selected luminance preset, reapplies mandatory product settings, stores the result, and returns the complete resolved config. The frontend serializes config writes so an older request cannot arrive after a newer one and silently revert the session.
The frontend and backend use two names for the shared support filament. The visible control owns base_filament and forces cap_filament to "__same__"; every frontend sync also mirrors that selection into the older solver-facing white_base field and sends white_cap: null. _build_solve_config resolves those solver-facing fields. Settings-profile and saved-run normalization accepts either representation and reconstructs the shared-filament rule.
At POST /api/solve/start, the server copies the resolved session dictionary before starting the background worker. Later Settings changes therefore do not alter a solve already in progress. SolveConfig and PipelineConfig are ordinary mutable dataclasses, not frozen types; their isolation comes from this per-solve snapshot, facade copy, and pipeline compilation. Pipeline runtime limits are declared separately on PipelineRuntime, and swap-scout replacement creates a fresh carrier.
The production flow is:
frontend config
  → POST /api/session/config
  → merged and normalized session dict
  → snapshot at /api/solve/start
  → _build_solve_config
  → SolveSettings.__post_init__
  → facade effective-request copy
  → PipelineConfig.from_solve_settings
  → run_pipeline
  → staged_runner compatibility entry
  → staged.orchestration.run_staged_backend_path
The web app uses the staged backend. The older engine in solve.py remains a compatibility/CLI path and is not the normal web-app solver.
Printer-owned printability
Printer configuration is a separate Workspace contract at Generator/Workspace/config/printers.json; it is not owned by session["config"] or Settings Profiles. Each nozzle profile stores its diameter, layer-height and nominal-line-width data, and an integer min_line_length_multiplier from 2 through 10. It does not store a separate minimum width or physical minimum length.
The backend resolver derives and canonicalizes:
minimum extrusion width = nozzle diameter
minimum line length      = nozzle diameter × multiplier
minimum component area   = width × length
GET /api/printers/active and successful printer writes return those resolved values under printability. The frontend uses that response to refresh its display and session mirror, but the server overlays the active printer’s values again on every session update and solve-start snapshot. A stale or hand-written printability_minimum_* client value therefore cannot override the current printer.
Changing the active printer or nozzle updates the session mirror and solve-owned fingerprint. The selected nozzle diameter also remains the solve-admission floor described below. Physical printability checks retain their existing solve-grid quantization; this schema change does not introduce fractional occupied cells or alter the component grader.
Resolution schema
config/resolution_schema.py owns three canonical schema fields:

























FieldDefaultMeaningimage_sample_pitch_mm0.20Physical pitch of the source raster sampled for the solve.solver_fine_pitch_mm0.20Physical pitch of the solver grid.color_region_target_mm0.60Target physical width of initial color-planning regions.
The first two are one user-facing Solve Pitch under two internal names. They must both be present and agree within the schema tolerance. When they agree, the normalizer writes the accepted value back to both fields. color_region_target_mm is independent.
Solve-pitch constraints
The Settings UI always writes the same value to image_sample_pitch_mm and solver_fine_pitch_mm. It does not silently change the pitch when a user selects a different nozzle. Instead:

the UI displays the active nozzle diameter as the minimum;
solve preflight offers to set an undersized pitch to that exact diameter before continuing, while leaving equal and coarser pitches alone; and
_validate_solve_pitch_for_nozzle repeats the check in the backend before a job is reserved.

The correction updates both canonical pitch fields through the normal settings synchronization path and preserves the physical cap-smoothing radius while recalculating its solve-grid cell representation. Declining it changes nothing. Other settings failures remain ordinary blocking validation because they may have multiple valid corrections. The resolution schema itself only checks field presence, finite numeric values, and agreement. The nozzle constraint belongs to solve admission.
Retired aliases
The following aliases are retired:





















Retired fieldCanonical replacementpixel_size_mmimage_sample_pitch_mm and solver_fine_pitch_mmmesh_xy_pitch_mmimage_sample_pitch_mm and solver_fine_pitch_mmcolor_pixel_mmcolor_region_target_mm
A non-null retired alias raises ResolutionSchemaLegacyFieldError. An alias present with null is dropped. ConfigPayload deliberately permits extra keys long enough for _payload_model_fields to identify retired fields and return a useful HTTP 422 response; unrelated unknown extras are ignored. Egress removes all three aliases defensively.
Canonical config also excludes eight retired no-op fields: smooth_iters, allow_print_despite_hazards, detail_cap_pitch_mm, v2_cleanup_de_budget, v2_enable_cliff_closure, v2_enable_cap_topology_cleanup, v2_max_cleanup_rounds, and v2_full_cap_quality_report. Old Settings Profiles and saved-run config carriers are normalized when they enter or leave the live state model, so these names do not reappear as active settings. Unrelated metadata dictionaries are not recursively rewritten.
Where normalization runs
normalize_resolution_schema runs at the external dictionary boundaries that can persist settings:

merged session updates in POST /api/session/config;
Settings Profile creation;
Settings Profile update; and
Settings Profile file loading.

For a profile payload or direct call to the normalizer, submitting only one member of the pitch pair is a conflict. The session endpoint first merges a partial request with the current session, so an omitted member can come from existing state; the merged pair must still agree.
Both typed config dataclasses call _apply_resolution_backstop in __post_init__. This backstop does not inspect legacy dictionary keys. It defaults the pitch pair only when both are absent, rejects a missing or disagreeing member, and defaults/coerces the independent color-region target.
The two schema exceptions are translated to structured HTTP 422 responses:




















Exceptiondetail.errorAdditional fieldsResolutionSchemaLegacyFieldErrorlegacy_resolution_fieldfield, replacementsResolutionSchemaConflictErrorresolution_schema_conflictboth field names and values
Other explicitly retired config fields use retired_config_field. Some deliberately quiet-dropped historical residue is logged and discarded instead.
Mandatory product settings
_force_mandatory_product_settings is applied on session updates, profile normalization/egress, and solve construction. _build_solve_config also passes several of the same values as literals, so a stale or hand-edited profile cannot turn them off.























































SettingForced valueConsequencemodel_domain_ingressTrueSource targets use the active library’s Camera Transform path.enforce_printabilityTrueProduct printability enforcement runs.cap_continuity_cleanupTrueCap continuity cleanup remains enabled.color_region_target_from_printabilityTrueThe effective region target cannot fall below the nozzle-derived printability floor.detail_cap_enabledTrueThe detail-cap stage cannot be disabled, although detail_cap_max_layers = 0 permits no optional detail height.stage2_final_printability_gate_fine_overrideTrueThe final Stage-2 gate runs.stage2_printability_gate_fine_overrideTrueThe Stage-2 gate runs.stage2_printability_repair_fine_overrideTrueStage-2 repair runs.stage4_printability_gate_detailTrueStage-4 detail authoring is gated for printability.
The same gate rounds d_wc_min upward to a whole number of layer-height steps. The normal UI expresses it directly as Min Cap Layers.
The Camera Transform path is not trusted from an archived run or stale Settings Profile at solve time. _build_solve_config resolves the path from the active published model library owned by the launcher.
Selecting Luminance mode also expands a preset. It forces the smooth boundary-cap mode, enables the luminance handler, sets its boundary-ceiling path, enables detail residual handling, and selects the final-gate luminance authoring policy. Returning to Color mode disables the luminance handler; the frontend restores its separately remembered Color-mode boundary-cap selection.
Settings Profiles and module state
Settings Profiles persist only _SETTINGS_PROFILE_KEYS, plus a separate snapshot of module enablement. They do not persist printer profiles, the active printer/nozzle selection, resolved minimum-width or minimum-length values, the selected image, palette deck, frame/crop state, image adjustments, border/export settings, or solve history. See Settings for Basic, named, and TEMP profile behavior.
The distribution ships two revisioned named-profile records under Prisma/data/generator/settings_profiles/refinement/: refinement-balanced and refinement-strong. On the first launch after this profile revision, the server removes the retired wing-c-minimal and wing-c-standard ids, installs the current bundled records into the Workspace profile store, and records bundled_profile_revision in state.json. The revision marker makes this a one-time migration, so a user may subsequently delete either optional profile without it reappearing on every launch.
Loading a profile is a two-part frontend/backend transition:

write the profile’s config fields to the session; then
replace the persisted module-state snapshot.

If the second write fails, the frontend attempts compensation with the prior config and module snapshot. This is not one backend transaction, so ordinary error compensation is stronger than hard-process-kill convergence.
Module toggles live in the Generator Workspace at config/modules.json, not inside session["config"]. server._MODULES_PATH resolves that file through data_paths.CONFIG_DIR; the checked-in generator/app/modules.json is not the production state file. Preprocessing parameter blocks do live in config. Cache identity includes all module enablement, but includes parameter blocks only for preprocessing modules that are enabled.
Solve-owned cache identity
_solve_owned_fingerprint hashes the settings and external state that can change solved output. This includes:

the coupled pitch pair, color-region target, and cap parameters;
palette, stack geometry, solver, gamut, correction, luminance, and region-refinement settings;
the selected image plus its frame and image adjustments;
active-nozzle printability data;
module enablement and enabled preprocessing parameters;
the selected appearance provider, configured model paths, and photo-stack predictor/domain contract versions.

Presentation/export-only settings such as the border are intentionally outside the solve fingerprint. Retired resolution aliases are absent because ingress rejects or removes them.
preprocessing_params remains canonical settings state and contributes to the fingerprint only for enabled preprocessing operators. The facade consumes each enabled operator’s block when it constructs the ordered instances; the pipeline receives those instances rather than another parameter copy.
Saved runs are different from Settings Profiles: a completed card and its archive may retain the resolved millimeter thresholds as historical solve provenance. Loading that result preserves those values on the loaded card. Any new solve uses the current active printer resolver and does not copy archived thresholds into printers.json.
Selected field reference
Defaults here are the web-app defaults in _DEFAULT_CONFIG, not the fallback values of every lower-level compatibility constructor.











































































































Session/UI fieldSolver fieldDefaultMeaningbase_filamentwhite_basepackaged default whiteShared base/cap filament selected in the UI.cap_filamentwhite_cap"__same__" / nullCurrent product UI always reuses the base filament.layer_heightsame0.08 mmPrinted layer quantization step.d_wbsame0.20 mmWhite base thickness.d_wc_minsame0.16 mmMinimum cap thickness; UI represents the default as 2 layers at 0.08 mm.t_maxsame3.0 mmTotal stack-height ceiling.k_maxsame3Maximum distinct colored filaments in one recipe.de_thresholdsame0.01Nearest-sample distance above which a target is remapped as out of gamut.gamut_modesame"hull""hull" for nearest reachable color or "hue_preserving" for the hue-preserving route. Legacy "chroma" normalizes to "hue_preserving".chroma_weightsame1.0Chroma-versus-lightness weight used for recipe matching; reported dE remains unweighted.cap_modesame"appearance_bounded_smooth"Detail Aware in Color mode; "smooth_variable" is Smooth and is forced in Luminance mode.boundary_cap_de_budgetsame0.004Extra modeled dE allowed for the smoothed Detail Aware boundary candidate.detail_cap_max_layerssame5Maximum optional detail layers; zero permits none.color_region_target_mmsame0.60 mmRequested region width before the mandatory printability floor.appearance_model_providersame"photo_stack_bundle"Color Model v2; "historical_spline" selects Color Model v1.source_resample_kernelserver ingress only"lanczos"Downsampling kernel; "area" is the alternative. It is consumed while preparing the source raster before facade solve construction.
effective_max_layers() derives the available color layers from total thickness, base, minimum cap, and layer height. effective_d_wc_max() derives the remaining cap ceiling. Runtime luminance and swap-band limits can further constrain the boundary cap.
Research and compatibility residue
Normal UI sync explicitly keeps emit_pressure_diagnostics and emit_geometry_attribution off; scripts or direct API callers may enable those heavier diagnostic products. emit_blueprint_printability remains on for product solves.
Several lower-level dataclass defaults differ from the web-app defaults because those constructors also serve tests and compatibility paths. Documentation of normal Generator behavior should begin with _DEFAULT_CONFIG, the UI serializer, and _build_solve_config, then follow pipeline.runner into pipeline.staged.orchestration—not infer product behavior from a dataclass fallback or the thin pipeline.staged_runner facade in isolation.
